innovations.name: Przecieramy szlaki: diagnoza młodych dorosłych z FASD
innovations.desc: W ramach innowacji opracowano zalecenia diagnostyczne do diagnozy w kierunku FASD dla młodych dorosłych, czyli osób w wieku 18-24 lat. Diagnoza FASD - zgodnie z zaleceniami - składa się z 5 elementów: wywiadu, badania medycznego, neuropsychologicznego, neurologopedycznego oraz fizjoterapeutycznego. Specjaliści, którzy powinni wejść w skład zespołu diagnostycznego, to: lekarz, psycholog specjalizujący się w diagnozach neuropsychologicznych, neurologopeda oraz fizjoterapeuta lub diagnosta procesów integracji sensorycznej. Rozwiązanie zawiera zatem zalecenia do diagnozy FASD w tych 5 obszarach, ale traktując je jako jedną całość diagnostyczną – interdyscyplinarne badanie ukierunkowane na jeden cel (potwierdzenie lub wykluczenie FASD, a przy potwierdzeniu FASD – zidentyfikowanie rozmiarów i głębokości dysfunkcji zależnych od alkoholu, tak aby można było na podstawie diagnozy skonstruować…
innovations.target: Młodzi dorośli w wieku 18-24 lat z niezdiagnozowanym FASD.
innovations.evidence:
Uzupełnienie luki w zakresie braku procedury spajającej kilka zupełnie odrębnych metodologii diagnostycznych;
szerszy dostęp do możliwości uzyskania diagnozy FASD w przypadku młodych dorosłych.
authors: Fundacja na rzecz Dziecka i Rodziny FASCYNACJE

innovations.name: Szczypta wiedzy szefa kuchni
innovations.problem:
Ograniczona możliwość korzystania z oferty punktów gastronomicznych przez osoby z alergiami i nietolerancjami pokarmowymi;
brak prostych narzędzi dla branży gastronomicznej, które ukazywałyby w sposób czytelny konsekwencje spożycia alergenów przez osoby z alergią.
innovations.desc: Pracownicy gastronomii - z uwagi na niski poziom świadomości i wiedzy o alergiach pokarmowych - często nie zdają sobie sprawy z konsekwencji, jakie ponoszą ich klienci w wyniku źle oznaczonego menu czy zanieczyszczonych alergenem posiłków. „Szczypta wiedzy szefa kuchni” to zbiór informacji o alergenach, checklista ułatwiająca składanie zamówień, a także ścieżka postępowania w sytuacji zgłoszenia reakcji alergicznej. W ramach innowacji powstało także pięć krótkich filmów, w których występują popularni aktorzy i postaci ze świata kulinarnego. Opowiadają oni o zagrożeniach wynikających z nieprawidłowych oznaczeń alergenów i nieprawidłowej obsługi osób z alergiami w gastronomii.
innovations.target: Osoby z alergiami i nietolerancjami pokarmowymi.
innovations.benef:
Menedżerowie lokali gastronomicznych i firm cateringowych;
osoby pracujące w gastronomii (np. obsługa kelnerska).

innovations.name: Dziewczyny rządzą
innovations.problem: Kwestie stereotypowego postrzegania w społeczeństwie ról kobiet oraz częste przekonanie, że nie powinny one angażować się w politykę i że nie znają się na niej, przyczyniają się do sytuacji, w której nastolatki nie planują zajmować w przyszłości stanowisk zarządczych. Nastoletnim dziewczynom brakuje wzorców kobiet działających w obszarze zarządzania czy podejmowania istotnych decyzji. Jednocześnie w szkole brakuje przestrzeni na ćwiczenie umiejętności wystąpień publicznych czy krytycznego myślenia.
innovations.target: Gra dla młodzieży w wieku 12-18 lat, dedykowana młodym kobietom. Szczególnie pożądane jest popularyzowanie gry wśród młodzieży zamieszkującej małe miasta czy wsie.
innovations.evidence: W ramach innowacji zorganizowano 3 spotkania w 3 różnych szkołach, 4 spotkania w siedzibie fundacji, spotkanie w gronie międzynarodowym: gra 3 grup jednocześnie. W trakcie obserwacji uczestników i uczestniczek gry widoczne było ich zaangażowanie. Deklarowali, że narzędzie jest ciekawe, zachęca grupę do zabawy. Uczestnicy testowania aktywnie brali udział w wyciąganiu wniosków z rozgrywki, chętnie dzielili się swoimi obserwacjami, szczególnie istotnym rezultatem była widoczna refleksja młodzieży na temat faktycznej działalności w samorządach.

innovations.name: Bunja – kraina możliwości
innovations.problem: Innowacja odpowiada na problem niedostosowania przestrzeni publicznej do potrzeb dzieci i młodzieży, które nie są włączane w działania miastotwórcze i nie mają wpływu na otaczającą ich przestrzeń. Negatywne konsekwencje braku partycypacji dziecięcej to obniżenie poczucia sprawczości, mały związek emocjonalny z otoczeniem czy niewykształcenie się postaw obywatelskich, przejawiających się m.in. dbaniem o przestrzeń publiczną. Brak głosu dzieci w dyskusji i planowaniu funkcjonowania miasta ma także swoje odzwierciedlenie w niskim poziomie bezpieczeństwa młodych osób, a także braku czytelności przestrzeni miejskiej i jej przebodźcowaniu. Gra odpowiada na potrzebę wzmocnienia samostanowienia…
innovations.desc: Innowacja ma postać gry, w ramach której dzieci zostają podzielone na kilka plemion. Ich zadaniem jest zaplanowanie i zrealizowanie pomysłu drobnej interwencji w bliskim im otoczeniu, np. poprawienia zielonej infrastruktury, zapewnienia czystości i porządku, organizacji wydarzeń integrujących grupę. Do przeprowadzenia gry konieczne jest uzyskanie zgody właściciela miejsca (np. dyrektora szkoły czy urzędu miasta) na wprowadzenie zmian w przestrzeni. Dobrą praktyką jest również poinformowanie rodziców dzieci o tym, na czym polega działanie.
innovations.target: Dzieci i młodzież w wieku 10-15 lat, uczniowie klas 4-8 szkoły podstawowej. Istotne jest posiadanie przez uczestników gry rozwiniętych umiejętności czytania, analizy, abstrakcyjnego myślenia. Grupę biorącą udział w rozgrywce można stworzyć w każdym miejscu, w którym dzieci spędzają czas, np. w szkole, świetlicy środowiskowej, klubie młodzieży.
innovations.evidence: W kreatywnej ankiecie dla dzieci uzyskano informację, że 20 na 23 dzieci odczuło, że ma wpływ na bliskie miejsce, przed rozgrywką takiej odpowiedzi udzieliło 13 na 25 dzieci. 11 na 23 przebadanych dzieci po rozgrywce czuje się odpowiedzialne za bliskie im miejsce, przed uczestnictwem w grze takiej odpowiedzi udzieliło 4 na 25 dzieci.

innovations.name: Powitalnik
innovations.problem: Moment diagnozy niepełnosprawności narodzonego dziecka jest dla rodziców często traumatycznym doświadczeniem – powoduje poczucie dezorientacji, zagubienia, niewiedzy. Rodzice nie wiedzą co robić dalej, gdzie szukać pomocy, do kogo się zwrócić. Ponadto gdy okazuje się, że wyczekane dziecko mierzy się z poważnymi wyzwaniami zdrowotnymi, rodzice często pozostawieni są sami sobie. Brakuje wsparcia, dostępu do informacji, przestrzeni do dzielenia się trudnymi emocjami i wymiany doświadczeń.
innovations.target:
Rodzice dzieci z niepełnosprawnością;
personel medyczny na oddziałach położniczych.
innovations.evidence: W „Powitalniku” opisane zostały najważniejsze rodzaje pomocy terapeutycznej i finansowej, które przysługują rodzinom mierzącym się z diagnozą dziecka. Ponadto wskazane zostały dane kontaktowe do osób znajdujących się w podobnej sytuacji. Dzięki temu narzędziu rodzice uzyskali szybki dostęp do kompleksowego kompendium wiedzy, które wspiera ich w przetrwaniu trudnego okresu, co pozytywnie wpłynęło na ich poczucie bezpieczeństwa i komfort psychiczny.

innovations.name: Przenośne modularne łazienki
innovations.problem: Wiele domów i mieszkań, zwłaszcza położonych na obszarach wiejskich lub miejskich o niższym standardzie życia, może nie mieć dostępu do podstawowych udogodnień sanitarnych. Innowacja pomaga rozwiązać ten problem, umożliwiając szybkie dostarczenie podstawowej infrastruktury sanitarnej w miejsca, gdzie wcześniej nie było to możliwe.
innovations.desc: Innowacja oferuje dostęp do projektu przenośnych modułów łazienkowych, które są łatwe w montażu i demontażu i można je zainstalować w różnych przestrzeniach. Materiały użyte do ich produkcji są lekkie, trwałe i łatwe w transporcie. Gotowe moduły są transportowane do miejsc przeznaczenia, gdzie następuje ich instalacja.
innovations.target:
Osoby ubogie;
osoby zamieszkujące lokale nieposiadające łazienki.

innovations.name: Asystent studenta z ASD
innovations.problem:
Według badań przeprowadzonych m.in. przez rzecznika Praw Obywatelskich studenci z niepełnosprawnościami psychicznymi są praktycznie niewidoczni na uczelniach wyższych, a ich specjalne potrzeby rzadko są brane pod uwagę w działaniach na rzecz zapewnienia równego dostępu do nauki. Dzieje się tak dlatego, że studenci neuronietypowi często unikają zauważania, starając się uniknąć negatywnych reakcji otoczenia oraz stygmatyzacji. Rzadko też korzystają z usług biur ds. osób z niepełnosprawnościami, próbując radzić sobie na swoich wydziałach samodzielnie lub z pomocą swoich bliskich. W związku z tym, wielu z tych studentów zostaje bez wsparcia i często rezygnuje z kontynuowania nauki.
Opis…
innovations.desc: W ramach projektu zaoferowano studentom i studentkom z ASD poradnictwo oraz usługi asystenckie. Zakres i częstotliwość wsparcia ustalana jest indywidualnie i może dotyczyć różnych obszarów związanych ze studiowaniem, np. załatwianie spraw w dziekanacie, poruszanie się po mieście, relacje z osobami prowadzącymi zajęcia, planowanie nauki oraz czasu wolnego. Korzystanie ze wsparcia nie wymaga orzeczenia o niepełnosprawności i diagnozy spektrum zaburzeń autystycznych. Każda studentka i każdy student, którzy podejrzewają u siebie ASD, mogą wziąć udział w projekcie i otrzymać wsparcie. W ramach projektu prowadzone są również prace nad rozpowszechnieniem wiedzy o spektrum zaburzeń autystycznych.
innovations.target: Studenci oraz osoby zakwalifikowane do rozpoczęcia studiów, którzy w okresie ostatnich 5 lat korzystały (bądź korzystają aktualnie) z pomocy specjalistycznej, psychologicznej bądź też są pod opieką organizacji zrzeszającej osoby z ASD.
innovations.evidence:
W ramach testowania udało się realnie poprawić sytuację wielu studentów ze spektrum autyzmu. 79 studentów z ASD otrzymało wsparcie w komunikacji ze środowiskiem akademickim, co pomogło zrekompensować ich trudności społeczne i ograniczyć zakłócenia w procesie studiowania. U 68 nastąpił wzrost kompetencji społecznych i umiejętności radzenia sobie w życiu zawodowym. Przyczyniło się to do zwiększenia pewności siebie i poziomu samodzielności osób z ASD.
W czasie trwania projektu 42 osoby zdobyły wiedzę w zakresie lidera adwokata studenta z ASD. Powstało też 48 sieci adwokatów studentów z ASD.

innovations.name: Model Dom – skalowanie innowacji społecznej
innovations.problem: Najczęstszymi nowotworami u dzieci jest białaczka – stanowi ok. 30% zachorowań, kolejnymi są: guzy mózgu (16%), chłoniaki (13%), nowotwór układu współczulnego (7%), nowotwór nerek (7%). Według danych krajowego konsultanta w dziedzinie onkologii pediatrycznej, w Polsce co roku na raka choruje ponad 1000 dzieci (co daje 1000 rodzin rocznie dotkniętych problemem choroby onkologicznej), co stanowi około 1% ogółu zachorowań na nowotwory w społeczeństwie. Każdego roku 2000-2200 dzieci poddawane jest leczeniu przeciwnowotworowemu, a około 10 000 dzieci wymaga monitorowania stanu zdrowia. Ponad 85% małych pacjentów chorujących na białaczki zostaje wyleczona. Wyleczalność dla wszystkich nowotworów…
innovations.desc:
Innowacja opiera się na publikacjach merytorycznych, głównie poradnikach, dotyczących tematyki związanej z problemami dzieci chorych onkologicznie lub po przebytym leczeniu oraz ich rodzin. Rozesłano je w formie papierowej do wszystkich ośrodków biorących udział w projekcie jako jedno z narzędzi wsparcia rodzin. Publikacje są również dostępne w formie elektronicznej na stronie
www.wsparciezdrowiadzieci.pl
.
W ramach projektu Model Dom – skalowanie innowacji społecznej zaoferowano 30 rodzinom wsparcie w 15 ośrodkach środowiskowej opieki psychologicznej i psychoterapeutycznej (I poziom referencyjny nowego systemu ochrony zdrowia psychicznego dzieci i młodzieży)
z terenu całej Polski.
Ośrodki poprzez zatrudnienie psychologów i edukatorów zapewniały wsparcie w zgodzie z Modelem DOM dla rodzin biorących udział w projekcie. Oferowane wsparcie było zindywidualizowane i nastawione na pomoc…
innovations.target: Odbiorcami innowacji są dzieci w trakcie leczenia onkologicznego lub po przebytej chorobie onkologicznej oraz pośrednio instytucje środowiska lokalnego, tj. instytucje pomocowe, instytucje oświaty (w szczególności przedszkola, szkoły) , podmioty organizujące zajęcia dodatkowe dla dzieci itd.
innovations.benef: Ośrodki środowiskowej opieki psychologicznej i psychoterapeutycznej (I poziom referencyjny nowego systemu ochrony zdrowia psychicznego dzieci i młodzieży) oraz podobne instytucje zajmujące się wspieraniem zdrowia psychicznego.
innovations.evidence:
Rezultaty osiągnięte w wyniku wdrażania na szerszą skalę:
W ramach skalowania udało się realnie poprawić sytuację wielu rodzin dzieci w trakcie leczenia onkologicznego lub po przebytej chorobie onkologicznej oraz pośrednio zaktywizować i wyedukować instytucje środowiska lokalnego we wsparciu osób z podobnymi problemami.
Grantobiorcy – ośrodki środowiskowej opieki psychologicznej i psychoterapeutycznej (I poziom referencyjny nowego systemu ochrony zdrowia psychicznego dzieci i młodzieży) dzięki projektowi miały możliwość wprowadzenia modelu wsparcia pod nadzorem ekspertów z Fundacji Wspierania…

innovations.name: koMIX życiowy
innovations.problem: Innowacja jest odpowiedzią na wyzwania związane z trudnościami w rozumieniu i radzeniu sobie z silnymi emocjami przez podopiecznych placówek opiekuńczo-wychowawczych. Dodatkowo rozwiązuje problem braku narzędzi, które mogłyby wesprzeć opiekunów w prowadzeniu edukacji emocjonalnej młodzieży z tych placówek.
innovations.desc: Innowacja działa dzięki interaktywnej, angażującej grze planszowej, która jest dostosowana do potrzeb i wyzwań młodzieży przebywającej w placówkach opiekuńczo-wychowawczych.

innovations.evidence: To narzędzie wspiera rozwój emocjonalny młodzieży, umożliwiając jej zdobywanie nowych umiejętności i dzielenie się trudnościami w bezpiecznym otoczeniu. Gra nie tylko integruje grupę rówieśniczą, ale także buduje zaufanie między graczami. Podopieczni placówek opiekuńczo-wychowawczych…

innovations.name: Les Héritiers de la Récup'
innovations.problem:
The association addresses a dual social and environmental challenge: the overproduction of waste and intergenerational isolation. On average, every French person produces 4.6 tonnes of waste per year, whilst overconsumption and waste are depleting natural resources. Beyond raising awareness of the need for moderation, the development of a more circular economy is desirable. This is based on the reuse, repair and transformation of materials.
At the same time, a survey carried out by Petits Frères des Pauvres in 2021 indicated that 530,000 elderly people were in a state of ‘social death’ in France in 2021, whilst 52 per cent of 18–30-year-olds would like to have closer ties with their elders.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Since its foundation in 2021, Les Héritiers de la Récup has organised nearly 350 workshops, raised awareness amongst more than 3,000 people and helped prevent more than 3.5 tonnes of waste. Today, the association organises 95 workshops a year and reaches nearly 950 beneficiaries, with 75 members and a growing network of local authorities and partner organisations.
Its impact is based on two key drivers: building bridges between generations and passing on skills, whilst giving materials a new lease of life and reducing waste.

innovations.name: Alim'Mater
innovations.problem:
Nutrition during the first 1,000 days of life (from pregnancy to the child’s third birthday) is crucial for the mother’s health and the child’s development. Poor-quality nutrition during this period is associated with an increased risk of gestational diabetes, preterm birth, reduced cognitive abilities and obesity. These risks primarily affect the most vulnerable families. Indeed, social inequalities in health begin on the plate, right from pregnancy.
In France, figures show that one in three children aged between 2 and 7 is overweight, according to a survey by the League Against Obesity. According to DRESS, childhood obesity is three to four times more common in nursery schools in priority…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
In 2025, Alim’Mater reached 553 families through 119 workshops aimed at pregnant women and parents of children aged 0 to 3. The association also distributed €5,000 worth of organic food (fruit, nuts, baby food, and vouchers) to the most vulnerable families.
Alim’Mater brings together 197 healthcare professionals as members, offers 18 webinars available for replay, and has participated in four conferences. Its app, ‘9 mois à croquer’, has been downloaded 10,000 times. This work is carried out thanks to three staff members, around thirty volunteers, a board of directors and a multidisciplinary…

innovations.name: Le Réseau Éco Habitat
innovations.problem:
The energy and environmental crisis is hitting the most vulnerable households particularly hard: according to the National Observatory on Precarity, in 2022, 4.8 million households – representing 12 million people – were affected by energy poverty in France, including 350,000 very low-income owner-occupier households living in substandard accommodation. Cold in winter, hot in summer, excessive energy consumption and deteriorating health are the main consequences.
Yet it is the lowest-income households that find it hardest to access public renovation schemes, despite increased financial support.
innovations.desc:
Since 2014, Le Réseau Éco Habitat has been providing end-to-end support to owner-occupiers on very low incomes with the comprehensive energy-efficiency refurbishment of their homes.
Through its support, it removes the social, financial and technical barriers that often prevent these households from undertaking such work. Its support is based on a community-focused approach: each family receives personalised support from the initial contact right through to the end of the works, with the help of a volunteer and a team of staff.
The organisation identifies the household’s needs, helps them access public grants and additional funding, ensures the renovation project is properly managed, and oversees the works. This approach enables the most vulnerable households to take an active role in their project and carry out renovations that lead to a sustainable reduction in their energy consumption.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
Since 2014, Le Réseau Éco Habitat has supported 424 families and successfully completed 175 renovation projects in the Hauts-de-France region, achieving an average energy saving of 64.8 per cent per renovated home.
The Social Impact Bond, carried out in partnership with the National Housing Agency (Anah) and Secours Catholique between 2020 and 2024, has enabled the organisation to support 111 very low-income households, with the average energy saving rising from 49 per cent to 66 per cent over the period, thanks in particular to the involvement of 58 volunteer support workers.

innovations.name: L'Alternative Urbaine
innovations.problem:
Priority neighbourhoods under urban policy (QPVs) are characterised by a combination of precarious living conditions, distance from employment and a negative public image. The unemployment rate there exceeds 26 per cent, compared with 11.7 per cent nationally, whilst one in three residents believes that their neighbourhood is viewed unfavourably by the rest of the city, according to the National Observatory for Urban Policy. Furthermore, fewer than one in four residents of a QPV consider their neighbourhood to be ‘a very pleasant place to live’.
At the same time, over 90 per cent of the integration schemes offered to the unemployed are in the construction, maintenance or personal care…
innovations.desc:
Since 2016, L’Alternative Urbaine has been transforming walking and cultural mediation into tools for professional integration and the revitalisation of working-class neighbourhoods.
Its work is based on three complementary activities:
a programme for integration through cultural mediation: people who are distant from the labour market undertake the ‘Becoming an Urban Guide’ programme, a vocational training course in cultural mediation and public speaking, and then lead paid walking tours as part of a socio-professional integration programme run in partnership with the intermediary association ARE 33. The programme also combines individual and group support, particularly addressing barriers related to mobility, digital literacy and health;
cultural walking tours in working-class neighbourhoods: offered to the general public on a pay-what-you-can basis or commissioned by businesses,…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence:
In 2025, with three branches, L’Alternative Urbaine supported 24 urban guides who were distanced from the labour market and organised 238 walking tours in 13 priority neighbourhoods, bringing together 1,600 participants.
90 per cent of participants reported having greater self-confidence after the training, compared with 30 per cent at the start of the programme, and 93 per cent felt comfortable speaking in public, compared with 56 per cent at the outset. 60 per cent of those completing the programme went on to find a job, undertake further training or set up their own business.

innovations.name: La Jardinière
innovations.problem:
French agriculture is facing a crisis that is at once social, economic and ecological: nearly half of all farmers will retire within the next ten years, whilst 18 per cent live below the poverty line. At the same time, the dominant agricultural models are damaging the soil, water and biodiversity, and are contributing to the decline of rural areas.
Collective and cooperative farms offer a solution to these challenges by pooling means of production, responsibilities and resources, whilst promoting agroecological practices and short supply chains. They also serve as hubs for cooperation and community life, re-establishing links between agriculture and society.
innovations.desc:
Founded in 2012, La Jardinière has, since 2022, focused primarily on developing community-run agroecological farms, which it regards as a catalyst for transforming the agricultural system. It is currently building a network driven by the farms themselves, promoting mutual support, the sharing of best practice and the emergence of new projects.
Its work is based on a collaborative approach: the farms and project leaders are both beneficiaries and active participants in the network. The organisation facilitates meetings between collectives, encourages peer-to-peer exchanges and develops shared resources (a wiki, feedback on experiences, training courses and working groups) to support the creation and long-term sustainability of collective farms.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The association’s dissemination strategy is based on these replicable models, which are capable of fostering autonomous local initiatives. Inter-collective meetings, in particular, serve as a key driving force: the third edition, held in March 2026, brought together 115 participants from 22 collective farms and 19 project leaders over three days. In particular, it helped to spark plans to establish networks in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté and Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur.

innovations.problem:

According to France Assos Santé, nearly two in three people say they have already foregone or postponed treatment for financial or administrative reasons, or because of the complexity of the healthcare system. The failure to claim entitlements exacerbates this situation: nearly 30 per cent of those eligible for the supplementary solidarity health cover do not make use of it. Only about one in two people make use of the State Medical Aid.
Barriers such as a lack of awareness of entitlements, administrative red tape, language barriers, stigma and out-of-pocket costs lead to delays in care and to repeated…

La PASS de ville Marseille provided 720 in-person accompaniment services to medical appointments over the course of the year. In 2025, the organisation drew on a network of 133 partner healthcare professionals, compared with 45 when it was first established.

This comprehensive support system not only improves the health and social situation of individuals but also contributes to reducing social exclusion and to a more efficient use of existing resources in society. innovations.name: L'Économe
innovations.problem:
According to ADEME, around 10 million tonnes of food are wasted in France every year. A significant proportion of this occurs as early as the agricultural production stage. Between overproduction, sizing requirements and a shortage of labour during the harvest, a large quantity of perfectly edible fruit and vegetables is left to go to waste. It is estimated that a third of the fruit and vegetables produced never reach the consumer.
At the same time, food insecurity is on the rise. According to the Centre for Research into the Study and Observation of Living Conditions, one in six people in France do not have enough to eat. Charities are struggling to provide fresh, local produce to their…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
Since its creation, L’Économe has saved 58 tonnes of fruit and vegetables from going to waste. In 2025, the organisation diverted 12.7 tonnes of fruit and vegetables from being destroyed, of which 8.8 tonnes were redistributed to ten partner charities in the Var region and 3.6 tonnes were turned into 12,682 jars thanks to its mobile canning facility.
Its work has benefited around 13,000 people, including nearly 10,000 recipients of food aid. L’Économe has also reached 2,768 people through 77 awareness-raising events across 32 local authorities.

innovations.name: Réfugiés Bienvenue
innovations.problem:
In France, refugees (more than 689,000 in 2024) are expected to be able to secure housing and employment independently. In reality, however, the complexity of the asylum process, their distance from the labour market, support schemes that are often inadequate, and social isolation hinder this independence.
At the same time, the labour market is experiencing persistent pressures: in the third quarter of 2025, there were around 458,000 vacancies in the private sector, particularly in sectors facing labour shortages, such as construction and the hospitality and catering industries.
innovations.desc:
Since 2015, Réfugiés Bienvenue has been working in the Île-de-France region to promote the reception, inclusion and self-reliance of refugees.
The organisation runs two separate accommodation schemes:
‘citizen-hosted accommodation’, which involves refugees staying with private individuals in the Île-de-France region, supported by a network of volunteers;
the ‘Réfugiés Bienvenue’ Houses, established in 2022: shared accommodation for 3 to 4 people for 12 months, each linked to a sector facing labour shortages. Those accommodated benefit from stable housing as well as social and professional support aimed at helping them access employment and independent housing.
In addition to its accommodation schemes, the organisation offers personalised social and professional support, as well as the Créations de Liens InterCulturels (CLIC) programme, which promotes social and intercultural ties…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities
innovations.evidence:
Since 2020, more than 90 per cent of those supported by the association have secured independent accommodation, following an average support period of twelve months.
Five ‘Maisons Réfugiés Bienvenue’ centres are now open in Paris and Neuilly-sur-Marne, and nearly thirty people have been supported there. By the end of 2025, over 80 per cent of those who had completed the programme had secured a long-term employment contract (a fixed-term contract of more than one year or a permanent contract) and found independent accommodation. In 2025, the association supported 40 beneficiaries and relied on…

The CARE+ project brings innovation in four areas:

• community support a volunteer program in pilot locations focused on interpersonal connections and social inclusion,
• collaboration with employers: creating workplaces that are accommodating to employees with caregiving responsibilities,
• building local ecosystems: connecting communities, local governments, experts, and services.

innovations.name: Social Entrepreneuership for Rural Development
innovations.problem: Many rural areas face an interconnected set of challenges: demographic decline, young and qualified people leaving, limited employment opportunities, long commuting distances, declining services and fewer places for social interaction. This can create a cycle in which shrinking opportunities make rural areas less attractive, leading to further population and infrastructure decline. At the same time, digitalisation and remote work have reduced the need for many jobs to be located in cities. However, rural communities often lack the professional infrastructure, networks and social environments needed to benefit fully from this transition. Coconat addresses this gap. It creates local…
innovations.desc: Coconat's innovation is the combination of a commercially viable workation business with community infrastructure and rural development. Instead of treating employment, tourism, entrepreneurship and social inclusion as separate fields, the model connects them in one physical and social ecosystem. Coconat combines coworking, temporary living, hospitality, events and entrepreneurship support. Revenue-generating activities create the critical mass of people and resources needed to sustain a rural hub, while local residents and initiatives gain access to spaces, networks, events and new opportunities. A central method is intentional community-building: bringing together people who would otherwise rarely meet – local residents and newcomers, rural and urban professionals, craftspeople and digital workers, entrepreneurs and civil society. Local residents have also participated in developing…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Other target groups

The project has created employment and an environment in which additional businesses and initiatives can establish themselves. It provides local coworking opportunities that can reduce commuting while connecting rural residents with professional and international networks. The manor estate has also become a community space used for civic meetings, elections, village events and other local activities. Its impact extends beyond the site. Coconat…

innovations.name: Cooperative archipelago for coastal habitability
innovations.problem: Low-lying coastal territories face a convergence of accelerating threats: sea-level rise, coastal erosion, marine flooding — and a near-total absence of tools, skills and community frameworks to adapt in time. Gâvres peninsula illustrates this blind spot: physically vulnerable, socially fragile, economically seasonal, yet without the infrastructure to turn local exposure into collective capacity. Beyond Gâvres, 10,000 km² of French coastline and 500,000 homes face submersion by 2100.
innovations.desc: 3 interlocked innovation ecosystems and projects : First, a permanent convivial infrastructure — open year-round, economically self-sustaining through activity cross-subsidisation — that makes coastal adaptation a lived, everyday reality rather than an expert debate. Second, a pioneering training ecosystem: France's first sail-work maritime programme, first flood rescue course for the general public, and an incoming university degree in coastal resilience — building the professional and citizen skills territories urgently need. Third, an expanding cooperative archipelago: a Submersion Witness House exploring legal and economic frameworks for coastal heritage adaptation, and a Campus of Coastal Transitions on Bailleron island — designed as a shared infrastructure for cross-territorial learning, replication and European cooperation.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Other target groups
innovations.evidence: From Maison Glaz (historical project since 2019) to the upcoming Coastal Transition Campus on Bailleron island (2026) For participants: 150 people trained in coastal resilience in 2025, including 30 job-seekers; 15 permanent jobs maintained year-round on a seasonally fragile territory; measurable pathways from exclusion to qualified employment. For the territory: 35,000 annual visitors, 100+ events per year, €1M in locally circulated value over three years — sustaining social cohesion and economic activity on a peninsula otherwise emptied off-season. innovations.name: La Banque Solidaire de l'Équipement
innovations.problem: Drawing on the experience of its social workers, who support people undergoing social and professional integration on a daily basis, Emmaüs Défi has identified financial and material difficulties in accessing long-term housing. Indeed, whilst access to housing is a crucial step that offers hope to people in difficulty, it also raises issues regarding household furnishings, which can act as a barrier to them settling into their new home.
innovations.desc:
The Banque Solidaire de l'Équipement (BSE) has five shops in France, in Paris, Toulouse, Lyon and Lille. In these shops, beneficiaries – who have been referred by social workers from partner organisations – are welcomed by BSE staff, who assist and advise them with their purchases.
The products on offer in BSE shops are new, high-quality items at prices that are, on average, 71 per cent lower than market prices. Indeed, BSE’s aim is to enable everyone to personalise their home so they can make it their own and feel ‘at home’.
The logistics involved in handling the items – both upstream (receiving donations) and downstream (preparing orders and home deliveries) – are managed by employees on work integration programmes at Emmaüs Défi.

innovations.name: Le RECHO
innovations.problem: The refugee crisis we are currently facing is an unprecedented situation. This ordeal further fuelled fear of ‘the foreigner’, intensified the state of emergency, encouraged isolationism and the closing of borders… Yet it also strengthened the spirit of citizenship and solidarity, characterised by resistance and resilience.

Every Monday, RECHO brings together around twenty people – either recipients of food aid or referred by the project’s partner associations – in the kitchen of the Secours Populaire solidarity food shop in the 18th arrondissement to cook together recipes that are economical, easy, tasty and healthy.
O2R Re-engagement Programme
This re-engagement programme is aimed at people living in exile in France who are far from the labour market. It combines cookery workshops, social support and group activities.
Cookery workshops for children

innovations.name: La Ferme de Moyembrie
innovations.problem: A spell in prison deeply undermines a person’s confidence and will to live. Regaining one’s place within a community, breaking free from the routine of prison life, and taking responsibility for oneself once again are all challenges that must be anticipated. Discovering or rediscovering one’s life plan, and returning to the outside world and its rules of social life, are key challenges of reintegration for which prisoners nearing the end of their sentences are still far too ill-prepared.
innovations.desc:
La Ferme de Moyembrie is unique in that it takes in people who are still in custody but nearing the end of their sentences, with a view to facilitating their return to society. The residents are exclusively men. The project is structured around three key areas:
> work: market gardening and livestock farming, carried out in accordance with the principles of organic farming, with six AMAPs as clients.
> accommodation: each prisoner has their own accommodation on the farm and pays a monthly rent. They are not permitted to leave the farm’s 20-hectare grounds without being accompanied by a supervisor or a volunteer coordinator.
> Support: assistance with social and administrative issues, as well as support in finding employment and new accommodation upon completion of the programme.

Men and women
25 workers on a work integration programme, including 20 residents on external placements who are accommodated at the farm.

500 people have been supported since 2000. 150 applications for admission are received from prisoners each year, and 50 people are admitted annually.
The residents’ journey

innovations.name: Pistyles
innovations.problem: The Pistyles project was set up to address the under-use of environmentally friendly techniques in the landscaping sector and to highlight the human, social and entrepreneurial qualities of gardeners, whose profession has become increasingly technical in recent years and has lost its original purpose: caring for nature.
innovations.desc:
Pistyles’ role is that of both a gardener (someone who looks after the garden, a space of human-shaped nature) and a mediator (that is to say, someone who facilitates dialogue and rebuilds close-knit relationships).
The project is structured around three key areas:
Putting residents back at the heart of their gardens and customer relations
Putting nature and respect for it back at the heart of the professional landscaping and gardening sector
Restoring the gardener’s full role as a passionate professional and entrepreneur
innovations.target: Other target groups

As an accredited social integration enterprise, RézoSocial is committed to promoting integration through economic activity. Employees on integration programmes are hired, for a maximum period of two years, in roles as IT maintenance technicians or junior developers.

To this end, Croc la vie selects fresh, flavourful fruit and vegetables, as well as local and seasonal produce, but above all strives to offer a wide variety of dishes and flavours to develop children’s palates and curiosity.
Whilst Croc la vie initially chose organic farming to provide the best nutrition for children’s mental and physical development, the organisation also wished to make an environmental and economic commitment.

innovations.name: Plateau Urbain
innovations.problem: In 2013, Simon Laisney observed a structural vacancy in the property market. Indeed, nearly 4 million square metres of office space stood empty in the Île-de-France region, 800,000 of which had been vacant for more than five years and were therefore off the market. He then came up with the idea of prioritising the utility value of these premises over their market value, thereby saving owners unnecessary expenses (maintenance, security, insurance and taxes).
innovations.desc:
Plateau Urbain is a cooperative specialising in social housing and transitional and temporary urban planning, offering affordable workspaces and, where possible, emergency accommodation solutions in vibrant, creative and community-focused third places with a social purpose, in the Île-de-France region and in several major cities (Lyon, Bordeaux, Marseille). Whether you are a local authority, a developer, a landlord or a community group, we support you in designing your transitional and temporary urban planning projects, and ensure the successful implementation of your third-place initiatives.
Setting up and managing third places We manage and oversee fixed-term third-place projects from start to finish: leasing, bringing the premises up…

a solidarity grocery shop accessible on the basis of social criteria, where students can stock up on food, cleaning products or school supplies at reduced prices (between 10 and 30 per cent below standard prices). The idea of proposing an alternative way of consuming – to boost people’s ability to cope with precarious circumstances, enhance their self-esteem and promote individual and collective agency – was born.

innovations.name: CAIRE13
innovations.problem: In France, the self-employed and entrepreneurs (retailers, craftspeople, micro-entrepreneurs, independent professionals, etc.) account for 99 per cent of businesses and 52 per cent of salaried jobs; yet there is no comprehensive support scheme to assist them when they are faced with illness, particularly cancer. innovations.desc:
To support the self-employed, CAIRE 13 works in collaboration with a range of local partners, including cancer care centres (the Centre for the Fight against Cancer, hospitals, radiotherapy centres) as well as private healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, etc.) who refer their patients to the association.

innovations.name: RoseUp
innovations.problem:
Every year, around 174,000 cases of cancer are diagnosed in women, but medical advances are leading to many remissions or cures. Indeed, according to the Fondation Contre le Cancer, nearly 70 per cent of patients are still alive five years after their diagnosis (all types of cancer combined).
However, according to a study by the National Cancer Institute (INCA), three in five people report continuing to experience the after-effects of the disease two years after diagnosis, whilst 8.5 per cent feel they are subject to discrimination. Furthermore, the growth in outpatient treatments and therapies administered outside hospital settings is heightening the sense of isolation, the need for…
innovations.desc:
The association's mission is to enable women facing cancer to continue living their lives as women, mothers and professionals both during and after treatment, and also to help them feel less alone in the face of the illness by enabling them to be part of a community, in particular by providing them with information and psychological support throughout the various stages of their illness.
To achieve its objectives, RoseUp has developed several initiatives, including:
Rose Magazine: A women’s magazine with a print run of 180,000 copies, combining in-depth features with lighter topics. It is distributed free of charge in cancer centres and departments and is available online.
Maison RoseUp: This centre aims to break the cycle of isolation, combat recurrence and empower women with cancer to take control of their own journey. Bringing together local organisations (charities, healthcare…
innovations.target: Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence:
With over 6,800 users, the RoseApp has established itself as the go-to tool for carers, extending our mission beyond the walls of our Maisons RoseUp.
On the advocacy front, 2025 was marked by significant victories. Our campaign on behalf of ‘single mums’ and our work to reduce out-of-pocket costs for patients resonated strongly with the public authorities, reinforcing our role as a key player in the healthcare system.

There is a high level of vulnerability amongst this section of the population, who are often isolated and whose homes are falling into disrepair due to a lack of maintenance. Nearly 6 per cent of homes occupied by people aged 65 and over are thus identified as ‘potentially unfit for habitation’, amounting to 3,500 homes across the entire department.
Furthermore, whilst new-build construction continues to rise, the department has…
innovations.desc:
Since 2013, the association has been creating shared living spaces designed in collaboration with local residents – spaces that foster connections and independence – so that housing can support a happy and independent old age in rural areas! Since 2018, it has also been running discussion workshops to enable everyone to reflect on and choose their living arrangements for today and tomorrow. Supporting and guiding pensioners as they consider their housing choices seems essential.
Supporting the decision-making process:
Through its commitment to enabling everyone to consider and choose their current and future housing, the association develops initiatives to support older people as they consider their housing options.
Furthermore, it now supports local councillors in developing housing for older people within their local areas.

Through its ‘E-Fabrik’ challenges, Traces brings together, at a local level, organisations working with people with disabilities and young people, and innovative digital creativity hubs such as fablabs. It provides spaces for collaboration between young people who are distant from the labour market and people with disabilities, enabling them to devise and create, together, practical solutions relating to disability, whilst acquiring the skills needed to master new digital tools.
Once recruited, the young E-Fabrik’ apprentices meet the E-Fabrik’ mentors – experts in education, disability, digital creation and design – during discussion and training sessions. At the same time, the young apprentices begin working with their E-Fabrik’ partner, a person with a disability who has chosen to get involved in the project. Together, they identify and describe a problem that the partner experiences…

innovations.problem: Guided by the values of cooperation, transparency and realistic idealism, the association Le Paysan Urbain is dedicated to the development of environmentally friendly, socially responsible urban agriculture and healthy eating.
innovations.desc:
The association focuses its work on two areas: raising public awareness of the challenges facing sustainable agriculture and high-quality food, and establishing urban agroecological farms that are economically viable, socially responsible and firmly rooted in their local communities.
In light of the observed deterioration in social ties in urban areas, the disconnect between city-dwellers and the environment, and the growing desire for access to high-quality local food, the association runs workshops in its educational garden to help and encourage city-dwellers to rediscover a connection with the land, and to raise awareness amongst young and old alike of environmental issues – such as the use of chemicals in conventional agriculture, significant food waste, the considerable distances food is transported over, and pollution caused by production and consumption patterns – as well as…

innovations.name: Utopia 56
innovations.problem: The story of Utopia 56 begins in the Calais jungle. Whilst on a voluntary mission, Gaëdig, Yann and Liza noticed a lack of coordination on the ground. They therefore decided to put their organisational skills to good use to supervise the volunteers and act as a link between the various charities. They thus founded Utopia 56 in January 2016.
innovations.desc:

Indeed, more than two in three asylum seekers are refused the status of unaccompanied minor by the state authorities, a status which guarantees long-term support for these individuals who are particularly vulnerable to insecurity and financial and social hardship. In response to this situation, Utopia 56, in partnership with Médecins Sans Frontières, has set up a network of accommodation centres to support these young migrants with their administrative, health and social procedures.
Originally, Utopia 56 focused its activities on organising and coordinating outreach patrols designed to help and support refugees. It was through experience on the ground that the association gradually refined its work and came to…

innovations.name: Biocycle
innovations.problem:
1/3 of the food produced worldwide is wasted
20 per cent of French people are food insecure
10 million metric tonnes of food are thrown away every year in France
25 per cent of food waste can be prevented through simple actions
innovations.desc:
Biocycle has set up a system for collecting unsold food. As well as tackling food waste and food insecurity, Biocycle is committed to an environmentally friendly approach by using bicycle deliveries. The association is also committed to a social mission, as its two delivery riders are employed as part of a work-based reintegration programme.
Their work involves innovative tools, such as the ‘cargo bike’ used by the delivery riders to transport food, or the ‘VéloMixeurs’ – created from scrap bicycles – which allow food to be blended using leg power, enabling them to offer delicious fruit and vegetable juices. innovations.problem: The association was founded in response to the observation that the production of renewable energy is controlled by companies that are often out of touch with the realities and needs of local communities. Énergie Partagée was therefore set up to support and finance the development of renewable energy generation sites harnessing solar, wind and hydro power, or energy from waste treatment. Its aim is to develop community-led renewable energy projects by involving all local stakeholders – citizens, local authorities, farmers and SMEs – from the design stage right through to the operation of the facilities.
The association thus offers support to residents’ groups, local authorities and farmers: it contributes its knowledge and expertise in collective organisation, legal and economic structuring, and support for local savings schemes, amongst other areas. It also trains intermediary organisations such as local energy agencies and runs national communication campaigns, such as the ‘Juin citoyen’ initiative, a major national event focusing on community-led energy.

The association also aims to raise awareness amongst the general public and elected representatives of mobility issues, as well as the technological advances that can help overcome them.
ANTS is developing genuine expertise in neuro-rehabilitation therapies, spanning both scientific research and medical practice: two founding members are part of the neurological rehabilitation team at the physics laboratory of the École Normale Supérieure (ENS) in Lyon, whilst another founding member holds a PhD in neuroscience and practises at the functional rehabilitation centre…

innovations.name: Permis de construire
innovations.problem: In France, nearly 80 per cent of prison releases are so-called ‘unassisted releases’, meaning that no support has been offered to the prisoner in terms of integration into the labour market or healthcare.
innovations.desc:
The association promotes a genuine social reintegration programme based on empowering each individual and on giving every prisoner the freedom to choose and invest in their own personal projects. To this end, the support offered by Permis de Construire is structured around the ‘Building Ourselves, Together’ programme, centred on four fundamental pillars: physical wellbeing, mental wellbeing, living well and doing well.
This personalised support focuses on the health and psychological challenges faced by prisoners, whilst highlighting the talents of each participant. It includes weekly one-to-one sessions, group socio-educational activities and training programmes that provide a structured framework for supporting individuals.
The ‘Permis de construire’ programme enables work to begin well in advance of release from prison, which is essential for defining a career plan. It thus…
innovations.target: Other target groups

Permis de construire also estimates that, following the support provided, the three-year reoffending rate amongst these beneficiaries is less than 10 per cent.

innovations.name: Coopcoloc
innovations.problem: A student on a moderate or modest income who wishes to move to a major university town faces a major problem these days: the very high cost of rent. As CROUS student accommodation is already at full capacity, many young people give up on the idea of moving out of their parents’ home or are forced to live in substandard accommodation.
innovations.desc:
Coopcoloc therefore runs a solidarity-based rental agency scheme: the association rents large flats – which its four partner social housing providers struggle to let due to their size – and houses several students in shared accommodation, at a rent approximately 20 per cent below the traditional rental market rate.
The Coopcoloc project was conceived as a means of empowering students: moving out of their parents’ home is the first step for students towards building a life for themselves. Having accommodation close to where they study also helps to reduce journey times and the associated inconveniences. Finally, by enabling these students to save an average of €100 per month, CoopColoc makes it easier for them to access better-quality food and leisure activities.
Beyond property management, the association organises activities designed to foster a sense of community amongst students and…

innovations.benef: l'Association de Coopération pour le Logement des Etudiant·es de France (ACLEF)

More than a thousand applications were submitted via the website in 2018.

The association works closely with a wide range of organisations across the area. At an operational level, the association liaises with around 700 to 800 organisations, including sports, cultural and leisure centres. These are essential to DAHLIR’s work as they enable the association to cater for its diverse range of participants. The association also has numerous referral partners, such as clinics, hospitals and local…

innovations.name: Les Concerts de Poche
innovations.problem: In France, isolation within different regions is a particularly pressing issue in rural areas. The situation faced by farmers is a good illustration of this reality. In 2020, according to an Ipsos survey, 45 per cent of farmers ‘feel more isolated than ever’.
innovations.desc:
The association’s aim is to forge connections and bring people together through classical music, opera and jazz. The idea is to reach out to an audience that is, for various reasons – such as limited mobility, lack of financial means, disability, age or a lack of familiarity with the sector – very distant from the world of music. Les Concerts de Poche manage to bring together a diverse audience, even going so far as to put local residents on stage alongside renowned concert performers.
Beyond organising concerts and workshops, the association helps to revitalise villages and has become one of the cornerstones of local cultural policy. It breaks down barriers between residents and helps to foster a sense of community within a local authority and with neighbouring villages.

innovations.name: Recyclerie Sportive

Of all the social and environmental issues surrounding sport, three major ones have been identified: - sports waste - ‘fast sport’ and energy-intensive modes of transport - access to sport for all.

innovations.problem:
The Caracol association was founded on the realisation that the majority of refugees leave accommodation centres without any housing arrangements, which acts as a real barrier to their social and professional integration. Furthermore, many people – both local residents and refugees – are looking for a place to live that fosters intercultural exchange, enables them to pursue their aspirations, and supports an eco-friendly and community-minded way of life.
On the other hand, property vacancy is a major issue in large cities and can sometimes prove costly for property owners.
innovations.desc:
The Caracol association offers solidarity-based, multicultural shared accommodation accessible to people on low incomes. These shared arrangements bring together refugees and long-term residents of France for an average period of 1 to 3 years in vacant properties, in partnership with the owners. Caracol undertakes to renovate and maintain the properties in exchange for the owners making them available free of charge. For their part, in addition to saving on caretaker costs, landlords are able to make their properties available to a project that is meaningful and beneficial to the local community.
The association manages the running of these shared accommodation schemes by organising communal activities and involving the residents in the Caracol project.

innovations.name: Latitudes
innovations.problem:
Digital technology is part of everyday life for almost all French people: 98 per cent of those aged 12 and over own a mobile phone, one in two people now use AI, and we spend several hours a day in front of our screens.

innovations.name: Terre de Liens
innovations.problem: By 2030, 40 per cent of farmers will have retired, representing a quarter of France’s agricultural land. This structural change carries the risk of accelerating trends towards farm consolidation, speculation and the expansion of intensive farming. Indeed, in 2021, 44 per cent of French people felt they did not have the opportunity to take part in activities with people from different backgrounds (2021 Fraternity Barometer), and 7 million people were experiencing social isolation (Fondation de France).
innovations.desc:
Since 2014, the Kif Kif Vivre Ensemble association has been organising a new kind of get-together for local residents: surprise meet-ups that bring together people from diverse backgrounds in a ‘blind’ setting for activities organised by one of the participants (local residents or community organisations). Participants take turns as hosts and guests and are connected via the association’s online platform, kifkif.org.
These surprise meet-ups and activities primarily involve people from priority neighbourhoods under urban policy (QPVs) in the Île-de-France region and bring together people of all ages (between 18 and 87).
Beyond the Kif Kif Vivre Ensemble digital platform, the association relies on its outreach work on the ground and its strong local roots to ensure its visibility and long-term sustainability. This strong local presence enables Kif Kif Vivre Ensemble to forge partnerships…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: 93 per cent of surprise meet-ups take place in public places. Those taking part (Kiffeuses and Kiffeurs) are aged between 18 and 85, come from over 60 different nationalities, and live in 114 different cities.

innovations.name: Traces de Vies
innovations.problem: Drawing on her own personal experience, the founder of Traces de Vies has observed that people who are vulnerable and isolated as a result of illness sometimes need to reflect on their life journey and share their story with those around them. Hospital-based biography is therefore a way of meeting this need to be listened to and heard, whilst enabling those receiving support to feel valued and not merely seen as objects of care. This process encourages people to speak freely, whilst also helping to combat the isolation of those receiving support and improve their mental health and self-esteem.
innovations.desc:
The hospital biography service offered by Trace de Vies is aimed at children and adults who are seriously ill or at the end of their lives, and who find themselves isolated due to care protocols or have little contact with their loved ones. They are identified by the care teams looking after them (hospital departments, care homes, home care workers) and who then contact the association’s biographers, whose role is to listen to and faithfully transcribe the words of the people they support. Trace de Vies offers this service to patients and their families, making it accessible to all. The association also prints 10 books and sends them to recipients chosen by the beneficiaries.
The association has developed a training programme to professionalise new hospital biographers, thereby enabling them to support as many people as possible.
Recognition of the profession of hospital biographer is a…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: + 360 people supported as at 31 January 2026 + 3,600 people who have benefited from support since 2013

innovations.name: Re-Belle
innovations.problem:
In France, food loss and waste amount to 10 million tonnes of produce per year (Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, 2022). More specifically, 45 per cent of fruit and vegetables from local producers do not end up on our plates (ADEME, 2016).
Furthermore, the department of Seine-Saint-Denis is the poorest in the Île-de-France region, with a poverty rate of 28.4 per cent and 11 per cent of the population receiving the RSA (INSEE, 2020).
In light of these two findings, the Re-Belle association was established as a Atelier Chantier d’Insertion (Social Integration Workshop) and has developed two strands of activity:
The production of jams;
The organisation of…
innovations.desc:
As a social integration workshop, Re-Belle offers personalised social and professional support based on the method of vocational and personal development activation, enabling the employees it supports to take back control of their career paths. Throughout their time with the organisation, employees are trained in various roles: anti-waste production officer, collection and delivery driver, and administrative assistant.
Re-Belle’s main activity is the production of jams. Every week, unsold fruit and vegetables from supermarkets, restaurants, hotels and partner farmers in the Île-de-France region arrive at Re-Belle’s kitchens in Stains. The food collected is sorted, washed, chopped and processed in the organisation’s workshop.
At the same time, Re-Belle runs workshops to raise awareness of healthy and sustainable eating amongst residents of priority neighbourhoods in Seine-Saint-Denis and…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: 30 tonnes of fruit and vegetables are repurposed by Re-Belle every year.

innovations.name: Locaux-Moteurs
innovations.problem: The Locaux-Moteurs association has chosen to focus its work on the under-utilisation of housing policies relating to energy-efficiency refurbishment and housing adaptations (support for those with reduced independence). Combating energy poverty lies at the intersection of the quest for a better quality of life, the reduction of social inequalities and the fight against global warming. 20 per cent of French people say they suffered from the cold for at least 24 hours during the winter of 2021–2022. Today, the ‘lower middle classes’ are bearing the brunt of energy costs, and energy-efficient refurbishment goes beyond the mere notion of quality of life. 11.9 per cent of households are in…
innovations.desc: The Locaux-Moteurs association has opted to use the ‘outreach’ approach, with door-to-door visits organised by local residents acting as liaisons from the rural areas where the scheme operates; households’ needs are then channelled to housing providers. To inform and support households, Locaux-Moteurs volunteers are recruited to help them access housing improvement support schemes. The strength of Locaux-Moteurs and the effectiveness of their visits lie in their role as peers.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Nearly 4,200 owner-occupiers (between 2017 and 2024) received an initial information pack accompanied by explanations. Between 7 and 8 out of 10 doors are opened when the Locaux-Moteurs teams visit. Nearly 400 tenants were contacted (between 2017 and 2023) Nearly 1,000 application forms submitted 20 to 25 per cent of households are taking part in the scheme Over 1,200,000 euros’ worth of works (projects completed since 2020)

innovations.name: PaQ'la Lune
innovations.problem: In working-class neighborhoods, access to cultural activities and the arts remains difficult. Although there are community centers, social services, and incubators for new initiatives, residents of neighborhoods designated as “priority neighborhoods” under urban policy (QPV) rarely feel comfortable approaching these institutions to ask for support.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion

innovations.name: Sira
innovations.problem:
Accessing training or employment may require temporary or long-term relocation, sometimes involving two successive places of residence. Many people may abandon their plans when faced with the difficulty of finding and affording a new rental property. Furthermore, there is growing pressure on urban areas, with a sharp rise in prices that makes it more difficult for the most vulnerable to access housing, and a rise in the number of unscrupulous landlords.
At the same time, in suburban areas, the stock of rental accommodation suited to people on the move (small flats, furnished or unfurnished) is rather limited. Finally, a further challenge is the near-total digitisation of many administrative…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Over 3,000 contacts per year
Over 4,000 referring partners and landlords
Over 3,000 housing solutions listed across mainland France
Over 1,600 people follow us on social media

innovations.name: Lève les yeux !
innovations.problem:
Over the past decade or so, screen addiction has become a key issue for virtually every society around the world, and all the more so in France, where daily screen time has literally skyrocketed with the advent of smartphones and tablets.
The ASNAV estimated the average screen time for adults in France at 10 hours a day in 2019 (compared with 5 hours 40 minutes in 2012), and we know that usage has increased further during the lockdowns linked to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Children and teenagers are the most vulnerable: imitating their elders, engrossed in social media which has become an essential space for socialising, addicted to video games designed for this purpose, and watching…
innovations.desc:
Lève les Yeux ! has developed around two main areas of awareness-raising work, which reinforce one another: grassroots activities (at local level) and advocacy work (at national level). The organisation also stands out for its educational approach, notably a board game designed to raise awareness called ‘Planète déconnexion’.
Community-based activities mainly involve running community education workshops for children and teenagers in schools and community centres, as well as for parents and teaching staff. Lève les Yeux ! also trains professionals working with children. ‘Disconnection Challenges’ are launched at neighbourhood or school level. Finally, the association runs workshops and talks in companies on the theme of ‘Mindfulness and wellbeing at work in the digital age’.
The association’s second area of focus encompasses advocacy work, notably the coordination of the Collectif…
innovations.target: Other target groups

innovations.name: Énergie Solidaire
innovations.problem:
In France, 12 million people are experiencing energy poverty in their homes – one in five people – according to the National Observatory on Energy Poverty.
Although public funding for energy-efficiency renovations is available, the application processes are lengthy and complex, and the ‘out-of-pocket costs’ for the work are often too high for households to afford, given that their financial situation is already untenable. Whilst there are specialist organisations attempting to tackle this social and environmental emergency, they lack the resources to cope with growing demand and the ageing of housing and infrastructure, against a backdrop of inflation.
innovations.desc:
Énergie Solidaire brings together local communities and strengthens the capacity of associations to reduce the number of households experiencing energy poverty.
The Fund is aimed at all individuals and businesses involved in the energy transition (producers, suppliers, consumers, local authorities, etc.) to enable them to contribute to the fight against energy poverty in their local area and to increase their commitment.
Énergie Solidaire implements innovative fundraising solutions. These include financial donations as well as micro-donations based on energy consumption, sourced from various stakeholders: private companies, foundations, members of the public, local authorities, and so on. The Fund then redistributes these donations via annual calls for proposals organised for locally-based public-interest organisations committed to tackling energy poverty and supporting low- and very…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: In the five years since it was founded, Énergie Solidaire has supported 27 projects, thanks to the growing involvement of people committed to the energy transition

innovations.name: Ikambere
innovations.problem:
Ikambere aims to contribute to health equity, a concept which means that everyone has equal access to the opportunities to live a healthy life, regardless of their social, economic or demographic circumstances. To achieve equity, it is essential to address the social determinants of health, such as income, housing and food insecurity, and to ‘reach out’ to those populations furthest removed from the healthcare system and information.
In France, cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death among women, claiming the lives of 200 women every day. Those most affected are women living in precarious circumstances. Furthermore, 54 per cent of women living in priority neighbourhoods (QPVs)…
innovations.desc:
Ikambere’s activities are divided into three main areas of work. All the services offered by the organisation are provided free of charge to beneficiaries.
Support towards self-reliance: each woman receiving support benefits from individual support (social, health and employment integration) and can take part in group activities organised according to a fixed weekly schedule. The approach is structured around four main areas: social support and responses to urgent needs, physical health, mental health, and social and professional integration.
‘ Outreach and health mediation: community-based mediation in hospitals for female patients living with HIV (individual support, support groups, information workshops), screening and awareness-raising initiatives on sexual health and rights in migrant accommodation centres and in public spaces, and monthly workshops in community centres on topics…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Ikambere manages 3 houses helping 850 women per year.

innovations.name: Règles élémentaires
innovations.problem:
As periods have a daily impact on the lives of half the population, they are a matter of public concern. In France, 4,000,000 people experience period poverty, and one in two French people believe that periods are a taboo subject, according to the Period Poverty Survey published by Règles élémentaires and OpinionWay. This taboo remains very real and has negative consequences in many areas. Indeed, period poverty can have an impact on social inequalities, starting at school and continuing into the world of work. It is estimated that one in three adults has missed work, and that nearly one in two young people has missed school because of their periods.
The taboo surrounding periods has…
innovations.desc:
Règles Élémentaires is France’s leading association working to tackle period poverty and the taboo surrounding periods. Its mission is to enable everyone affected to manage their periods in good conditions, so that they no longer act as a barrier to their daily lives. It aims to put an end to period poverty, to make period education and awareness-raising more widespread, and to improve the quality of life for people who have periods, by taking action at various levels.
The organisation operates in three areas:
collection and redistribution: facilitating the collection of sanitary products via an online platform, then redistributing these products to its 1,000 partner organisations across France;
awareness-raising and training: workshops, events and outreach sessions (in schools, sports clubs, businesses and medical and social care organisations). The organisation also trains medical and…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: 1 million people directly affected by our work 29 million sanitary products distributed 470,000 people benefiting through our partners Over 1,800 partner organisations across the country Over 700 media reports on our work 20,000 young people educated about periods 4,000 professionals educated

innovations.name: L'Alterfixe
innovations.problem:
In ten years, France has lost 100,000 farms, and by 2030, half of all farmers will have retired. More than two in three farms have no guaranteed succession plan. The average size of farms has increased by 25 per cent over the last ten years, rising from 55 hectares in 2010 to 69 hectares in 2020.
At the same time, there is a trend of people from non-farming backgrounds returning to the land. These individuals, who are often changing careers, face two major challenges when setting up: finding partners for their farm and finding a farm on which to settle.
innovations.target: Other target groups

innovations.name: Territoire Zéro logement passoire
innovations.problem:
In France, 62 per cent of households experiencing energy poverty are tenants. There are 3 million low-income tenants who struggle to pay their energy bills and suffer from discomfort in their homes. They have no say in the renovation of their homes, and current state support is focused mainly on homeowners, thereby leaving tenants in energy-inefficient homes behind.
They are therefore affected by landlords’ ‘renovation procrastination’ – the tendency to put off renovation work due to regulatory uncertainty and the lack of guaranteed returns on such work. The cost of this delay is borne by tenants in the form of high energy bills that could have been avoided. Whilst 50 per cent of the rental…
innovations.desc:
Territoire Zéro Logement Passoire (TeZeLoPa) has a twofold aim: to empower tenants to initiate renovations and to develop tools for eco-friendly planning and support provided by local authorities.
Data analysts, cartographers, thermal engineers, community organisers, lawyers, local councillors and local authority departments are thus working together in a pioneering initiative to make the goal of a ‘Zero Substandard Housing Area’ tangible and achievable, and, first and foremost, to eradicate substandard housing from the private rental sector.  The method combines the mapping of substandard housing, the collective organisation of tenants, the provision of expert advice, engagement with landlords, and support and assistance schemes for the tenants concerned.
The project is part of a highly local and experimental approach, designed to enable rapid positive outcomes and to create a space…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: This innovative project has proven its concept and has now completed its first two pilot schemes in partnership with the cities of Grenoble and Lyon. Following the presentation of the pilot scheme, a similar project has been underway in Charleroi, Belgium, since April 2024.

innovations.name: Territoire des possibles
innovations.problem:
According to INSEE, by 2030 people aged over 65 will account for a quarter of the French population. This highlights the need to plan for this ageing population in all its dimensions, taking into account the various challenges associated with ageing: economic, social, health-related, and so on.
85 per cent of people hope, if they are forced to leave their home, to have access to accommodation that is as similar as possible to their original home. At present, institutional approaches do not meet these needs, and alternative housing options are limited, particularly in rural areas.
innovations.desc:
To address these challenges, Territoires des possibles has set itself the mission of broadening the range of possibilities for retired people living in rural areas, so that they can freely choose where to live, through discussion and awareness-raising workshops, and by working with them to design shared and accessible housing.
In 2022, it opened its first shared and inclusive housing scheme, an innovative shared-living solution designed to meet the needs of many retired people. Designed to enable people living in rural areas on modest incomes to continue their retirement in a home that meets their need for social connection, their health requirements and their financial means, these small-scale shared homes ensure a balance between independence, freedom, the need for social interaction and security.
They are co-developed with residents and local authorities, with the involvement of…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The first shared housing scheme, located in Lestiac-sur-Garonne in southern Gironde and conceived during a participatory feasibility study in 2017–2018, now comprises eight independent private studio flats and 220 m² of shared spaces. All the homes are designated as social housing. The participatory approach lies at the heart of the project: a total of 43 workshops have been organised since 2017, bringing together 200 participants.

innovations.name: Happiness Lessons Integrated Programmes – A Whole-School Well-being Programme with Scalable Impact on Mental Health Promotion
innovations.problem:
Educational institutions play a central role not only in academic development but also in children’s and young people’s emotional, social and psychological well-being. However, many educators and institutions lack a coherent, age-appropriate and practically applicable framework for promoting mental health and well-being as part of everyday education. Support is often limited to isolated activities, short-term interventions or the involvement of external professionals after difficulties have already emerged.
Children and young people need regular opportunities to learn how to recognise and regulate emotions, manage stress, develop self-confidence, use their personal strengths, build…
innovations.desc:
Happiness Lessons Integrated Programmes translates research-based well-being promotion into an educational model that trained educators can implement within the day-to-day life of kindergartens and schools. Its innovation lies in moving beyond isolated interventions and combining structured curricula, educator capacity-building, age-specific experiential learning, institutional commitment, family engagement, professional networking and continuous development within one scalable framework.
Rather than functioning as a conventional school subject, the programme creates experiential learning situations in which children and young people practise evidence-informed behaviours and mental strategies through discussion, play, movement, music, creative activities, reflection and shared experiences.
The integrated model comprises seven complementary programme pathways covering more than 50…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
