innovations.name: More appreciation of nature and food - Educational programmes for schools and kindergartens
innovations.problem: As natural spaces become increasingly rare in everyday life and food production becomes more industrialised, many young people are losing the opportunity to experience where their food comes from. The social consequences of this are significant: around 30% of food produced is wasted. The lack of engagement with food also leads to unhealthy eating habits. In Germany, more than 20% of children are overweight, putting them at high risk of subsequent diseases.
innovations.desc: To address this, our vision is to promote a deep appreciation of nature and food, encourage healthy eating habits, and reduce the growing disconnect between society and the natural world. Central to this vision is our belief that every child has the right to a natural learning environment. To make this a reality, we develop educational programmes that enable participants to explore, understand, and value the process of growing food. At the heart of our work are the educational programmes GemüseAckerdemie and AckerRacker, tailored for schools and kindergartens as a train the trainer approach. These programmes equip teachers and educators with the necessary tools, resources, and support to implement nature and nutrition education. Through growing their own vegetables, children gain valuable hands-on experience and develop a deeper understanding of sustainability, nutrition, and…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: At Acker, we have been impact-oriented since our beginnings. This means that the ultimate goal of our educational programmes is to bring about sustainable and holistic change - in the participants of our programmes and in our society. Our impact analysis proves it: Participants in our educational programmes acquire a basic understanding of food production and agricultural interrelationships and develop conscious and sustainable consumer behavior. Participating children acquire new knowledge about food, eat more healthily and spend more time outdoors. To name some examples we can say that in…

innovations.name: From dreams to impact with Start-Up de Territoire
innovations.problem: Many French territories face pressing social and environmental challenges — social isolation, lack of local services, ecological transition — yet struggle to mobilise citizens and local actors around collective solutions. At the same time, research shows that 94% of French citizens want to contribute to solving societal issues, but only 20% have done so concretely (Ticket for Change & Occurrence, 2016). This gap between civic willingness and actual engagement reflects a lack of accessible, structured frameworks for collective action at the local level. Additionally, locally-rooted entrepreneurial projects often lack the community support, visibility, and accompaniment needed to emerge and…
innovations.desc: Start-Up de Territoire introduces a pioneering model of citizen-led territorial innovation combining community organising, collective intelligence, and social entrepreneurship support. The approach is innovative in several ways: 1. A structured 4-step territorial methodology: Step 0: Building a core team and shared vision Step 1: Collecting dreams, ideas, and needs from inhabitants and local actors Step 2: Co-designing solutions during large-scale open creativity events (from 30 to 1,492 participants) Step 3: Selecting projects and forming collective teams Step 4: Accompanying project development within the local ecosystem 2. Joyful collective intelligence : The approach deliberately combines rigour and celebration, making participation accessible and attractive to a wide diversity of citizens. 3. A replicable model with local adaptation: Each territory adapts the methodology to its…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Start-Up de Territoire operates through a network model designed for replication, adaptation, and scaling: - Replicated: The core 4-step methodology has been transferred to 29 independent local teams across France and Luxembourg, maintaining its fundamental approach. - Adapted: Each territory customises the model to its specific context (urban, rural, overseas...) - Scaled-up: From 6 pilot territories in 2018 to 29 territories today, with 3 successive cohorts trained and a 4th launching in autumn 2026.
Quantitative results: 20,750 citizens mobilised to share their dreams and ideas 638…

innovations.name: Network of Future Places
innovations.problem: Rural regions across Germany—especially in the former East—are living through a compounding crisis that is both material and social: demographic shrinkage, physical decay, the thinning of civic life, and political radicalization feed each other. They accumulate into a pervasive sense among rural and small town residents of being left behind by the mainstream economy, by infrastructure decisions, and by national attention. The most concrete symptom is the quiet disappearance of shared or “third” places. A former school that no longer has children, a village pub that cannot survive without regulars, a church or farm building that sits locked and unheated—these are not just “properties.” They…
innovations.desc: Founded in 2018, Netzwerk Zukunftsorte connects, inspires and shares knowledge for the development of community-based places in rural areas as resilient spaces for social innovation as well as economic and ecological resiliance. Community-based living and working projects in villages and small towns serve as models and experimental hubs for practical climate protection, social cohesion, social entrepreneurship and regional development through the revitalisation of vacant spaces as well as nature and climate protection. As a network, we make good examples visible ( www.zukunftsorte.land/orte ), connect actors and stakeholders, organise knowledge transfer and provide recommendations to policy makers. So far, we have around 80 projects on our map across Germany. In our scaling strategy we want to add several hundred Future Places in the DACH region within the next 3 years and aim at…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Since 2020 our organisation has been instrumental in raising public and political awareness of the potential of community-focused property development in rural areas. We coined the term 'Future Places' to describe impact-driven co-living and co-working projects in the countryside - a term now adopted by many other organisations and government bodies. Thanks to the visibility of our Future Place projects, our publications and the policy dialogue we lead, funding programmes now include more and more of what we promote as crucial to their development. With our help, many Future Places have been…

innovations.name: An innovative approach to working with homeless individuals with substance use disorders in a new type of service (alcohol management)
innovations.problem: The project itself builds on nearly 20 years of work by Depaul Slovakia with homeless people in its services and addresses the lack of low-threshold residential services. The applicant has extensive experience working with homeless people with substance use disorders; it was the first organization in Slovakia to establish the very first low-threshold night shelter in Bratislava, which currently has a capacity of 200 beds.
innovations.desc: The purpose of the project is to create a sufficiently adequate and safe space for working with homeless individuals struggling with addiction who are repeat clients of the applicant, as their addiction prevents them from taking the next step toward integration. Upon completion of the project, a new social service will be established, which will complement the range of low-threshold crisis intervention services in Slovakia while implementing an innovative approach to working with homeless individuals with substance use disorders. The main output of the project—the implementation of an innovative method for managing alcohol consumption within a new type of social service—will support the proposals in the approved National Concept, which mentions the need for the creation of this type of service. Based on the applicant’s internal statistics, some clients of residential services repeatedly…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: The project proposer expects that clients receiving comprehensive support (social, psychological, and community-based), through the application of alcohol management methods, will gradually begin to work toward changing their life circumstances with the long-term goal of reintegration. The project will support that group of homeless people who are motivated to change their life situation but are limited by addiction.

innovations.name: Social Accelerator
innovations.problem: the project aims to reduce structural inequalities, promote social cohesion, and enable a green, digital, and inclusive transition across the region.
innovations.desc: Key activities within the project include: - Mapping existing social innovation initiatives and opportunities in 10 countries. - Establishing Social Labs for co-creation, pilot testing, and knowledge exchange. - Incubating and accelerating startups focused on social and environmental impact. - Delivering training in sustainability, digital skills, gender equity, and impact investment. - Organising contests and hackathons to foster innovation. - Providing competitive funding to third parties, focusing on territorial and sectoral diversity. - Launching a digital platform for e-learning, impact tracking, and community building. - Hosting public-private dialogue spaces to align local strategies with national and regional priorities
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups

innovations.name: Pinhal ImPACT – Itinerant Incubator for Impact Entrepreneurship in the Pinhal Interior
innovations.problem: The Pinhal Interior faces structural challenges common to many rural European regions: population decline, ageing, low density, difficulty in attracting and retaining people, limited access to support structures and weak connections between local ideas, institutions, entrepreneurs and investment opportunities. At the same time, the region has strong natural, cultural, social and entrepreneurial assets. The problem is not the lack of ideas or resources, but the lack of continuous support, coordination and pathways to transform these assets into sustainable initiatives with measurable impact.
innovations.desc:
Pinhal ImPACT builds on previous territorial innovation and social incubation experience, including the I3Social Beiras e Serra da Estrela itinerant social innovation incubator developed by Aldeia dos Girassóis, and adapts this approach to the specific challenges and opportunities of the Pinhal Interior region.
Pinhal ImPACT uses an itinerant incubation model, bringing support directly to different municipalities and communities rather than concentrating services in a single location. The project combines ecosystem mapping, community mobilisation, hackathons, capacity-building laboratories, mentoring, incubation, acceleration and impact monitoring. Its innovation lies in connecting territorial development, social innovation and impact entrepreneurship through a collaborative regional support structure. It brings together municipalities, associations, entrepreneurs, social investors,…

innovations.evidence: Expected results include 280 direct participants, 20 institutions involved in social innovation and experimentation, and 40 incubation, acceleration and capacity-building processes. The project is already mobilising a regional ecosystem through interviews, events, stakeholder engagement and project incubation. Benefits include stronger local collaboration, increased entrepreneurial capacity, better connection between ideas and implementation, support for rural impact projects, and greater visibility for social innovation in low-density territories.

innovations.name: How can we foster integrated, cross-sector approaches to child health and parenting support in order to promote children's well-being and thriving families?
innovations.problem: Families today face increasingly complex challenges, including parental burnout, mental health issues, social isolation, behavioural difficulties, disability, and major life transitions. Yet support services remain fragmented across healthcare, social services, education, and parenting support, making access difficult and reducing the effectiveness of interventions. This fragmentation limits prevention, delays appropriate support, and places an additional burden on families, who must navigate multiple organisations with little coordination between professionals.
innovations.desc: L'Étoile des familles has developed an innovative hybrid multidisciplinary coordinated pathway that brings together professionals from healthcare, parenting support, education, social services, and well-being around the needs of each family, regardless of the child's age and the family dynamics at play. Each personalised pathway combines: individual consultations; parent-child and family workshops; group activities; coordination between regulated and non-regulated professionals. Developed through a Social R&D approach, the model is co-designed with local stakeholders and supported by the creation of a health-focused community hub ("third place"). It promotes prevention, early intervention, and integrated support from preconception through adolescence.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The project delivers benefits at several levels: -For families: easier access to coordinated services, personalised support, stronger parenting confidence, improved family relationships, and enhanced mental well-being. -For professionals: improved multidisciplinary collaboration, better communication, and reduced fragmentation between services. -For the community: stronger social cohesion, more efficient use of local resources, and a preventive approach that may reduce the need for more intensive interventions later.

innovations.name: L'école comestible
innovations.problem:
Food production methods and diet have a major impact on our health, on society and the environment. According to ADEME, diet accounts for between 20 and 50 % of the environmental footprint of the French population. Furthermore, diet is the leading risk factor for the loss of healthy life years, ahead of tobacco, as highlighted by Santé Publique France. Diet is a significant factor in health inequalities, which are linked to socio-spatial inequalities.
The lack of high-quality, affordable food shops in many working-class neighbourhoods increases the risk of food insecurity and health risks for their residents. In light of these findings, it is essential to tackle these inequalities and food…
innovations.desc:
In collaboration with stakeholders in the school and out-of-school sectors, as well as local and national public authorities, l'école comestible offers a series of workshops on healthy and sustainable eating during school hours, mainly in priority neighbourhoods under the urban policy.
Each participating class takes part in 4 to 6 workshops a year, following a structured educational programme and the ‘La bouche pleine et les mains sales’ (Mouths full and hands dirty) methodology, based on hands-on learning (learning through handling, preparing and tasting) and working together (a sense of sharing and community). The workshops are structured around major cross-cutting themes: plants, the seasons, the plant life cycle, tastes and the senses, reducing food waste, world cuisines, etc.
L’école comestible bases its teaching approach on ecological, human and social values.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Since 2019, the association has built up a strong regional network comprising local and regional producers, associations that share its values, and public sector partners, including local authorities and schools. Thanks to this growing network, it has run more than 2,900 workshops, reaching over 20,000 children in 105 schools. L’école comestible also involves 150 dedicated volunteers.

innovations.name: CyclAvenir
innovations.problem:
The association, based in Île-de-France, operates in a region where cycling is one of the preferred modes of transport. However, access to cycling remains uneven, as not everyone has had the opportunity to learn how to ride a bike.
This divide creates barriers for some people, forcing them to turn to more expensive and polluting transport options. In 2023, mobility difficulties were ranked as the second biggest obstacle to returning to work.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
Thanks to short- and long-term programmes, more than 88 % of female beneficiaries say they now feel confident cycling around town.
In total, more than 320 women took part in the training programmes, 150 of whom acquired a bicycle at the end of the programme. Among the programme’s beneficiaries, more than 62 % say they have seen an improvement in their quality of life thanks to regular cycling.

innovations.name: Low-tech Lab
innovations.problem: The low-tech approach offers everyone the means to meet their needs whilst respecting both people and the planet. It aims to answer the question: ‘What do we really need to thrive in a world of constraints?’. For over 10 years, numerous initiatives have emerged across the country. To spread the low-tech approach more widely, it is necessary to support and guide the development of these local initiatives.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The Low-tech Lab wiki has been viewed more than 2 million times to date. It lists more than 300 low-tech systems and techniques, the result of 10 years’ work. There are also 28 documentaries available. The Low-tech Lab also provides the general public with a directory listing more than 950 low-tech initiatives .

innovations.name: Robin.e.s des bennes
innovations.problem:
Les Robin.e.s des Bennes was founded in Amiens, where more than 36,000 residents are living in precarious circumstances. In the Hauts-de-France region, 15.5 per cent of the population lives below the poverty line.
Faced with difficulties in accessing food and clothing, even as many goods and foodstuffs are thrown away, the Robin.e.s des Bennes offer practical solutions to make better use of these resources and meet the basic needs of the most vulnerable members of society.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
According to an impact study carried out in 2023, for every euro invested in the charity, 4.30 euros of social, environmental and economic value will be generated in the local area.
To date, more than 44 tonnes of food, 17 tonnes of textiles and 9 kilograms of plants have been recovered and redistributed free of charge. 82 % of beneficiaries say they have gained purchasing power thanks to these solidarity-based, anti-waste initiatives, and 90 % say that their mindset has changed as a result of their involvement with the association.

innovations.name: Travaux suspendus
innovations.problem:
The climate crisis highlights the urgent need to scale up the renovation of energy-inefficient homes. Yet many owner-occupier households continue to face poor housing conditions and energy poverty.
The construction sector alone accounts for 28 per cent of greenhouse gas emissions in France, whilst more than 2.2 million people are energy-excluded and 1.3 million live in homes that expose them to health and social risks. As existing state support does not always meet the needs of the most vulnerable households, Travaux Suspendus was set up to provide a complementary and tailored solution.
innovations.desc:
Travaux Suspendus works to make decent, refurbished housing accessible to everyone.
The association runs a community of socially-minded building craftspeople who volunteer on renovation projects for substandard housing. These projects, which are free for households in precarious circumstances, are made possible by fundraising from individuals and businesses.
Furthermore, the creation of a dedicated fund enables better remuneration for the building craftspeople, thereby strengthening the social and solidarity-based nature of the initiative.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Since Travaux Suspendus was founded in 2023, more than 50 craftspeople have volunteered for community building projects and more than 100 craftspeople have been involved in collecting donations.

innovations.name: Toit à moi
innovations.problem: The issue of poor housing is one of the major challenges our society has long faced. Today, particularly as a result of the financial and migration crises, it has become an even more pressing issue: between 2001 and 2012, the number of homeless people rose by 50 per cent, reaching 141,500 people without a fixed abode in the latter year ( Infographie Les personnes à la rue , Fondation pour le Logement des Défavorisés, September 2017). Despite a strong commitment from the voluntary sector to the issue of housing support, not all needs can be met and many approaches still need to be developed.
innovations.desc:
In 2006, when they founded the association Toit à Moi in Nantes, Denis Castin and Gwenaël Morvan were determined to transform the small, informal donations that people make on a daily basis into a collective, regular and impactful sponsorship scheme. Their calculation was simple: it would take fewer than 100 people donating an average of €20 a month to finance a flat within five years. They therefore launched a campaign to recruit sponsors, volunteers and patrons, which culminated in 2008 in the securing of a loan and the purchase of their first flat.
The Toi à Moi model is truly built on a principle of cooperation and complementarity between various forms of giving: regular donors help to repay the loans taken out to purchase the flats; volunteers regularly devote their time to activities organised jointly with those who have been rehoused; and corporate sponsors fund the…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
Since 2016, the organisation in Nantes has settled into a comfortable rhythm, with a dedicated community of volunteers and staff working to bring this community of stakeholders to life.
Today, the association owns 18 apartments, which have enabled it to rehouse more than 50 people over the past 10 years.

innovations.name: Association Zoein
innovations.problem:
There are many entrepreneurial citizen-led initiatives working towards the ecological transition, but they still receive too little support from public or private funding.
Those leading transition projects often use their own funds to support their activities and sometimes struggle to make a decent living in a stable environment.
innovations.desc:
Association Zoein provides guidance and financial support to project leaders through the Ecological Transition Income (RTE). Aimed at those committed to the ecological transition, the RTE helps to ensure the long-term sustainability of socially and environmentally innovative initiatives.
The association targets two groups:
project leaders who wish to implement their initiatives and meet with peers;
social and solidarity economy organisations and local authorities that are exploring new ways to revitalise their local areas in an environmentally friendly manner.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Today, seven RTE experimental groups welcome project leaders and their teams so that they can pool their skills and experiences with their peers.
This community brings together more than 70 project leaders across the various experimental fields.

innovations.name: Topophone
innovations.problem:
In priority neighbourhoods and rural areas, young people are particularly affected by a lack of access to musical culture.
In France, around 50 per cent of pupils in state schools take part in musical activities, whether at school or outside school hours. However, this average masks significant inequalities: the figure drops to 30 per cent in the most disadvantaged areas, whilst it reaches 70 per cent in more affluent areas.
innovations.desc:
In order to address inequalities in access to musical culture, Topophone offers a range of music learning and introductory activities aimed at young people:
music workshops and lessons, enabling young people facing social, educational or family difficulties to play a full part in artistic discovery;
music programmes in schools and medical-social settings, aimed at fostering young people’s creative development.
Topophone also organises outreach initiatives to promote local artists through the organisation of concerts.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion

innovations.name: Innovative Solutions for Refugee Integration and Crisis Mitigation in EU Member States (ISRICM-EU)
innovations.problem: Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine has resulted in the displacement of millions of people, creating significant challenges for host communities across the European Union. Displaced Ukrainians often face barriers to employment, education, social inclusion, access to services, and community participation, while public authorities and civil society organisations require innovative approaches to respond effectively to these evolving needs. The project addresses these challenges by developing and promoting social innovation solutions that strengthen integration, improve employability, foster community cohesion, and enhance cooperation among key stakeholders.
innovations.desc: ISRICM-EU applies a transnational social innovation approach that combines education, employability support, entrepreneurship, community engagement, policy dialogue, and stakeholder cooperation into a single integrated framework for refugee inclusion. Rather than addressing individual needs in isolation, the project strengthens collaboration among public authorities, civil society organisations, educational institutions, employers, and local communities to co-create sustainable and transferable solutions. Through knowledge exchange, capacity building, awareness-raising activities, and the testing of innovative practices across multiple EU countries, the project promotes long-term social inclusion and strengthens the capacity of communities to respond effectively to the challenges arising from forced displacement.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: ISRICM-EU delivered significant results by strengthening the social inclusion and resilience of displaced people from Ukraine through coordinated actions implemented across nine European partner organisations. The project enhanced beneficiaries' access to education, vocational training, entrepreneurship support, social services, and community engagement opportunities, while increasing awareness of refugee inclusion among public authorities, employers, civil society organisations, and local communities. Strong stakeholder cooperation was established through transnational collaboration,…

origin.region: Bulgaria, Denmark, Greece, Italy, Slovenia, Spain

innovations.name: #radikalanders – New Work in the Social Economy
innovations.problem: Before the transformation, the organisation was close to insolvency. Rigid hierarchies, central control and heavy bureaucracy produced long decision paths, an elaborate reporting system, overloaded managers – especially middle management – and frustrated teams. The consequences were high sickness-absence rates, poor decisions and a dangerous financial and cultural imbalance. At the same time the whole social and care sector faces a severe shortage of skilled workers, constantly changing client needs and external shocks – pandemics, uncertain public budgets – that centralised, top-down structures cannot react to quickly enough. In the social economy these effects of outdated working cultures…
innovations.desc: Instead of reforming the old structure, AWO Mönchengladbach made a radical break and moved to a self-organised, hierarchy-free model based on the BetaCodex. Today the organisation works like a network of mini-enterprises (“cells”). Decisions are made where the work is – without committees or approval chains – by the colleagues and situational peer groups who hold the relevant knowledge and responsibility; what counts is evidence and competence, not status. The organisation rests on two complementary structures: a value-creation structure, in which cells decide autonomously, close to clients and impact, and a compliance structure that does not control but enables – setting the safe legal, financial and ethical frame within which self-organisation can work; where a decision binds the whole, it is taken jointly and visibly, with no votes but reasoned by evidence. Cells manage their own…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.benef: Arbeiterwohlfahrt Mönchengladbach und im Rhein-Kreis Neuss e.V. (AWO)
innovations.evidence: The organisation moved from the brink of insolvency back to stability, with faster, more flexible decisions taken close to the people it serves. A key measurable outcome concerns staff health: in a joint analysis with the health insurer AOK, colleagues at AWO Mönchengladbach had on average around 10 fewer sick days per year than the sector average, and the share of colleagues with no absence at all was notably higher. Lower staff turnover and a more attractive employer profile have made the organisational model a real advantage in recruiting and retaining skilled workers – decisive in a…
authors: Arbeiterwohlfahrt Mönchengladbach und im Rhein-Kreis Neuss e.V. (AWO)

innovations.name: Climate and Environmental Literacy
innovations.problem: The Adult Literacy for Life programme is a national initiative in Ireland to improve all types of literacy. Notably, over 1 in 5 adults in Ireland does not have a functional level of literacy. Alongside this, many adult learners and adult education tutors do not feel confident engaging with topics of climate change, sustainability, and environmental action.
innovations.desc:
This project, led by ECO-UNESCO in collaboration with Kilkenny and Carlow ETB and Laois and Offaly ETB, comprised several key stages:
Focus groups with adult literacy learners and adult education tutors in target areas
ECO-UNESCO workshops with adult literacy learners; these workshops served to improve participants' climate and environmental literacy, as well as providing valuable feedback on the development of activities for the resource pack
Development of a resource pack, provided in both digital and physical formats, for the use of adult education tutors. The resource pack takes an Education for Sustainable Development approach to building confidence in climate and environmental literacy within adult literacy learning contexts.
Training sessions were delivered by ECO-UNESCO to adult literacy tutors in target areas
The final resource pack was launched in December 2025 with a launch…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
The resource pack, designed with an Education for Sustainable Development approach in mind, has been disseminated through Education and Training Boards across Ireland. Future development of this project includes training sessions to be delivered to ETB staff.
Over 40 individual adult learners were impacted through the workshop sessions for this project, helping to build their climate and environmental literacy.

innovations.name: UNITE Ukrainian Newcomer’s Integration Towards Employment!
innovations.problem: UNITE responds to several challenges faced by Ukrainian refugees when rebuilding their lives in a new country: Loss of stability and networks — people arrive without their familiar support systems, professional contacts, or community ties. Uncertainty about career pathways — qualifications, labour‑market expectations, and job‑search processes differ significantly across EU countries. Language barriers — limited host‑country language skills reduce confidence and access to employment. Emotional strain and insecurity — even highly qualified individuals often experience self‑doubt after displacement and repeated job‑application rejections. Fragmented support systems — many refugees struggle to…
innovations.desc:
The UNITE approach is inspired by an existing model developed by Folkuniversitetet Uppsala in Sweden, where Ukrainian refugees have been supported through mentoring, coaching, and workshops since shortly after the war began. The strong demand and positive outcomes in Sweden demonstrated the value of a holistic, individualised support system. This successful model became the foundation for the EU‑funded UNITE project now piloted in Austria, Germany, Poland, and Sweden.
UNITE introduces an innovative, holistic, and individualised support model, built on the principle that every story is different and every person needs something different. Key elements include: Individual Mentoring Mentors help participants manage uncertainties, rebuild confidence, and navigate everyday integration challenges. This one‑to‑one relationship provides emotional support and practical guidance. Targeted…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities
innovations.evidence: Across Austria, Germany, Poland, and Sweden, UNITE has already shown strong results: Clearer career direction Participants explore possible training pathways and understand how to pursue them in their host country. Several have chosen new vocational training routes and now know how to build their professional future. Successful job placements Many participants have found employment after receiving tailored career orientation, CV checks, and support with motivation letters. Reduced insecurity and increased confidence Even highly qualified individuals often arrive with significant self‑doubt.…

innovations.name: I listen, watch and easily learn a foreign language
innovations.problem: The problem we addressed is that of increasing learning efficiency by capturing students' attention during classes by using an innovative method of displaying words spoken by foreign language teachers.
innovations.desc: We believe that the method of displaying the teacher's words during classes is innovative and uses elements that are easy to install and implement in practice: Bluetooth headset, laptop and a large screen TV.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Ease of use according to what was stated by the teachers in the project. Very useful for students, according to the survey conducted! Benefits: increased attention, higher grades!

innovations.name: Inclusive Recruitment Programme
innovations.problem: People with disabilities continue to experience significant barriers when seeking employment, despite having the skills, qualifications and motivation to work. Traditional employment initiatives often focus on preparing individuals for work and adapting to the workplace but do not sufficiently address the barriers that exist within recruitment systems, workplace cultures and employer practices. Many employers have positive intentions regarding inclusion but lack the knowledge, confidence or practical understanding required to recruit and support employees with disabilities effectively. This can lead to missed opportunities for both employers and jobseekers. The Inclusive Recruitment…
innovations.desc: The Inclusive Recruitment Programme takes a different approach to disability employment by focusing on employers as well as jobseekers. Rather than viewing disability employment solely as a challenge for individuals to overcome, the programme recognises that inclusion is a shared responsibility. It shifts the focus towards preparing workplaces, recruitment systems and hiring professionals to become more accessible and inclusive. The programme provides practical training covering every stage of the employment journey, including accessible recruitment practices, inclusive interviewing, workplace accommodations, onboarding and employee retention. By equipping employers with practical tools and confidence, the programme helps create lasting organisational change rather than one-off recruitment outcomes. This dual approach bridges the gap between job-ready candidates and inclusive employers,…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: The Inclusive Recruitment Programme delivers benefits for individuals, employers and the wider community. For people with disabilities, the programme helps create greater access to meaningful employment opportunities, increased independence, improved confidence and enhanced quality of life. For employers, it provides practical knowledge and tools that support inclusive recruitment and retention practices. It also helps organisations access a wider and often underutilised talent pool, strengthen workplace culture and improve diversity and inclusion outcomes. The wider community benefits from…

innovations.name: Youth Impact Säffle
innovations.problem: Many young people in rural communities feel excluded from decision-making and lack opportunities to influence the present and future of their communities. This contributes to disengagement, outmigration and a loss of valuable perspectives in local development.
innovations.desc: The project brings young people and decision-makers together to co-create solutions to local challenges. Unlike traditional consultation processes, youth-generated ideas are developed into concrete actions and embedded into municipal structures for lasting impact.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The project aims to engage hundreds of young people in shaping their community, strengthen trust between youth and local authorities, and ensure that at least two youth-generated solutions are implemented. Youth impact Säffle also educate decision-makers and creates more inclusive and effective local decision-making processes.

innovations.name: Specialsitter
innovations.problem:
People with disabilities and their families should have the same opportunities in society as every one else.
Article 1 UN-CRPD and other international and EU treaties are the foundation and guidance of our work. According to the German Institute for Human Rights, people with disabilities remain disadvantaged across nearly all areas of life, despite the Convention having been in force for 16 years (Deutsches Institut für Menschenrechte (2025), file:///C:/Users/Anne/OneDrive%20-%20Specialsitter%20GmbH/Desktop/Nebenprojekte/Social%20Innovation/Eckpunkte_Bundestagswahl_2025_MST_UN-BRK.pdf). We aim for the goal to support people in Germany who don’t have the same access and participation in…
innovations.desc: There are multiple ways we intake clients. The vast majority of new requests are arranged through municipal agencies like the Social Welfare Department or the Youth Welfare Department (Youth Welfare Department = 96,81 % and Social Welfare Department = 3,19 %). Some clients find us through online research, and others recommend us to their friends and acquaintances. The first contact of a new client is the coordinating team of the respective site. The coordinating team conducts the admission interview, which covers the entirety of the client’s situation: their diagnosis, their character, their preferences, hobbies, the day-to-day tasks as well as special wishes such as the preferred background or gender of the assistant. After the admission interview, the matching begins. Part of it is digitalized: our dashboard allows us to filter employees, or sitters, according to their qualifications,…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: With our inhouse digital platform we digitalized the administration of assistant services both within and outside our organization, we have transformed the way support services for people with disabilities are delivered. This has streamlined processes and reduced administrative burdens for public authorities. The positive experience with our digital way of working is that our central administration consisted of four employees in 2019 and remained at the same size in 2021, even though the organization had tripled in scale. We attribute these efficiency gains to the implementation of our…

innovations.name: Ro(o)tation - sustainable integration of the long-term unemployed into the labour market
innovations.problem: RO(O)TATION addresses the growing challenge of long-term unemployment, particularly among neurodivergent individuals and people on the autism spectrum, who often face multiple barriers to labour market participation. The project responds to limited access to tailored support, low financial literacy, mental health challenges, employer stereotypes and insufficient cooperation between key stakeholders by developing innovative, community-based and person-centred employment solutions.
innovations.desc: RO(O)TATION combines psychotherapy, financial education, career coaching and subsidised employment into one integrated support pathway for long-term unemployed people. By engaging employers, public institutions, academia and civil society through the Quadruple Helix model, it creates inclusive employment communities and promotes sustainable labour market integration for neurodivergent individuals.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: RO(O)TATION supports 120 long-term unemployed people (including 40 neurodivergent participants) through integrated employment pathways. Key outputs include 24 Diversity Celebration events, 24 Rooted Rooftop employment community meetings, financial education tools, mental wellbeing materials, reports on neuro-friendly workplaces and a sustainable local employment network connecting employers, public institutions and NGOs. The project enhances participants’ employability, mental wellbeing and financial skills, while fostering inclusive workplaces, stronger local partnerships and greater…

innovations.name: Connecting Artists Europe
innovations.problem: The project addresses significant challenges experienced by artists with intellectual disabilities, including social isolation, unequal access to arts opportunities, limited professional progression pathways, and ongoing under-representation within the cultural sector. These challenges are evident both in Ireland and across Europe. Census 2022 found that 56% of people with an intellectual disability in Ireland experience difficulties participating in work, education, and other aspects of daily life, highlighting the barriers that continue to limit inclusion and participation. Similar patterns exist across Europe, where research spanning 28 countries has identified persistent physical,…
innovations.desc: The Connecting Artists Programme responds to these challenges through an innovative, artist-centred model that combines accessible creative development, one-to-one mentoring, peer support, networking, and public engagement opportunities. The programme supports artists with intellectual disabilities to develop their creative practice while building the professional skills required to participate more fully in the arts sector. Participants receive training in areas such as presenting and discussing their work, valuing and pricing artwork to professional standards, framing, and preparing for exhibitions and public showcasing opportunities such as artists talks and workshops. Each artist is paired with an mentor who provides tailored one-to-one support throughout the programme, helping them to identify goals, build confidence, and navigate preparing for exhibition. Through this combination…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Since its launch, the programme has supported 40 artists nationally, generated over €33,000 in artwork sales, delivered exhibitions and public events across Ireland, and created a thriving artist collective. For CAC, engagement reflects how visible our artists are within the broader arts landscape, and how actively they are participating in it. We assess this through: The exhibitions we co-create with participating artists. The development of their artistic portfolios For those pursuing a professional pathway, the sales they generate From 2022 - 2024 12 exhibitions and showcases have been…

innovations.name: Re:Match
innovations.problem: Ukrainian protection seekers often face relocation pathways that do not sufficiently consider their skills, preferences, family needs, or long-term employment prospects. At the same time, German municipalities need better tools to connect available places, local services, housing, and labour-market opportunities with people who are likely to integrate successfully. Re addresses this gap by moving beyond place-based allocation towards needs-based and individualized matching. It responds to the lack of coordinated systems that align individual agency, municipal capacities, and job-market integration, creating safer, more informed, and more sustainable relocation pathways.
innovations.desc: Re introduces a human-centred, data-supported approach to refugee relocation that matches people not only to available places, but to municipalities where their skills, preferences, family circumstances, and employment prospects are most likely to lead to successful integration. The project combines algorithm-based matching with human support, bringing together individual profiles, municipal capacities, housing availability, local services, and labour-market opportunities. Through outreach, informed decision-making, municipal coordination, relocation support, and follow-up after arrival, Re creates more sustainable integration outcomes for both participants and host communities. By linking labour-market needs with individual aspirations and local capacities, the project offers a scalable model for needs-based and employment-oriented relocation that can be adapted across Europe.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities
innovations.evidence: Re enables Ukrainian protection seekers to make informed relocation decisions and access employment opportunities that better match their skills and professional experience. Participants benefit from increased agency, improved access to information, and stronger prospects for long-term economic and social integration. Municipalities benefit from better matching outcomes, improved retention, and stronger alignment between local labour-market needs and incoming residents. Employers gain access to qualified talent, helping address labour shortages in key sectors. The project demonstrates that…

innovations.name: Community Centre
innovations.problem: The Chiojdu community lacked a dedicated, accessible space for social activities that could strengthen community cohesion and support local development. At the same time, there was a need to preserve local architectural identity, engage community members in decision-making processes, and create opportunities that would stimulate the local economy in a sustainable manner. The project responded to these challenges through a participatory process that identified community needs and priorities directly with local stakeholders.
innovations.desc: The Chiojdu Community Center was conceived through a collaborative and participatory design process involving local community members, students and teachers from the “Ion Mincu” University of Architecture and Urbanism, local authorities, artisans, and businesses. The center combines contemporary architecture with elements inspired by traditional wooden architecture specific to the area, creating a contemporary yet locally rooted intervention. The project applies circular economy principles by prioritizing local resources, engaging local craftsmen and companies in the construction process, and supporting knowledge transfer between generations. Through three international ArhiPera Summer Schools, architecture students actively participated in the construction process, developing innovative applications of traditional, eco-friendly materials while working directly with community members.…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: - Creation of a multifunctional community facility that addresses local social needs. - Enhanced collaboration between academia, public authorities, civil society, and the local community. - Strengthened community engagement through participatory planning, design, and implementation processes. - Preservation and contemporary reinterpretation of local architectural heritage. - Support for the local economy through the involvement of local contractors, artisans, and businesses. - Development of practical skills and knowledge among architecture students through hands-on construction experience.…

innovations.name: VEM mobility with dignity
innovations.problem: Millions of older adults, people with disabilities, and individuals with reduced mobility face significant barriers when accessing healthcare, public services, cultural activities, and community life. While transport systems may exist, many people cannot use them independently and lack reliable human support. As a result, they often miss appointments, reduce social interactions, become increasingly isolated, and experience a loss of autonomy, wellbeing, and quality of life. Families and caregivers frequently struggle to provide the necessary support, creating additional emotional and practical burdens. With Europe's ageing population and growing demand for inclusive services, the lack of…
innovations.desc:
VEM was inspired by existing independent living, mobility assistance and community accompaniment approaches that support people with disabilities and older adults. It also draws on sighted guiding practices used by organisations supporting people with visual impairments. However, VEM combines these principles into a professional, on-demand, door-to-door mobility support model tailored to the Portuguese context, with a strong focus on autonomy, dignity and social inclusion.
VEM introduces a new approach to inclusive mobility by focusing on the human support that many people need to move safely and independently within their communities. While existing solutions typically focus on transportation, VEM addresses the gap between transport availability and actual accessibility. Through a network of trained companions, the service provides door-to-door assistance before, during, and after each…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: VEM enables older adults and people with disabilities to access healthcare, public services, cultural activities, and community life with greater independence and confidence. Key benefits include reduced social isolation, improved wellbeing, increased autonomy, better access to essential services, and reduced burden on families and caregivers. The model also creates meaningful employment opportunities for young people while promoting disability awareness and social inclusion. Since launching, VEM has already supported dozens of beneficiaries through more than 300 assisted mobility missions,…

innovations.name: Centro de Inovação Carlos Fiolhais
innovations.problem: Across Europe, the digital divide remains one of the most pressing social challenges of our time. In 2025, only 60% of EU citizens aged 16–74 had at least basic digital skills, with stark disparities linked to education level — ranging from 82% among those with high formal education to just 38% among those with low or no formal education. In Portugal, basic digital skills remain unevenly distributed across society, and according to the 2023 International Computer and Information Literacy Study, 37% of Portuguese eighth-graders have a low level of digital skills. But the problem goes deeper than access or basic literacy. Young people are heavy consumers of technology yet rarely learn to use…
innovations.desc:
The CICF in Maia joins an existing national ecosystem. CDI Portugal's Digital Citizenship Centre in Valongo, for instance, is already in its 8th edition (2024/25), having been inaugurated in 2018, demonstrating that this model can achieve long-term continuity and institutionalisation. The CICF represents an evolution of this approach — more structured, thematically richer and co-branded — that can serve as the new benchmark for future centres.
The CICF's innovation lies not in any single technology or tool, but in a comprehensive model that reimagines how, where and for whom learning happens. A "choose your own journey" learning architecture. Rather than following a fixed curriculum, participants choose from seven thematic universes — Code, Bot, Play, Make, Green, Voice and Link — covering areas from AI and robotics to media literacy, digital fabrication and community engagement. innovations.problem:

The patient pathway is structured and gradual. Upon admission to the First Lviv Territorial Medical Union, former prisoners of war first undergo comprehensive medical assessment and stabilisation. innovations.name: Rural Revive
innovations.problem: Long-term unemployment in rural areas poses significant economic, social and infrastructural challenges that are structurally distinct from urban unemployment. In the project's target regions of Crete in Greece and Cavan/Monaghan in Ireland, adults aged 45+ face compounding barriers rooted in geographical isolation, inadequate infrastructure and reliance on declining industries and seasonally dominated sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, retail and tourism. Ireland's LTU rate stands at 26.3%, with rural areas most affected. Those who are long-term unemployed in Ireland tend to have been out of work for over a decade, a troubling trend driven by insufficient wages, lack of effective…
innovations.desc:
Rural Revive builds directly upon two proven models from Austria that have demonstrated measurable success in addressing long-term unemployment through employer engagement and guaranteed employment schemes.
The first is the MAGMA Model, which provides unconditional job guarantees for long-term unemployed individuals, matching them with suitable jobs while offering ongoing support including training, counselling, and health services. The success of MAGMA lies in its comprehensive approach, which integrates not only job creation but also social support, leading to sustainable employment outcomes. The project has helped over 112 long-term unemployed individuals secure employment through customised support services and job guarantees.
The second is the V/Faktor Initiative, which focuses on employer engagement and skills development, equipping employers with the tools and knowledge to create…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Rural Revive directly targets 100 long-term unemployed individuals aged 45+ across Ireland and Greece, providing them with stable employment, fair and decent wages and personal development through career coaching and training - rebuilding confidence, improving employability and addressing skill gaps. A minimum of 30 rural employers will be engaged across both countries benefiting from subsidised employment costs, access to trained workers and improved inclusive hiring practices that broaden their talent pool. At least 50% of participants are targeted to be offered contract extensions or to…

innovations.name: I want to work
innovations.problem: People facing poverty, homelessness, low education, long-term unemployment, migration backgrounds or other vulnerabilities often encounter multiple and interconnected barriers to employment. Conventional employment measures rarely provide the long-term, individualised support needed to overcome these challenges, resulting in persistent exclusion from the labour market and society.
innovations.desc:
The project was inspired by other Work Integration Social Enterprise (WISE) models that combine paid employment, personalised support and skills development for people facing barriers to employment. Ateliere Fără Frontiere adapted this approach to the Romanian context, integrating circular economy activities with socio-professional inclusion pathways.
The programme applies a Work Integration Social Enterprise (WISE) model that combines real paid employment, personalised socio-professional support and skills development within circular economy activities. By integrating economic activity with social support, participants gain work experience, professional skills and confidence in a protected yet realistic work environment, preparing them for transition to the open labour market.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
The model was adapted and scaled within Bio&Co, AFF’s organic farm in rural Romania. While following the same socio-professional integration methodology and personalised support pathway, the programme was adjusted to local labour market realities by removing the standard two-year time limit, as employment opportunities in the area are significantly more limited than in urban settings.
Since 2008, the programme has supported over 8,000 people towards labour market integration and provided employment opportunities for 360 people within Ateliere Fără Frontiere’s circular economy workshops. In…

innovations.name: Youth Aware of Mental Health (YAM)
innovations.problem: In recent years, there has been a growing recognition of an increase in mental health problems among adolescents, ranging from clinical disorders to broader emotional distress and well-being difficulties. These issues often emerge during adolescence and may persist into adulthood, where they can become more severe and consolidated, generating significant personal suffering as well as long-term costs for healthcare systems and society as a whole. At the same time, there is an increasing sense of disconnection between young people and key social environments, particularly schools and community support services. Many adolescents report feeling that existing resources are not designed for them,…
innovations.desc:
The project is based on the SEYLE study (Saving and Empowering Young Lives in Europe), a large-scale European research initiative focused on the promotion of adolescent mental health and suicide prevention in school settings across several European countries. SEYLE provided evidence on the effectiveness of school-based, universal prevention programmes and served as a key reference for the development of YAM (Youth Aware of Mental Health).
The innovative solution of the programme is based on bringing mental health promotion directly into the adolescents’ most familiar environment: the school setting. By working within the educational centre, the programme ensures accessibility and reduces barriers to participation. The sessions are delivered by professionals with experience in mental health who are specifically trained in the programme methodology. Their role is not to provide answers,…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The programme has demonstrated positive outcomes in increasing mental health awareness and reducing stigma among adolescents. Students show greater willingness to talk about emotional well-being and to seek help when needed. The participatory approach fosters student engagement and empowers young people to take an active role in their own well-being. Overall, YAM contributes to prevention, improved emotional literacy, and better connection between young people and available social and community resources.
The YAM (Youth Aware of Mental Health) programme has been replicated and implemented in…

innovations.name: “Bridges Beyond Bars” – Supporting Children of Romanian Prisoners Across Europe
innovations.problem: Many tens of thousands children across Europe experience the negative consequences of parental imprisonment. In the Romanian context, a significant number of citizens (over 10.000) are incarcerated in other European countries while their children remain in Romania, often under the care of relatives or extended family members. These children face multiple challenges, including increased risk of school dropout, emotional distress, social stigma, reduced parental support and limited access to specialised services. Despite their vulnerability, they often remain invisible to public authorities and social support systems. Currently, there is no coordinated transnational mechanism that allows…
innovations.desc:
The project is based on the SEYLE study (Saving and Empowering Young Lives in Europe), a large-scale European research initiative focused on the promotion of adolescent mental health and suicide prevention in school settings across several European countries. SEYLE provided evidence on the effectiveness of school-based, universal prevention programmes and served as a key reference for the development of YAM (Youth Aware of Mental Health).
The innovative aspect of the proposed project lies in its transnational and child centred approach. While support services for prisoners or vulnerable children exist in many countries, there are currently very few mechanisms that connect imprisoned parents abroad with support services for their children in their country of origin. The project introduces a coordinated model involving prisons, civil society organisations, schools and local authorities…

innovations.name: Ajungem MARI
innovations.problem: Children and young people in the child protection system face multiple forms of vulnerability caused by traumatic experiences such as abandonment, family separation, neglect, or abuse, often occurring in their earliest years of life. These experiences affect their emotional, educational, and social development, increasing the risk of social exclusion and limiting their chances of integration and autonomy in adulthood. In Romania, more than 36000 children and young people in the protection system need consistent support, stable relationships, and positive role models who can help them build confidence in their own potential. Many of them face educational gaps, limited access to personal…
innovations.desc: The innovative solution proposed by the Ajungem MARI program consists of creating a national network of volunteers and specialists who provide long‑term educational, emotional, and mentoring support to institutionalized children and young people. Unlike one‑off interventions, the program builds consistent, trust‑based relationships between volunteers and beneficiaries, helping reduce the effects of institutionalization and increasing their chances of social integration. The intervention model integrates non‑formal education, mentoring, academic support, personal development activities, vocational guidance, vocational and professional training courses, as well as specialized services such as psychotherapy and speech therapy, all tailored to the individual needs of each child. This multidisciplinary approach addresses educational, emotional, and developmental needs, contributing to trauma…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The socio‑educational innovation Ajungem MARI was launched in Bucharest in 2014, starting with zero financial resources, and beginning the following year it was replicated and expanded nationwide. In these cases, outreach is either accompanied by training ambassadors or contact with the training ambassadors is established by Joblinge staff only afterwards. In addition, the recruitment of ambassadors has been revised. Ambassadors are now deployed…

innovations.name: Cluj Innovation and Experiment Fund
innovations.problem: Young people with innovative ideas often lack access to practical entrepreneurial education, early-stage funding, and real connections to the startup ecosystem. As a result, many ideas never move beyond concept stage. FIX Cluj addresses this gap by providing structured support, resources, and opportunities to turn ideas into viable startups.
innovations.desc: FIX Cluj offers an integrated innovation pathway that combines digital learning, incubation, funding, and ecosystem access in one program. By linking education with real startup support, it enables young teams to move from idea to company with tailored guidance, resources, and direct funding opportunities.

innovations.name: Community Lunch
innovations.problem: Community Lunch responds to a deeply entrenched and multi-layered crisis affecting children in disadvantaged communities across Romania, one of the most acute in the European Union. Child poverty and food insecurity. Over 32% of Romanian children — more than 1.16 million — live in risk of poverty or social exclusion. In the past year there has been a worrying increase in the number of families that cannot afford a meal with meat or fish even once every two days. School dropout and educational exclusion. In 2024, over 400,000 children aged 7 to 17 were outside the education system, representing 18.7% of the resident population of that age. Romania has one of the highest early school leaving…
innovations.desc: Community Lunch is not a food aid programme. It is a community activation model that uses the shared meal as a catalyst — a deliberate social technology for rebuilding trust, stimulating learning and generating local educational ecosystems in communities where institutional support has largely failed. What makes it innovative is not any single element, but the integration of all of them. 1. The meal as a pedagogical tool. Rather than distributing food packages or vouchers, Community Lunch organises the cooking and eating of meals together — children, elderly people, volunteers and community members side by side. This transforms a basic survival need into a recurring ritual of socialisation, dignity and belonging. The table becomes a classroom without walls. 2. Non-formal learning embedded in every event. Every Community Lunch includes structured workshops on literacy and reading…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Since its launch in January 2021, Community Lunch has grown from a two-community pilot into a national network active across Romania, with documented, measurable results across five dimensions: food security, education, community cohesion, environmental impact and institutional leverage. From pilot to national network — growth over 4 years. The programme started in 2 communities in 2 counties. By 2025 it operated across 19 urban and rural communities in 10 counties — Hunedoara, Ialomița, Ilfov, Gorj, Vâlcea, Giurgiu, Tulcea, Bacău, Prahova and București — and had prepared hot meals for at…

innovations.name: Kopfsachen – Mental Health Prevention in Schools
innovations.problem: Research shows that 75% of all mental health conditions emerge before the age of 25. Yet most young people never receive support (Molecular Psychiatry, 2023). The gap is widest among those from socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds, where access to private therapy is limited, schools are under-resourced, and mental health remains stigmatised. Schools are the one institution that reaches all young people regardless of background but educators lack the training, tools and structures to respond effectively. Without early prevention, mental health challenges translate directly into educational disengagement, school dropout and reduced life chances.
innovations.desc: Most school mental health initiatives rely on external experts who deliver a session and leave. Kopfsachen takes the opposite approach: rather than importing support from outside, it builds lasting capacity from within the school itself. Five staff members per school are trained as Mental Health Ambassadors over one year. We are equipping them to recognise warning signs, lead preventive programmes and build peer support networks. They are not therapists, but skilled first responders embedded in the everyday life of the school. Age-specific workshops reach every student cohort: younger students explore emotions and transitions in peer-led clubs, middle schoolers develop self-care strategies, older students build resilience for key life transitions. Parents are brought in as partners, not afterthoughts. Older students support younger ones through structured peer mentoring. And when the…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: By end of 2028, the programme will have directly reached 12,900 people: 6,000 students through workshops, 750+ students through peer clubs, 1,500 teachers through training, 4,500 parents through awareness events, and 150 staff trained as Mental Health Ambassadors. A further 12,000 students benefit indirectly through the structural changes embedded in their schools. But the numbers only tell part of the story. The programme's deepest impact lies in what remains after it ends: 150 trained Mental Health Ambassadors embedded in their schools, equipped with practical skills, and connected through…

innovations.name: ZekkiPro
innovations.problem: Measures and digital tools are rare in social work globaly. However, digitalization is becoming more and more popular with the advent of artificial intelligence for the use of social welfare. Often, data collections with meters appear to respondents from traditional forms and it is not motivating for the customer, especially young people, to answer administrative queries. There is therefore a clear need for customer-oriented user interfaces that strengthen agency and inclusion. If support cannot be accessed on time, problems become more complex and prolonged. This can lead to social exclusion (loneliness), marginalisation and resentment towards society. At the same time, the society loses…
innovations.desc:
ZekkiPro is based on the experiences from open zekki.fi website.
ZekkiPro offers support for strengthening wellbeing in three ways. First, an understanding of one's own life situation becomes clear to the respondent when he or she does a quick but comprehensive life situation survey which highlights both problems but also strengths. Often, one's own resources are hidden if there are difficulties in some area of life. Seeing areas of life that are in good shape supports in trouble. Second, ZekkiPro can be used to generate verbal, encouraging feedback for each area of life. This way, a professional can use ZekkiPro to give their customers the kind of feedback they think is best. Third, ZekkiPro also offers the organization's own services based on the self-assessment of the clients. ZekkiPro is integrated into the national Suomi.fi Service Data Reserve and picks up from there suitable…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The roots of ZekkiPro are in 3X10D measure and open Zekki.fi website. 3X10D is widely used in projects and social services nationwide. The measure is validated before, and validating studies are going on. Zekki.fi is nominated in 2021 European innovation council's the best European social innovation (EUSIC) award and it has also been awarded in national competitions. ZekkiPro is also integrated into the organization's customer information system and its results have been taken to the organization's information management dashboard.

innovations.name: The Magic Locker
innovations.problem: Children from disadvantaged rural communities often lack the basic school supplies needed to participate fully in class. Many come from families facing financial hardship, including large families, single-parent households or families in which children are raised by grandparents. The problem is not limited to the beginning of the school year: notebooks, writing instruments, backpacks and other materials must be replaced continuously as they are used, lost or damaged. Previous support initiatives showed that one-time donations do not always provide a lasting solution. Even when pupils receive individual school-supply packages, the materials may be left at home, lost or returned to school in…
innovations.desc: The Magic Locker replaces one-off school-supply donations with a recurrent, school-based support mechanism. A dedicated locker is installed inside each participating school and stocked with the materials pupils need throughout the year, including notebooks, writing instruments, drawing supplies, pencil cases, backpacks and reusable items such as geometry sets. Consumable supplies are replenished periodically, ensuring that support remains available after the beginning of the school year. Each locker is managed by a volunteer teacher who distributes supplies fairly, according to the pupils’ needs. This simple system ensures that essential materials are available at the right place and at the right time, while reducing the risk that they are lost, damaged or left at home. It also removes the stigma associated with arriving at school without the supplies needed to take part in lessons. The…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Since its launch in 2021, The Magic Locker has developed into a recurrent educational support programme. More than 50 fully equipped lockers have been installed in rural schools across four Romanian counties: Arad, Bihor, Timiș and Vaslui. Existing lockers are replenished throughout the school year, while additional schools are included as new partnerships and funding become available. The project has expanded steadily: In 2021, approximately 700 pupils received support. In 2022, around 1,400 children from 12 schools benefited from the supplies available through the lockers. innovations.name: "Coach for Inclusion". Training coaches with disabilities for a more inclusive society
innovations.problem: There are approximately 957,000 people with disabilities (various abilities) in Romania. All of them, down to the last one, have valuable life experiences and extraordinary resilience, and many of them also have extraordinary empathy. Because it is not easy for them to make it in a country where accessibility is often non-existent, and inclusion is still seen as an obligation.
innovations.desc:
We transform people with disabilities from simple beneficiaries into authors of change. Our company previously offered the opportunity for 3 people with disabilities to complete the coaching training program. Seeing the impact on them, we decided to take the project to a much higher level.
We have confirmed a fundamental need: there are people who do not want to be defined by their limitations or viewed exclusively through the prism of compassion. Beyond these, they seek real opportunities for development, autonomy and contribution. They want to be part of a more united and inclusive “we”, a community where differences do not separate, but complement. And now we want to develop the first coaching training groups dedicated to people with disabilities, conducted entirely online and adapted to the needs of the participants. In a pragmatic sense, our project creates: ✔ Leaders of inclusion…

innovations.name: AGRI-CIRC SocInoLab: Developing an innovation ecosystem and tools to support social innovation in agriculture and the circular economy.
innovations.problem: Less-developed rural regions across Slovakia face severe socio-economic decline, depopulation, and limited municipal capacity, exacerbated by high structural long-term unemployment rates often exceeding 10%. Vulnerable populations, including individuals with disabilities, long-term unemployed youth (NEETs), and marginalized groups, face immense barriers to labor market integration. While social farming and the circular economy offer tremendous local development potential, their implementation has been stifled by a total absence of cross-sectoral collaboration. Standard approaches isolate farmers from social workers and disconnect waste management entities from the enterprises that could…
innovations.desc: The project introduces a highly novel framework that breaks traditional sector silos by combining social farming and the circular economy into a unified, cross-sectoral regional ecosystem. Departing from traditional top-down integration models, it utilizes cutting-edge tools including gamification, artificial intelligence (AI) for innovation scouting, hybrid (online/offline) decentralized incubators, and scientific modeling. Through active "Living Labs" and co-design workshops, target groups co-create the solutions rather than acting as passive recipients, structurally shifting public governance from a hierarchical setup to a highly participatory, decentralized model.

The initiative adapted these principles to the Romanian educational context through the development of an integrated operational model combining anonymous early listening mechanisms, restorative educational interventions, teacher training and interinstitutional collaboration.
The initiative developed an integrated, community-based and restorative intervention model that…

innovations.name: FORTIFY: Empowering Greek Systems to Protect and Prevent Delinquency in Unaccompanied Minors
innovations.problem: The project addresses the need to prevent juvenile delinquency among unaccompanied minors in Greece by strengthening the capabilities of Greek practitioners and improving existing prevention systems. The project also addresses the need for a better understanding of current prevention challenges, stronger professional capacities, and the adoption of effective practices tailored to the Greek context. More specifically, the project tackles: Gaps in existing juvenile delinquency…
