innovations.name: Educational Hub – The Art of Being Together
innovations.problem: The local community of Anina lacks a modern and inclusive space dedicated to educational, cultural, and personal development. Children, young people, adults, and seniors have limited access to non-formal learning opportunities, artistic activities, and intergenerational programs that promote social inclusion, active citizenship, emotional well-being, and community engagement. This gap reduces opportunities for personal growth, cultural participation, and meaningful connections between generations.
innovations.desc:
The inspiration for the project came from the direct work with students in a school environment and from the identified need for a dedicated space where young people can learn, express themselves, and develop through non-formal education, arts, and collaborative activities. The idea emerged from practical experience within the local educational context in Anina, Romania, under the guidance of teacher Ruva Valentina Ancuța, where the lack of such a space for students was clearly observed.
The project introduces a multidisciplinary Educational Hub that combines non-formal education, arts, culture, volunteering, and intergenerational learning in a single inclusive space. By bringing together children, young people, adults, and seniors through creative, educational, and community-based activities, the Hub fosters lifelong learning, social cohesion, emotional intelligence, and active…

The experience provides a practical example of how non-formal education, arts, and volunteering can be combined to strengthen social cohesion at local level.

innovations.name: WISE – Supporting Ukrainian Refugee Women’s Socio-Economic Integration and Wellbeing
innovations.problem: UA refugee women face unique socio-economic integration challenges in IT and BG. Their higher education and skills contrast with the low-skilled, part-time jobs they secure due to language barriers and a mismatch between qualifications and available jobs (European Commission, 2023). In the context of forced displacement and forced conscription of UA men, women have no choice but to be fully responsible for caring responsibilities of children and elderly relatives. This limits women's labour market participation (UN Women and UNFPA, 2022), with 33% of women unable to work due to care obligations (FRA, Eurofound, 2023). It was subsequently adapted for implementation in public schools, including Școala Gimnazială Gălbinași (Călărași County) and Școala Generală Șag (Timiș County). These adaptations demonstrated that the framework can function effectively in both formal and non-formal education settings while preserving its core educational principles.
STEAM Clubs combines four complementary innovations. First, it leverages an existing nationwide public infrastructure rather than creating new educational centers. The project transforms Children’s Palaces and Clubs into local STEAM hubs, activating an underutilized network of public non-formal education institutions that already reaches tens of thousands of children throughout Romania. Second, it equips local teachers to become facilitators of hands-on…

Expanding to 16 locations in autumn through confirmed partnerships. • More than 420 children participating in the program and 44 teachers trained to facilitate hands-on STEAM learning. • Successful implementation in both large urban centers and smaller communities, demonstrating the model’s relevance across diverse…

innovations.name: Magic Donkey Land
innovations.problem: Many children today experience increased stress, social isolation, excessive screen exposure and limited access to meaningful outdoor activities. Rural communities often lack innovative educational and therapeutic services that support children's emotional wellbeing and social inclusion. Vulnerable children, including those with special educational needs, frequently face barriers in accessing nature-based interventions. Magic Donkey Land addresses these challenges by providing accessible, inclusive and nature-centered experiences that improve children's wellbeing, confidence and social skills.
innovations.desc: Magic Donkey Land offers a unique combination of donkey-assisted activities, outdoor experiential learning and social inclusion programs. Unlike traditional educational or recreational services, the project uses the natural bond between children and donkeys to encourage empathy, emotional regulation, communication and self-confidence. The activities take place in a farm-based environment where children learn through direct experience, interaction with animals and connection with nature. This innovative approach combines social impact, animal welfare, environmental awareness and rural development within a sustainable social enterprise model.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Since its establishment, Magic Donkey Land has engaged hundreds of children and families in educational, recreational and therapeutic activities. Participants report increased self-confidence, improved social interaction, stronger emotional wellbeing and a deeper connection with nature. The project has created local employment opportunities, promoted animal welfare and strengthened community involvement. It also contributes to raising awareness about alternative educational methods and the positive role of animal-assisted interventions in child development.

innovations.name: FLOW leerecosysteem
innovations.problem: Many young people struggle to identify their talents, interests and future opportunities. Those facing social, educational or economic barriers are particularly at risk of exclusion, low self-confidence and disengagement from learning and participation in society. FLOW addresses this challenge by creating accessible opportunities for young people to explore their strengths, connect with others and build meaningful pathways for their personal development and future.
innovations.desc: FLOW’s innovation lies in its ecosystem approach. Instead of offering a single programme or service, FLOW connects youth organisations, cultural actors, social services and creative learning environments into one flexible network around the young person. Young people are not guided towards predefined outcomes but are encouraged to discover their talents, interests and intrinsic motivation through real-life experiences, creativity, participation and reflection. This personalised, strengths-based approach helps them build confidence, ownership and meaningful pathways for their future. By combining cross-sector collaboration with talent-oriented guidance, FLOW creates learning opportunities that are more accessible, engaging and responsive to the needs of young people.
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: FLOW helps young people discover their talents, interests and strengths through creative, cultural and community-based experiences. Participants gain confidence, develop social and personal skills, expand their networks and become more engaged in learning and society. The project also strengthens collaboration between youth organisations, cultural actors and social services, creating more accessible and personalised opportunities for young people, especially those at risk of exclusion.

innovations.name: Providing Integrated Services in Rural Communities — Facilitating Access of Vulnerable Persons to Efficient and Quality Basic Services
innovations.problem: A child at risk of dropping out of school may simultaneously need educational support, medical care, and social assistance. An elderly person living alone may need care, medical monitoring, and social support all at once. A person with disabilities needs not just a financial benefit, but access to healthcare, rehabilitation, counselling, and community integration. Yet public systems are organised by domain, and vulnerable people are left to navigate different institutions on their own. This is the daily reality for millions of people in rural Romania. Poverty in rural communities is not a single problem — it is multiple, overlapping deprivations: poor health, low school attendance,…
innovations.desc: The project "Providing Integrated Services in Rural Communities — Facilitating Access of Vulnerable Persons to Efficient and Quality Basic Services" (PIDS/586/PO4/339395) addresses this systemic gap through the creation of 2,000 Integrated Community Teams (ICTs) in the most marginalized rural localities, implemented from January 2025 to December 2029 and co-financed by the European Social Fund Plus through the Inclusion and Social Dignity Programme 2021–2027. The ICTs are multidisciplinary teams composed of social workers and social assistance technicians, community health nurses and health mediators, school counselors, school mediators, speech therapists, and support teachers, supplemented — depending on the results of the social diagnosis — by elderly care workers, psychologists, social economy specialists, youth workers, and community development facilitators. This integrated service…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.benef: Ministry of Labor, Family, Youth and Social Solidarity
innovations.evidence: The project targets 450,000 vulnerable persons across 2,000 rural administrative units who will gain improved access to social, health, and educational services — including 40,500 Roma persons. A total of 10,000 professionals will be deployed across the 2,000 communities, of whom 6,373 will obtain a formal qualification, contributing directly to raising the quality of services offered to vulnerable persons in rural communities. Additionally, 2,000 community spaces will be renovated and equipped, and 2,000 approved and funded action plans will be developed, one for each locality. Progress…
authors: Ministry of Labor, Family, Youth and Social Solidarity

innovations.name: Edumetrix: From a 108-School Pilot to National Scale
innovations.problem: Many schools lack reliable mechanisms for understanding their strengths, challenges and development needs. Educational decisions are often based on fragmented information, while school leaders have limited access to tools that support evidence-based planning, stakeholder engagement and continuous improvement. These challenges are particularly significant in schools serving vulnerable communities, where inequalities in educational opportunities and outcomes are more pronounced. There is a need for scalable solutions that help schools collect, analyse and use data effectively to drive sustainable improvement and promote educational equity.
innovations.desc: Edumetrix transforms a validated school transformation methodology into a scalable digital solution. Building on the experience gained through the School Transformation Programme implemented in 108 schools, the platform enables schools to assess organisational performance, educational quality and wellbeing through structured data collection and analysis. Schools receive tailored insights and recommendations based on feedback from students, teachers and school leaders. These insights support the development of evidence-based improvement plans and facilitate continuous monitoring of progress. The innovation lies in combining a proven school improvement methodology with digital technology, making high-quality diagnostics and school development processes accessible to a much larger number of schools while maintaining consistency and comparability of results.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The innovation was initially developed and validated through the School Transformation Programme implemented in 108 schools across Romania, engaging more than 50,000 students, over 4,000 teachers and 120 school leaders. Lessons learned from the pilot informed the development of Edumetrix, a scalable digital platform that standardises school diagnostics, improvement planning and progress monitoring.
The School Transformation Programme remains active, while Edumetrix represents the scaling mechanism developed from the pilot experience. The current scaling phase focuses on expanding access to…

innovations.name: Maurice & Nora
innovations.problem: Europe faces a growing care gap. In Flanders alone, the number of people over 80 is set to double to around 640,000 by 2040, while the pool of informal family caregivers shrinks. This squeezes the "sandwich generation", often women, between raising children and caring for ageing parents. Roughly one in two people over 50 provides informal care, frequently leading to reduced working hours or burnout, and care responsibilities fall disproportionately on women. At the same time, many seniors face loneliness and risk premature institutionalisation, and many young people lack meaningful, human work. Existing solutions are either expensive, hard to access, or rely on impersonal gig-economy…
innovations.desc: We use technology for humanity, not to replace it. Three elements make the model distinctive. First, we perform the matching ourselves through a bias-free algorithm based on personality, interests, abilities, and logistics, rather than letting clients pick by photo or name. This gives every student equal opportunity regardless of background or appearance. Second, we automate the cognitive drudgery, scheduling, payments, contracts, intake calls, and routing, using AI and voice agents so coordination happens in minutes rather than weeks, and so the time between student and family stays purely human. Third, we use a B2B2C model: employers fund the service as a care benefit through existing cafeteria and flexible-pay plans, removing the cost barrier for families while protecting employee wellbeing and productivity. Together this makes trusted intergenerational care scalable and accessible…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Maurice & Nora has grown into an active community of seniors, families, and students. To date the platform has over 3,900 registered clients and more than 3,800 screened students ready to help, with new registrations still coming in daily. The company closed a 1 million euro seed round in 2026 and ran a national launch campaign with broad press, radio, and television coverage. Recognition includes Business Startup of the Year and the Platforms category win at the Belgium Startup Awards, the HR Tech Startup Award 2025 by HR Magazine, and the Happy Aging Award 2025 by In4care, alongside a…

innovations.name: Savnet IT Academies - Connecting Skills to Opportunities. Together.
innovations.problem: 1. The digital skills gap that holds back people and economies. Demand for IT professionals far outpaces supply across Europe. Technology evolves faster than formal education can adapt, leaving roles unfilled, companies under pressure, and entire regions unable to keep up with digital transformation. We close this gap by training people in the exact, certified skills the labour market needs right now. 2. Youth unemployment and the academia-to-industry gap. Too many capable graduates leave university with strong theory but with less hands-on, job-ready skills and recognized certifications employers require — and they struggle to find their first role. We bridge that gap with practical,…
innovations.desc: Savnet IT Academies introduce a new model for closing the digital skills gap: high-quality, certification-based IT education delivered at zero commercial cost to both learners and employers, financed entirely by industry through corporate social responsibility. The innovation is not the training itself — it is who pays, why, and how the value flows back to society. A reversed financing model. Conventional IT education places the cost on the student or the employer, which excludes the very people who would benefit most. We reverse this: companies sponsor full cohorts as part of their CSR strategy, students learn for free, and the public good — a more employable, digitally skilled population — is produced as a direct result. Private investment is converted into shared social value. A self-sustaining, multi-stakeholder ecosystem. Rather than acting alone, we connect four actors that rarely…

Learning is hands-on, supported by three fully equipped labs with servers and 100+ routers and switches, and validated through 40+ internationally recognized certifications and badges. Quality is underpinned by world-class instructors — including trainers ranked in the global top 25% and top 10% best Cisco CCNA Instructors worldwide for over 30 times — backed by 4 partner universities and 5 international educational partnerships.…

innovations.name: Youngsters for the Future
innovations.problem: Every year, thousands of young people in Romania leave the child protection system and are expected to begin adult life with limited support. Many do so without stable family relationships, financial security, safe housing, trusted guidance, or access to consistent mental health services. This transition exposes them to poverty, unemployment, housing instability, social isolation, untreated trauma, and a high risk of long-term exclusion. The move into adulthood is often abrupt. Formal support can end at 18, while adult services are fragmented, under-resourced, and difficult to navigate. Mental health support is rarely connected to education, employment, housing, or social protection…
innovations.desc: Youngsters for the Future is innovative because it redefines social integration as both a practical and emotional process. The programme does not treat employment, education, housing and mental health as separate problems to be solved by separate services. Instead, it brings them together in one personalised pathway built around the real experience of young people leaving care. Its strongest innovation is the way mental health is embedded as a foundation for independence. Young people are not expected to become stable, employable or self-reliant while carrying untreated trauma, emotional distress, low trust or social isolation. The programme recognises that psychological safety, emotional regulation, self-confidence and healthy relationships are essential conditions for education, work and independent living. The model also introduces a prevention-to-care pathway. Young people can first…
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: In 2025, Youngsters for the Future / Tineri de Viitor delivered strong results across three levels: direct support for young people, strengthened capacity among professionals, and wider awareness of youth mental health. The programme reached 171 young people and provided a broad package of personalised support. Of these, 70 young people received psychological assessments and 31 entered individual therapy during the year. In total, the programme delivered 1,084 hours of psychotherapy and 275 psycho-emotional support sessions, offering young people consistent spaces to process distress, build…

innovations.name: ZINDR
innovations.problem: Zindr addresses the problem that decisions about marginalized groups are often made without their involvement, which can reinforce exclusion. It develops methods for inclusive knowledge co-creation and epistemic justice, so decisions become more grounded, effective, and fair. We believe that living and working together in a highly diverse world is essential to meeting today’s challenges, by creating spaces for equal collaboration, shared learning, and collective inquiry.
innovations.desc: Zindr is innovative in shifting from participation to the co-production of knowledge, where people affected by exclusion become co-researchers and co-designers of solutions. Learning is treated as a collective practice rather than an individual activity, grounded in epistemic justice as a design principle that redistributes whose knowledge counts. Instead of fixed methods, Zindr works through emergent, practice-based processes where “Zindr spaces” function as a living research and learning infrastructure. Building on safe and brave spaces, it introduces generative spaces where shared insight and collective agency can unfold.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: The main outcomes and benefits of Zindr can be summarized on three levels: 1. Better decisions and solutions By actively involving people with lived experience, insights become richer and more context-sensitive, leading to solutions that are more realistic, effective, and sustainable. 2. Redistribution of knowledge and power Zindr advances epistemic justice by recognizing and valuing the knowledge of people in situations of exclusion, making it meaningful in decision-making and design processes. 3. Stronger spaces for learning and agency It creates new forms of collective learning and…

innovations.name: DIDACTIC MINE OF YOUTH WORK
innovations.problem: Across Europe, many young people — particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds — transition from education to adulthood without adequate preparation for the demands of the modern labour market or civic life. Youth workers and educators, who are often the primary support system for these young people, frequently lack structured, accessible, and engaging resources to develop entrepreneurial thinking, social responsibility, and critical life skills in non-formal settings. At the same time, the growing urgency of sustainable development challenges requires a new generation capable of understanding complex systemic problems and contributing to collaborative solutions. Existing educational…
innovations.desc: The project addressed this gap through two complementary, practitioner-designed tools that make entrepreneurial and sustainability education tangible, engaging, and immediately usable. The e-book's 30 activities — each accompanied by a video presentation — are age-differentiated and ready to deploy in youth centres, classrooms, and non-formal settings without requiring specialised expertise. The interactive SDG game introduces a systems-thinking approach to social entrepreneurship, asking participants to forge connections between real-world problems and collaborative solutions, building competences such as strategic planning, communication, and teamwork in the process. Innovation lies in the integration of these two tools into a unified pedagogical framework that simultaneously targets individual skill development, organisational capacity building, and community-level impact — and does…

innovations.name: Smart Social Hub: Optimizing Community Support through Real-Time Matching
innovations.problem: The core problem addressed is the inefficiency and fragmentation of traditional social assistance in Vrancea, Romania. We identify three systemic barriers: Resource Mismatch and Waste: Currently, humanitarian aid is often ad-hoc and reactive. There is a lack of real-time data correlation between the specific, urgent needs of vulnerable families and the supplies provided by donors, leading to resource waste and gaps in coverage. Delayed Intervention: Bureaucratic hurdles and the absence of a unified digital tracking system prevent rapid responses to acute social crises, leaving marginalized individuals without support when they need it most. Lack of Transparency and Coordination: There is a…
innovations.desc:
Our project is inspired by the European 'Digital Social Services' frameworks and various community-based resource-sharing models implemented in countries like Denmark and the Netherlands (e.g., 'Social Tech' initiatives for local resilience). While we do not follow a specific single-organization project, we drew on the best practices of 'Digital Solidarity' networks that bridge the gap between public social services and private resources. We adapted these principles to the context of Vrancea, Romania, specifically by tailoring the workflow to fit the collaboration between the Local Social Assistance Directorate, private sector CSR sponsors, and our organization (Asociatia Smart Group Solutions).
Our innovation lies in the 'Smart Solidarity Network', a model that digitizes the social support chain to move from reactive charity to proactive, data-driven inclusion. Data-Driven Precision:…

innovations.name: Deep Inclusion: Unlocking Potential, growing Together in an Inclusive Society
innovations.problem: Every person is different. Disability is one of those differences, yet today it still too often leads to exclusion. People face barriers in all major domains of life. More than half (54%) report experiencing discrimination. Many also experience social isolation, with 44.2% reporting limited connectedness. Exclusion continues in education. Students with disabilities are twice as likely to leave school early, only 29% obtain a higher education degree. 6% of all children in Belgium are educated in segregated specialised settings. The situation is equally challenging in employment. Employment rates remain between 23% and 44%, people with disabilities face a 22% higher risk of poverty, and 38%…
innovations.desc: The Deep Inclusion Model addresses exclusion by focusing on both the individual and the environment. Inspired by years of experience in strengths-based practice, it equips people with cognitive support needs, their families, professionals and communities with the tools to recognize and build on strengths rather than limitations. What makes the model distinctive is that it translates inclusion into concrete, practices on both sides of the loop- what individuals develop and what environments actively enable. The model combines two complementary perspectives: Yes I Can, which supports individuals to develop confidence, skills and meaningful social roles, and Yes We Care, which helps families, schools, workplaces and support services create the conditions in which people can thrive. By strengthening both people and their environments, the model promotes a shift from care and protection…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: This model is grounded in more than a decade of practice across our programmes for young people with cognitive support needs. The Deep Inclusion Model builds directly on approaches that have already shown strong impact in real-life settings. We monitor around 300 participants annually, combining quantitative surveys, qualitative feedback and input from participants’ networks (family, peers, professionals). Our most mature impact data comes from Brake-Out, a three-year learning trajectory for young adults. We track development in the “yes I can” part: areas such as self-confidence, talent…

innovations.name: Talents in Action
innovations.problem: The increasing precariousness of the labour market, the difficulties young people face in accessing stable employment opportunities, the growing incidence of social and economic vulnerabilities, and the rising risk of isolation and disengagement all highlight the need for a profound rethinking of public policy approaches. In Tuscany the 13% of young people is NEETs and even though NEETs are not an omogenous group, researches agree that the main problem is to reach them in order to reactivate them in a training or job context. TALENTI IN AZIONE was designed to create and strenghten local network to identify NEETs and include them in a process of empowerment and training.
innovations.desc: In order to address the issue above, TALENTI IN AZIONE led to a perspective reversal in traditional approach: rather than expecting young people to adapt to the traditional modes of service delivery, policy instruments and support mechanisms must be redesigned around the target group's realities, taking into account their timing, languages, communication styles and the places they inhabit and frequent. Effective engagement is not associated with a single intervention; instead, it emerges from a combination of territorial proximity, educational relationships, clarity of the offer, personalised support, and a clear connection to tangible opportunities Breakthrough included: - building and strenghtening local networks of stakeholders (public services, municipalities, training agencies, cultural and youth associations, etc...); - focusing on innovative and active metodologies for training;…

innovations.name: AI Literacy & Future Skills Initiative
innovations.problem: AI is rapidly changing education, employment and civic life, but many people lack the skills and confidence to engage with it critically and productively. The World Economic Forum’s Future of Jobs Report 2025 highlights that employers expect almost 40% of workers’ core skills to change by 2030, making upskilling and reskilling a central challenge for the labour market. At the same time, the EU AI Act requires providers and deployers of AI systems to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff and other persons dealing with AI systems. This creates an urgent need for practical AI literacy beyond technical experts. Young people often use AI tools without understanding their…
innovations.desc:
The project is inspired by the AI Skills Coalition, a global initiative under AI for Good, coordinated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). The coalition brings together partners from across sectors to support inclusive AI skills development and help people build the competencies needed to participate in an AI-driven society and economy.
Young AI Leaders Linz adapts this broader approach to a regional and youth-led context in Austria, translating the AI skills agenda into practical AI literacy workshops, school formats, community programs and hands-on learning experiences for students, social organizations and non-technical audiences. Reference: https://aiforgood.itu.int/ai-skills-coalition/
The initiative uses a community-driven and youth-led model to make AI literacy accessible beyond traditional technical education. Instead of focusing only on coding or abstract…

Structural barriers, particularly within the vocational and technical education sector, translate into high rates of early school leaving, low financial literacy, and persistent exclusion from the labor market for young people from vulnerable backgrounds. Key data points that define the problem landscape: -Romania's youth unemployment rate is consistently 8 percentage points above the EU average. -Approximately 60,000 young people are active beneficiaries of the child protection system, and over 3,000 age out of institutional care every year with no preparation for independent adult life. -Only 1 in 70…
innovations.desc:
START MAJOR was originally conceived and funded by UniCredit Bank Romania as a financial literacy initiative targeting students in vocational and technical high schools. The first edition (2019–2020) was delivered by another NGO partner. From the second edition onward, Association The Social Incubator became the implementing partner, progressively expanding the program's scope. The original single-focus financial literacy model was developed into a three-module integrated curriculum: financial education (Module I), career and employability skills (Module II), and entrepreneurship camps (Module III).
START MAJOR 2025 addresses the above systemic gaps through a deliberately integrated, multi-layered, and experiential approach, one that operates at the intersection of formal education and non-formal learning. Module I – Financial Literacy (5,000+ participants | 90 live sessions)…

innovations.name: Engaging Youth in Digital Green Future 2.0 - GREENOVATE

Environmental debates are frequently communicated through institutional or technical language that is not accessible or engaging for youth audiences. At the same time, many schools and local communities still lack structured spaces where young people can connect digital communication skills with environmental literacy, advocacy, and civic participation. The challenge is even more visible in smaller communities and in the Western Balkans region,…

The original project was implemented within the youth and environmental sector through international cooperation between civil society organisations working on youth participation, sustainability, and digital engagement across Europe, including Western Balkan countries. The initial approach emerged during the post-pandemic period, when European societies were facing major social, economic, and environmental challenges connected to the green transition and the implementation of the European Green Deal. The project addressed the limited participation of young people in policy discussions and decision-making processes related to sustainability and climate action. innovations.name: The Museum of Abandonment
innovations.problem: The project addresses the long-term social consequences of child abandonment, institutionalisation, and the exclusion of vulnerable children from public memory. Despite affecting hundreds of thousands of children in Romania and across Europe, these experiences remain insufficiently documented, understood, and integrated into public awareness, education, and policymaking. The lack of recognition of this history contributes to stigma, social exclusion, and limited understanding of how institutional care impacts individuals, families, and communities across generations. The project also addresses the need for innovative ways to engage citizens, survivors, and decision-makers in conversations…
innovations.desc: The Museum of Abandonment is Romania's first fully digital and participatory museum and one of the few initiatives worldwide dedicated to documenting the history and legacy of child abandonment and institutional care. It combines a research hub, a digital archive of over 20,000 documents, participatory memory work, web and VR exhibitions, and immersive storytelling to transform collective memory into a tool for social inclusion and social change. Winner of the World Summit Awards 2025 (Culture & Heritage), the museum demonstrates how digital innovation can amplify marginalized voices, foster civic engagement, and address historical injustices.

For more than 36 years after the fall of communism, the experiences of hundreds of thousands of institutionalised children remained largely absent from public discourse, education, and collective memory. The project was created as a form of social mediation, helping society engage with a difficult and largely silenced history. innovations.name: VirIAto Assist
innovations.problem: The active population faces growing pressure to adapt to AI-driven workplace transformation, yet structured, accessible training remains scarce outside major urban centres. Many professionals fear job displacement but lack the tools or spaces to engage with AI constructively. Job seekers, in particular, are at risk of being left behind in a labour market that increasingly values AI competences. Meanwhile, higher education students enter professional life without practical AI skills aligned to real workplace needs. This skills gap is especially pronounced in regional cities like Viseu, where dedicated upskilling opportunities are limited.
innovations.desc: VirIAto Assist addresses this gap by delivering practical, context-adapted AI training directly within the institutions where the active population already operates — school clusters, employment centres, and universities. Rather than asking people to seek out training, the programme brings it to them. Sessions are co-designed with each partner institution to ensure immediate relevance, covering tools like generative AI assistants, prompt engineering for professional tasks, and responsible AI use. The volunteer-led, near-peer model keeps the tone accessible and non-intimidating, transforming AI from a threat into a practical ally.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Since its launch in 2026, VirIAto Assist has reached 180+ participants across 3 institutional partners in the Viseu district: a school cluster, the national employment and vocational training institute (IEFP), and a higher education institution. The programme has engaged a deliberately diverse active population — employed professionals, job seekers, and university students — demonstrating the model's adaptability across different professional contexts. All activity has been delivered at near-zero cost through volunteer commitment and institutional partnerships.

innovations.name: Educ'AI
innovations.problem: Students across Portugal are growing up in an AI-saturated environment without any structured preparation to understand, question or navigate it. AI literacy is largely absent from formal school curricula, leaving young people without the tools to critically engage with the technologies shaping their future. innovations.desc: Educ'AI addresses this gap through a modular, co-designed curriculum delivered by young near-peers — volunteers aged 18–30 who bring both technical knowledge and relatable proximity to students. Sessions are adapted to each school context and cover AI concepts, real-world applications, ethical dilemmas, and digital safety. The collaborative methodology — modular, interactive, and contextualised — ensures immediate relevance for participants and allows rapid adaptation across different school levels, from primary to post-secondary. Integration into the AI for Good (ITU/UN) network connects the programme to international standards and a global community of practice.

innovations.name: Vem D'AI
innovations.problem: Older adults in mid-sized Portuguese cities face significant barriers to participating in the digital transition. The rapid proliferation of AI tools — from voice assistants to generative content — has created an information gap that disproportionately affects seniors, increasing their vulnerability to disinformation, online fraud, and digital exclusion. At the same time, there is a lack of accessible, non-formal learning spaces where this population can engage with technology in a safe, supportive environment. Existing digital literacy programmes rarely address AI specifically, and even fewer are designed with and for senior communities at a local level.
innovations.desc: Vem D'AI addresses this gap through an intergenerational, peer-to-peer learning model: young volunteers aged 18–30 design and facilitate sessions specifically adapted to the cognitive rhythms, life experiences, and interests of older adults. The curriculum is structured progressively — from AI fundamentals and hands-on prompt engineering to more critical topics such as deepfakes, filter bubbles, and online privacy — and is iteratively refined based on participant feedback between seasons. The model is low-cost, volunteer-driven, and inherently scalable: it requires no specialised infrastructure, relies on community partnerships, and produces replicable pedagogical materials. Its integration into the global AI for Good (ITU/UN) network gives it international visibility and a framework for cross-border transfer.

innovations.problem: Romania has an estimated 80,000 people with visual impairments, including around 30,000 blind people. innovations.name: My Voice
innovations.problem: In a democracy, the average citizen has formal rights to influence decisions but rarely a real, practical channel to use them. Between elections every four years, people are left to participate passively or cynically while power concentrates in ever fewer hands – a gap that is widening as authoritarian and populist tendencies rise across Europe and trust in institutions falls. Referendums, the one direct tool available in Latvia, are rare, slow and expensive. Citizens want to solve concrete, everyday problems affecting their quality of life and public services, but individual concerns seldom translate into action, and those least connected to power are the least heard of all. There has been…
innovations.desc: Before ManaBalss (MyVoice), there was no everyday instrument to turn one person's idea into collective influence on the law. Our innovation is not the website but the binding bridge behind it: a legislated guarantee that any initiative reaching 10,000 signatures (0.5% of the population) must be formally reviewed by parliament. Unlike ordinary petition sites that collect signatures and hope someone listens, ManaBalss is wired directly into the lawmaking process – every qualifying idea is fact-checked, made legally sound, and then genuinely considered by elected officials. Just as important, it activates the large, normally passive majority: citizens willing to give just two minutes become a real political force, regardless of wealth, status or connections. The result is a fast, trusted, everyday alternative to referendums – and in moments of crisis, a democratic "first-aid kit".
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: In nearly 15 years ManaBalss has become an integral part of Latvian democracy. 118 citizen initiatives have won support in parliament and changed the laws – one of them the Constitution, the only known citizen-initiated constitutional change made through digital democracy anywhere in the world. Around one-third of Latvia's population are platform users and over two-thirds are readers – both world records for civic engagement. Many refugees experience language barriers, underemployment, limited access to labour market information and fragmented support systems. In Poland and Romania, existing services are often dispersed and sector-based, with no comprehensive, user-centred pathway guiding refugees and institutions through the integration process. There is a lack of structured, evidence-based guidance…

innovations.name: Entrepreneurial Mindset for Inclusion with the "Groupements de Createurs"
innovations.problem: The youth unemployment rate in France (15-24 years) reached 18% by the end of 2025, well above the average unemployment rate (7.7%), and is even higher for non-graduates (41% of young people who left initial training 1 to 4 years ago). Support measures exist, notably from Employment Service actors, but they fail to adequately address the insertion challenges faced by low- or unskilled youth, leading to precariousness, marginalization, mental and physical health deterioration, weakened social cohesion, and increased public spending. In the meantime, many young people, but also jobseekers of all ages, are interested in entrepreneurship. But they don't dare express it to the organisations…
innovations.desc: The "Groupement de Createurs" Network project uniquely addresses a key gap : supporting the emergence of entrepreneurial aspirations among people distant from the labour market. It transforms this desire into a powerful lever for inclusion—one overlooked by others. Employment inclusion actors focus on salaried jobs or training, while entrepreneurial support organisations target mature projects suited for business creation, skipping the upstream emergence phase. This proven approach boosts integration for hard-to-employ groups—mostly women and low-skilled youth—leveraging local stakeholders like the "Missions Locales" within the public employment network.

innovations.name: Lil’Ô – A Transferable Model for Regenerative and Inclusive Urban Transition
innovations.problem: European cities face intertwined crises: soil degradation, biodiversity loss, climate vulnerability and high unemployment in disadvantaged areas. Polluted urban brownfields often remain unused, reinforcing spatial inequalities. At the same time, vulnerable populations lack access to meaningful employment in the green transition. These challenges are rarely addressed together in a systemic way.
innovations.desc: Lil’Ô converts degraded land into fertile ecosystems using circular soil engineering (technosols made from local waste streams) combined with work-integration programmes. The site operates as a living laboratory, linking scientific research, ecological restoration and green job training. This integrated model aligns environmental regeneration with social inclusion and territorial revitalisation.

innovations.name: Stay Close
innovations.problem: When patients require intensive hospital care, distance often becomes an invisible but heavy burden. Informal caregivers and patients frequently face stress, exhaustion and financial pressure due to long travel times, lack of affordable accommodation near hospitals, and the uncertainty of finding a place to stay at short notice. This added strain affects wellbeing, care quality and recovery, and is insufficiently addressed by existing health and social care systems. Stay Close addresses this gap by turning proximity into a shared, community-based solution rather than an individual struggle.
innovations.desc: Stay Close is an innovative, digitally enabled care solution that transforms proximity from an individual challenge into a shared, systemic response. Through a dedicated digital platform and integrated communication flows, Stay Close enables safe matching, professional coordination and quality monitoring between hospitals, cities, host families, patients and informal caregivers. By embedding community-based solidarity into formal care pathways, Stay Close creates a scalable model that complements health systems and strengthens social infrastructure across regions and countries.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Stay Close delivers clear benefits at multiple levels. Patients and informal caregivers experience reduced stress, lower financial burden and improved wellbeing through reliable access to nearby accommodation. Hospitals benefit from improved patient and family experience, smoother care pathways and reduced non-medical pressure on care teams. Cities and communities gain a scalable model that activates local solidarity, strengthens social cohesion and embeds care proximity as part of a resilient social infrastructure.

innovations.problem: Families with experience of forced migration often live under conditions of prolonged stress, uncertainty and emotional overload, which affect family relationships, parenting roles, the well-being of children and adults, and their capacity to adapt to new social and institutional environments. Experiences of trauma, loss and disruption of previous life structures impact the family as a system, with difficulties faced by individual members reinforcing one another. At the same time, existing support systems are often fragmented, sector-based and focused on individual problems, which limits their effectiveness in working with the family as a whole. There is a lack of integrated, flexible and…

The programme combines biopsychosocial, systemic, resource-oriented and trauma-informed approaches into a single, coherent framework, addressing the complex and interrelated needs of families with experience of forced migration. The innovativeness of the solution also lies in its modular and flexible programme design, which allows support pathways to be tailored to the specific situations, resources and readiness of families. FAMILY integrates activities addressed to children, adults and families as a whole, avoiding the fragmentation typical of existing support systems. innovations.name: Torteltuin
innovations.problem: Amsterdam faces a severe housing crisis, with rising prices and speculative ownership putting secure, affordable homes out of reach for many residents. Traditional market-driven models fail to deliver long-term affordability or empower tenants, who often have little influence over how and where they live. In this context, a group of young Amsterdammers asked how they could live more sustainably, socially and affordably, without treating housing as an investment asset. They identified a gap for non-profit, resident-led housing that guarantees stable rents, community governance and environmentally responsible construction over the long term.
innovations.desc: De Torteltuin is a housing cooperative in development where residents collectively design, build and manage their future building on Centrumeiland, IJburg, in Amsterdam. The cooperative keeps ownership and decision-making in the hands of the resident community, ensuring development, use and management are not driven by profit. Homes will be let at fixed, low rents, protecting residents from market volatility and treating housing as a basic right rather than an investment object. The new building is planned as energy-neutral, climate-resilient and nature-inclusive, combining shared facilities, democratic governance and long-term social value for both residents and the surrounding neighbourhood.

At the same time, the rapid growth of wind and solar power demands smarter coordination between generation and consumption at regional level. Without new cooperative models, opportunities for local…
innovations.desc: Windunie is a cooperative developer and energy partner that connects landowners, citizen energy cooperatives, businesses and public actors to jointly develop wind and solar parks, battery storage and smart energy hubs with maximum local ownership. Acting from “idea to operation”, the organisation co‑invests in new systems, designs integrated wind‑and‑solar solutions, and supports partners throughout permitting, construction, management and power sales. Windunie pioneers local‑for‑local models in which generation and use are closely matched, combining technical optimisation with strong resident participation. The cooperative structure enables democratic decision‑making, long‑term collaboration and fair pricing for producers and off‑takers. By aiming structurally for at least 50% and ideally 90% local ownership, Windunie embeds energy assets in the community and aligns climate goals with…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: For over 20 years, Windunie and its members have been supplying sustainable electricity in the Netherlands and are involved in roughly half of all onshore wind projects. The cooperative now contributes to green power for around three million households, increasingly combining wind with solar generation and emerging storage solutions. Partners benefit from professional project management, reduced risks, and long‑term, reliable and fixed prices for both producers and energy users. Local communities gain structural revenue streams, strengthened citizen participation and visible ownership of the…

innovations.name: Leaders Gang
innovations.problem: The social problem addressed is the lack of, or barriers to, social mobility among young adults from vulnerable backgrounds. Our aim is to increase these young people’s employability and improve their transition into the labour market. Based on a study conducted for Edulog and presented in November 2021 on access to higher education and the transition to the labour market, it is possible to identify more precise data regarding the Portuguese context: First, access to higher education is not, in itself, a guarantee of equal opportunities or employability. Professor Alberto Amaral, one of Portugal’s leading experts in higher education, highlights, based on the study, that inequality in access…
innovations.desc: Leaders Gang provides an innovative, evidence-based solution that combines data-driven identification, real-world skills development, and peer-led impact to overcome barriers to social mobility. Its first innovation lies in how beneficiaries are identified. In partnership with public education authorities, the programme uses objective education data to identify young adults who demonstrated exceptional academic progress during secondary education despite socio-economic disadvantage. This approach moves beyond traditional merit-based or deficit-based selection models, ensuring fairness, precision, and transparency. The second innovation lies in the methodology. Instead of relying solely on classroom-based training, participants develop employability and leadership skills by facilitating workshops for younger students. This learning-by-teaching model positions beneficiaries as active…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Leaders Gang generates measurable benefits at individual, community and systemic levels. At the individual level, participants consistently demonstrate significant improvements in key 21st-century skills linked to employability, including communication, collaboration, critical thinking, leadership, resilience and self-efficacy. An external randomised control trial established a causal effect of the intervention in 2023, with statistically significant gains compared to a control group. Subsequent editions confirmed positive development across most of the 12 assessed competencies with high…

innovations.name: U-PLAYS - Ukrainian Participation in Language, Athletics, and Youth Support
innovations.problem: U-PLAYS addresses the social exclusion of Ukrainian youth displaced by the war, who face barriers to integration due to limited language skills, reduced employability, and restricted access to inclusive community activities.
innovations.desc:
U-PLAYS introduces an integrated, user-centered model that combines sport, language learning, and employment training into a single, coordinated pathway for youth integration. By delivering activities simultaneously across countries and actively involving participants in co-design, it ensures relevance, motivation, and measurable impact.
This initiative is born from a successful implementation of the project in the local context in Latvia and will now see its first scalability to a European context.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities
innovations.evidence: Key activities include (in each country respectively) 50 sports sessions to improve fitness and teamwork, 50 German, Latvian and Slovakian language classes to boost language proficiency, and 50 employment workshops to equip participants with job readiness skills. Implemented by professional trainers and language instructors, the project activities will be held conducted simultaneously in Austria, Latvia and Slovakia. Expected outcomes include improved physical fitness, better language skills, and increased employment prospects for participants. U-PLAYS adopts a user-centered approach,…

innovations.name: Harnessing the power of physical activity to sustainably recover from depression
innovations.problem:
It is estimated that 1 in 5 people in France will experience mental health issues at some point in their lives.
12.5% of French people aged 18-85 faced depression each year in 2021, a steep increase from 2017 figures (+3.7 pt). Depression disproportionately affects the most vulnerable members of society, namely women (15.6%), young adults (20.8%), unemployed individuals (22%) and people in precarious economic situations (18.8%). It not only reflects but also exacerbates pre-existing social disparities. (Source : Baromètre santé France 2021)
Beyond its emotional and psychological toll, depression significantly impacts daily functioning, overall well-being, and physical health. It often…
innovations.desc:
Je Bouge Pour Mon Moral (JBPMM) offers an innovative and complementary response to traditional mental health care by combining adapted physical activity with peer-to-peer social support. Free and accessible to all, the programme helps break social isolation and empowers participants to take an active role in their recovery.
The programme is delivered in cohorts of 10 to 12 participants, fostering group dynamics, mutual support and lasting social bonds. From enrolment, each participant benefits from individualised support, provided by a participant coordinator and a qualified Adapted Physical Activity trainer (APA), including an initial assessment to identify motivations, barriers and specific needs.
The core of the programme consists of 12 weeks of supervised physical activity, focused on Nordic walking—an accessible, nature-based activity with proven benefits for depression. Support is…
innovations.target: Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence:
This project aims to create sustainable and measurable improvements in mental health and overall well-being among adults living with depression and related conditions. It is designed to achieve the following tangible outcomes. In 2025, we measured the following impact:
- 50% reduction in depressive symptoms, as measured by scientific tools (PHQ-9, QIDS, BDI II), with sustained benefits 3 months post-program
- 17% increase in self-esteem, as participants experience personal achievements relying on their own resources (rather than medication), as measured with the Rosenberg self-esteem…

innovations.name: Performing Arts Festival - "Connectivity Technique"
innovations.problem: The numbers of young people who are NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) is rising. Many of these suffer from mental health problems such as lack of confidence, low self-esteem, poor communication skills and a lack of creativity. The challenge is to transform these young people  from "idle resources" to creative professionals through involvement in the different performing arts sectors managed by Dynamic Lab: Artistic and Performance Sector: NEETs can be included in professional training courses to become performers or choreographers, learning innovative contemporary and aerial dance techniques. Dynamic Lab has solid experience in turning passion into a career, thanks to…
innovations.desc:
At the Largo San Francesco 8/a location, the model has been expanded by integrating the "Creative & Cultural HUB". Here innovation has translated into the coordination of the board of the Culture Council (2021), transforming the residence into a strategic consultancy body for local cultural policies. At the headquarters in Via Principe Amedeo 106-110, the festival has adapted its offer by focusing on the production and organization of Theater and Dance courses specific to the province. Here the "Connectivity Technique" is actively applied, creating a center of attraction for emerging artists from the south-east of Bari. The adaptation of the model allowed Dynamic Lab to become the only winner of the Cross Border Open Innovation in the Performing Arts sector for the reference area.
Connectivity Technique: The use of a proprietary methodology based on improvisation and sensory perception…
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.evidence: Employability of NEETs: Transformation of inactive young people into qualified professionals in the fields of arts management, and in the production of dance and theater festivals for social inclusion. Young people can acquire skills in Euro-planning, Marketing and event management. Breaking down cultural isolation in cross-border areas through the creation of a permanent "cultural bridge".

innovations.name: Mobile Centres delivering integrated support in rural and underserved areas
innovations.problem:
Ukrainian refugees living in rural and underserved areas face compounded barriers to integration due to the absence or limited availability of essential services. Unlike urban settings, these areas often lack regular access to language courses, employment guidance, psychosocial support, childcare options, and community based integration activities. Geographic isolation, limited public transport, and fragmented local infrastructures further restrict participation in available support mechanisms.
Evidence from the project’s Needs Assessment indicates that refugees residing outside urban centres are significantly less likely to engage in learning or employment related activities, despite clear…
innovations.desc:
The Mobile Centres introduce a flexible, outreach based service delivery model designed to bring integrated support directly to rural and underserved areas where services are limited or unavailable. Rather than requiring refugees to travel long distances to access assistance, the Mobile Centres adapt the integrated hub model to local contexts by delivering services within accessible community spaces.
Mobile Centres operate through temporary setups in locations such as community halls, schools, municipal buildings, libraries, and other locally available venues. Trained facilitators and practitioners provide coordinated activities including language learning sessions, employment related guidance, psychosocial support, and community engagement initiatives. The services are delivered in a structured yet adaptable format, allowing responsiveness to local needs while maintaining consistent…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
For beneficiaries, the Mobile Centres significantly reduce geographical and logistical barriers to participation. Refugees gain access to learning and support opportunities close to where they live, lowering travel costs and time constraints while increasing sustained engagement. This contributes to improved language acquisition, greater confidence in navigating local systems, and enhanced psychosocial wellbeing.
For local communities, the Mobile Centres strengthen outreach capacity and foster inclusive local responses. By collaborating with municipalities, civil society organisations, and…

innovations.name: eDU Hubs and Mobile Centres, an integrated community based model for the long term integration of Ukrainian refugees
innovations.problem:
The eDU Hubs and Mobile Centres project addresses the structural gap between emergency humanitarian assistance and sustainable, long term integration of Ukrainian refugees within European host societies. While immediate responses have ensured safety and access to basic services, many refugees continue to face persistent barriers to social, economic, and psychosocial inclusion.
Evidence gathered through a cross country Needs Assessment conducted in Germany, Romania, and Slovakia shows that language barriers significantly limit access to employment, education, and public services. Despite high levels of educational attainment, many refugees experience unemployment or underemployment due to…
innovations.desc:
The eDU Hubs and Mobile Centres model introduces an integrated, community based approach to refugee integration that combines fixed hubs with mobile service delivery. The innovation lies in the coordination of multiple support dimensions into a single, accessible ecosystem rather than in the creation of isolated services.
Fixed eDU Hubs serve as trusted entry points within local communities, while Mobile Centres extend outreach to underserved and rural areas. Through this dual structure, the model ensures continuity of support regardless of geographical context. Services include language learning, employment guidance, psychosocial support, childcare facilitation, and community engagement, designed to function as interdependent components rather than standalone interventions.
The model is grounded in a Theory of Change that links identified needs to expected outcomes at individual,…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
At beneficiary level, the model improves access to coordinated integration pathways, reducing fragmentation and lowering barriers to participation. Refugees benefit from personalised support that strengthens employability, social participation, and psychosocial wellbeing.
At community level, the project enhances cooperation between civil society organisations, public authorities, employers, and educational actors. This contributes to improved service coordination, increased intercultural interaction, and stronger social cohesion.
At system level, the project generates transferable knowledge…

innovations.name: Crowdbuilding
innovations.problem:
The Netherlands is in a housing crisis. Housing construction needs to be radically transformed: more sustainable, more social, and more affordable. Collective self-build offers people the opportunity to create their own living environment together with others, with more say in the design, construction, and ultimate use. There are also advantages for municipalities, as it means greater support, participation, social innovation, and social cohesion. Building and living together creates resilient residential communities that contribute to the local community by caring for each other and their surroundings. What if 10% of the homes that need to be built, could be realized this way?
To get…
innovations.desc:
For residents , CrowdBuilding is the ideal starting point for building and living together. At Crowdbuilding.com, everyone dreaming of shared housing can find information and inspiration, start or join a group, connect with each other, register for plots, and much more. Together, we are building a fair and sustainable housing system where collective self-build is a viable option.
Construction groups, housing cooperatives, and self-builders are essential for good professional support. That's why CrowdBuilding is building a national network of partners who can offer quality, experience, and reliability. With a network of dedicated process facilitators, creative architects, smart consultants, and expert contractors , we can tackle the housing crisis in the Netherlands in an innovative and high-quality way.
As an expert in collective housing, CrowdBuilding is also the ideal partner for…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
In the last two years multiple housing projects have been built, others are still in the proces of planning or building; projects vary from eco-villages, tiny houses and redesigning old officebuildings into compact cityhouses for the elderly or the young.
Already two provinces and three municipalities are working as partners and the movement is rapidly expanding.
Eighty partners (procesmanagers, acrhitects, builders) take part in the expert network.
The online platform offers education through e-learnings, events and storytelling, tools (step-by-step planning) and matchmaking where residents…

innovations.name: Volunteers Everywhere
innovations.problem: Many refugees from Ukraine face social isolation, language and cultural barriers, and lack access to community-based support. At the same time, volunteer engagement is fragmented and lacks common standards, tools, and coordination.
innovations.desc:
VolEVer uses a mobile app and shared standards to organise volunteer–refugee matching in a clear and safe way, making it easier to expand the model to new places without losing quality.
The project builds on OPU’s previous digital volunteer registry (idobrovolnik.cz), but has been significantly adapted to introduce a mobile app, unified training, and cross-border coordination.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Key results include a mobile app that safely matches volunteers with refugees, a shared methodology and training package, and improved coordination across countries. Benefits include more accessible support for refugees, better-prepared volunteers, higher programme quality, and easier scaling of community-based activities.

innovations.name: SkillsPath - SKILLs and Innovation for Youth Employment PATHways
innovations.problem: Europe’s work landscape is rapidly changing due to digitalisation, decarbonisation, demographic shifts, and migration. While unemployment rates are at a historic low of 5.9%, these forces are driving increased demand in sectors and occupations already facing shortages or likely to do so in the future. This requires continuous updates of skill profiles and training to ensure the labour force can meet the demands of the future (ESDE, 2023). At the same time, inequality increases as marginalised youth, migrants and women continue to experience barriers to participation in the workforce. In 2022, 11.7% of 15-29-year-olds in the EU were NEETs, with Germany at a low 8.6% and Greece and Spain at…
innovations.desc: SkillsPath directly addresses the outcomes outlined in the CfP as it aims to (a) increase the participation of refugee and migrant youth in employment or training including in the green industry, (b) transfer/adopt practices that have been successful in other contexts and foster mutual collaboration, (c) enhance awareness and adoption of innovative approaches to skills assessment and skills development through capacity strengthening and dissemination, and (d) improve economic integration by bridging the skills gap.
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.benef: International Rescue Committee IRC Deutschland gGmbH
innovations.evidence: 140 youth will receive individualised support and at least 50% out of them will achieve significant career or education milestones, such as job placement, enrolment in apprenticeship/internship, occupational skills training; and 30% out of them will be employed or in training relevant to the green industry. Further, 80% of employment services providers’ staff, including project staff using the AI skills assessment tool report improved career services and ability to align refugee and migrant youth skills with occupations; and 50% of local and national stakeholders participating in…
authors: International Rescue Committee IRC Deutschland gGmbH

innovations.name: Women and Community Resilience through Inclusive Skills Development
innovations.problem: Vulnerable women, displaced families and marginalised communities face long-term unemployment, social exclusion, limited access to training, and psychosocial stress. Traditional services often fail to reach them due to language barriers, low digital literacy, stigma and lack of community-based delivery models.
innovations.desc:
The project introduces a community-embedded, low-threshold training model that integrates employability skills, life skills and psychosocial support. It uses peer learning, volunteer professionals, culturally adapted content and safe community spaces to remove access barriers and create sustainable social inclusion pathways.
The innovation has been adapted and implemented in different local contexts, including community-based initiatives in the Netherlands and preparatory implementation in Middle Eastern contexts addressing displacement-affected communities. While maintaining the core model of inclusive, low-threshold skills development combined with psychosocial and social inclusion support, the project has been locally adapted to respond to language, cultural and socio-economic needs of each target group. Adaptations include culturally tailored training content, flexible delivery…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence:
Over the past period, our volunteers have already provided hairdressing training to around 30 women through informal community sessions. These activities focused not only on practical hairdressing skills, but also on confidence, social connection and feeling more at home in Dutch society.
In addition, Stichting DOING organised several integration and employability workshops under the initiative “Bridging Cultures Together: A Collaborative Integration Project”, in cooperation with Maat for Peace, Development and Human Rights. Through these workshops we supported refugees with understanding…

innovations.name: The Room for Mental Power
innovations.problem: Young adults in the Netherlands face growing mental health challenges, with around one in three experiencing psychological problems, while existing support is often fragmented, difficult to access and poorly aligned with their daily lives. Help frequently arrives late, focuses mainly on symptoms rather than underlying causes and is limited by rigid rules, siloed funding and lack of regional coordination. Many promising local initiatives struggle to scale or sustain their work because they run up against institutional barriers and short-term project financing. As a result, young adults aged 16–35 risk not receiving timely, appropriate and affordable support to stay mentally healthy, recover…
innovations.desc: Ruimte voor Geestkracht is a long-term national programme of FNO that works for ten years with young adults, regional networks and national stakeholders to create a society in which young adults have space to be and remain mentally healthy. The programme combines regional collaboration in five areas with strong youth participation, ensuring that young adults do not just give feedback but actively co-decide on priorities and solutions. Through Team Geestkracht, a dedicated youth panel, young adults advise, set agendas and support regions in organising meaningful youth involvement. Ruimte voor Geestkracht focuses on reshaping rules, systems and financial flows, looking beyond healthcare alone to address root causes of mental health problems and build sustainable, integrated support structures.
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Ruimte voor Geestkracht strengthens regional networks that work on mental health in ways that genuinely fit young people’s lives, improving the quality, accessibility and affordability of support for those who need it. Young adults become co-owners of the programme, ensuring that their perspectives shape decisions, interventions and long-term system change rather than being treated as an afterthought. Valuable local initiatives gain support to overcome barriers such as fragmented rules or insecure funding, increasing their capacity to continue and grow. By targeting underlying causes and…

innovations.name: Prins Heerlijk
innovations.problem: Prins Heerlijk responds to the limited labour market perspectives of young people with serious learning difficulties or a disability, who often leave school without a qualification and struggle to find and keep meaningful work. Many of them experience low self-confidence, social isolation and a lack of opportunities to develop practical skills in real work environments. At the same time, employers in horeca, retail and care face shortages of motivated, well-prepared staff, while social support systems are not always equipped to provide integrated learning, work and living trajectories. This situation risks long-term dependence on benefits and reduced participation in society for these young…
innovations.desc: Prins Heerlijk is a social enterprise that combines education, work-based learning and tailored support in its own training companies in hospitality and retail, complemented by placements with partner employers in care and service sectors. Young people aged roughly 16–27 learn a profession while working in real restaurants, shops and service locations, supported by professional coaches who focus on development, autonomy, responsibility and wellbeing at the individual’s own pace. In cooperation with VET providers such as De Rooi Pannen and ROC Tilburg, participants can obtain an MBO diploma, increasing their chances of sustainable employment. For those who need more intensive support, Prins Heerlijk offers additional guidance and the option of assisted living in its own housing facilities, ensuring an integrated trajectory from learning to living and working.
innovations.target: NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Prins Heerlijk enables young people with learning difficulties or a disability to grow into confident service staff in hospitality, retail and care, often obtaining recognised qualifications and securing lasting jobs. Participants report increased self-esteem, independence and pride in their work, while families and professionals observe greater social participation and stability. Employers gain motivated, well-prepared employees and benefit from ongoing collaboration with a specialised partner that understands both educational and workplace requirements. The organisation has received several…

innovations.name: Herenboeren
innovations.problem: In many Dutch regions, citizens feel disconnected from how their food is produced and how nearby land is managed. Industrial food chains often prioritise efficiency over soil health, animal welfare and biodiversity, while leaving consumers with little influence over production choices. Households seeking seasonal, local food with a smaller ecological footprint frequently lack accessible, affordable options. At the same time, there are few inclusive community spaces where residents can learn about sustainable agriculture, meet farmers and involve children in nature-based activities. Farmers themselves face pressure to remain economically viable while transitioning to more sustainable…
innovations.desc: Herenboeren introduces a cooperative, citizen-owned farm model in which around 250 households jointly establish and govern their own “Herenboerderij”. Each household makes a one-off investment of approximately €2,000–€2,500 and pays a monthly fee of about €45–€80 per person, depending on location and meat consumption. In return, members receive a weekly share of seasonal vegetables, fruit, eggs and, for those who wish, occasional meat from their own farm. Professional farmers are employed as agrarian managers with a stable income, ensuring high-quality, nature-driven production. Members can voluntarily help on the land or join working groups, strengthening skills and shared ownership. This model reconnects people with food production while creating a transparent, fair and resilient local food system.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: There are already 23 operational Herenboerderijen across the Netherlands, with dozens more in development and more than 9,000 citizens involved as cooperative members. Participating households regain control over their food supply and enjoy fresh, seasonal produce grown on land close to home. Nature-driven farming practices improve soil health, support biodiversity and ensure better living conditions for animals, contributing to a more future-proof food system. The farms function as lively community hubs, hosting open days, guided tours and activities for children such as treasure hunts,…

innovations.name: Stadskamer Achterhoek
innovations.problem: Many people in the Achterhoek experience “colour loss” in their lives after disruptive events such as mental health challenges, social isolation, or other life crises.
