Traditional care systems often focus on diagnoses and protocols rather than on people’s own pace, strengths, and recovery journeys, which can make support feel conditional and distant. Long waiting lists in mental health care further delay access to meaningful activities and peer connection, deepening loneliness and passivity. There is a clear need for accessible, non-stigmatising environments where people of all ages can participate, recover socially, and regain a sense of belonging without having to fit rigid care-system…
innovations.desc: Stadskamer creates welcoming, recovery-oriented spaces across thirteen lively support points in the Achterhoek where everyone is invited to “just be”, participate, and work on personal recovery. The organisation uses the “Route van de Vraag” to start from each participant’s own question, wishes, and rhythm, instead of predefined trajectories. A broad “waaier van mogelijkheden” of activities—developed directly from participants’ needs—offers accessible recovery pathways that quickly connect people to suitable programmes. People can join as participants, volunteers, team members, local entrepreneurs, or care initiatives, making Stadskamer both a community hub and a driver of more human-centred care.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Stadskamer has grown into thirteen vibrant local hubs where young and old can participate, feel welcome, and work on recovery in their own way. This low-threshold offer enables people to quickly access meaningful activities and peer support, contributing to shorter mental health care waiting times. Participants regain confidence, structure, and social connections, which brings “more colour” back into their lives. At the same time, the initiative mobilises volunteers, professionals, and local partners around positive health, shared recovery, and social inclusion, strengthening the wider…

innovations.name: Sociëteit Tof
innovations.problem: Seniors with prior high socio-economic status, broad education, or cultural interests often experience memory issues or isolation, feeling out of place in standard day care settings. These individuals, living independently, require active daily structure to maintain skills, prevent decline, and relieve family caregivers, yet conventional programs fail to match their backgrounds, leading to disengagement and lost societal contributions. This gap distances them from meaningful participation, exacerbating vulnerability in later life.
innovations.desc: Sociëteit Tof, hosted by Proteion in Roermond's Retroscoop, provides specialized day activities from Monday to Friday for self-reliant seniors with distinguished backgrounds. Tailored to education, career history, and interests, offerings include discussions, (art) painting, reading, classical music, chess, lectures, museum visits, and library trips, led by facilitators ensuring inclusive dialogue. A shared warm lunch enhances community, offering an upscale alternative to regular day care while supporting skill preservation.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Participants feel valued and heard, engaging in stimulating conversations that boost confidence and role fulfillment. Families gain respite as seniors maintain autonomy through culturally resonant activities that sustain cognitive and social skills. The model promotes well-being for educated elderly, fostering connections and purpose without stigmatizing care environments.

innovations.name: Dynamisch Op Weg
innovations.problem: Many people in the Netherlands face significant barriers to entering or returning to the labour market, including limited work experience, uncertainty about their abilities, and a lack of supportive, low-threshold opportunities to start. Standard recruitment and employment pathways often demand immediate productivity and full clarity about job fit, which can deter those who are unsure, anxious, or have been out of work for longer periods. As a result, people who could thrive with the right guidance and gradual onboarding remain side-lined, missing chances to develop skills, confidence, and sustainable work perspectives.
innovations.desc: Dynamisch op Weg tackles these barriers by offering a highly accessible entry route into work, where people can quickly sign up and even test a working day before committing. This trial option lowers psychological and practical thresholds, allowing candidates to explore whether the work suits their interests, capacities, and personal situation. The organisation positions itself as a supportive team environment, signalling that newcomers “fit perfectly” and will not be left alone in figuring things out. This client-friendly, stepwise approach makes work-based learning and reintegration more attractive and realistic for those who need security and experimentation before taking the next step.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence: By enabling people to try out a working day, Dynamisch op Weg helps participants make informed choices about their future job, reducing mismatches and early drop-out. Candidates gain a concrete, experience-based understanding of tasks, team culture, and expectations, which builds confidence and motivation. The organisation simultaneously identifies who is likely to succeed with further support, increasing the effectiveness of its onboarding and guidance. This mutual clarity benefits both participants and the employer, fostering more sustainable placements and better prospects for continued…

innovations.name: Campus Woudhuis
innovations.problem: Many people who receive care or guidance from institutions struggle to find or keep regular paid work, despite having talents and motivation to contribute. They are often seen primarily as “clients” instead of colleagues, which limits their opportunities for development, autonomy, and participation in society. At the same time, employers experience a gap between their ambition for social responsibility and concrete ways to involve people with support needs in their teams. This leads to underused labour potential, persistent exclusion from the labour market, and a missed opportunity to build more diverse, socially cohesive workplaces in and around Apeldoorn.
innovations.desc: Campus Woudhuis operates as a green work–learn company and living lab for inclusive entrepreneurship on the Woudhuis estate near Apeldoorn. The campus offers practical work in nature management, hospitality, activities on the estate, and projects with nearby employers (“common grounds”), combined with coaching and learning trajectories. People who find it difficult to access regular work are hired through open hiring: everyone who can and wants to contribute is welcome, without heavy selection procedures or stigmatising labels. Partners IVN, Natuurmonumenten, ’s Heeren Loo and De Onderwijsspecialisten jointly run the cooperative estate and knowledge centre, connecting care, education, nature organisations and employers around one inclusive workplace.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: On Campus Woudhuis, around 35 people with very diverse backgrounds work together on meaningful tasks, ranging from nature management and hospitality to research and learning projects. Participants “bloom” by doing what they enjoy, discovering talents, gaining work experience, and increasingly co-deciding on the future of the campus. The environment deliberately avoids the word “client”, which strengthens equality, pride, and ownership among workers. Employers on and around the estate benefit from motivated staff, higher job satisfaction in teams, and a more diverse workforce that reduces the…

innovations.name: Buurtbaan
innovations.problem: In Amsterdam's diverse neighborhoods like West and Zuidoost, sleutelpersonen—local key figures with deep community ties—lack formal recognition and paid opportunities despite their vital role in fostering connections and inspiration. These individuals, often distant from the labor market due to limited formal qualifications, face barriers to sustainable employment, hindering neighborhood resilience and bottom-up development. Traditional structures overlook their experiential knowledge, resulting in fragmented community building and missed chances for in-streaming talent into professional roles.
innovations.desc: Buurtbaan transforms voluntary sleutelpersonen into paid community builders through a 2-year program of 25 jobs, providing coaching, training, and recognition aligned with municipal regulations since 2021. Launched in Amsterdam West in 2017, it emphasizes neighborhood strengthening from within—reaching and inspiring residents without relegating participants to assistant tasks. Flexible models like subsidies atop benefits, ZZP entrepreneurship, or full buurtwerker roles empower participants to lead with their strengths, fostering peer-to-peer training and ambassadorship for scalability.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence: Participants gain profound recognition, perspective, and career advancement, with many aspiring to become ambassadors and trainers for future buurtbaners. Neighborhoods benefit from sustainable "layer-upon-layer" strengthening, enhancing connections between residents and organizations while promoting in- and through-flow of local talent. Shared intervision reveals broad support for the model, delivering dual impact: personal development for sleutelpersonen and resilient, resident-led community building.

innovations.name: NO-STRESS
innovations.problem: In 2019, there were over 3 million accidents at work, often due to accidental events and human error. Psychologists attribute the causes of these phenomena to stress and fatigue, which manifest themselves both mentally and physically and derive from productive tasks and work environments. Even when stress does not cause accidents, it can still have repercussions on workers' health and social lives. In the literature, the physical, physiological and psychological aspects of stress have already been studied through the analysis of biometric data, but they have never been integrated with neurophysiological and psychological data. The NO-STRESS Manufacturing project, therefore, aimed to develop…
innovations.desc: The NO-STRESS Manufacturing project has proposed a system that integrates different and complementary technologies, such as exoskeletons, voice assistance and non-invasive biomedical devices. This solution allows real-time monitoring of data relating to physical effort, psychological workload, through the verbal administration of questionnaires, and the physiological parameters of workers in real industrial contexts. The combination of these data is essential for analysing the causes of work-related stress and mitigating its intensity, providing reliable evidence for redesigning the work environment in order to improve the well-being of workers.
innovations.target: Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: The NO-STRESS Manufacturing project merged already tested technologies for biometric measures with already commercialised tools for physical and vocal assistance aimed at studying cognitive load and stress in workplaces. This implies developing a platform-based monitoring system with tools aimed at workers’ well-being. Over time, the technology integration performed by this project would imply personalising types of workers and tasks, up to aiding the design of collaborative or digital technologies in Manufacturing. Companies will get healthier working contexts, increased workers’ well-being,…

innovations.name: Wender – Empowering vulnerable people through shelter and reintegration
innovations.problem: Many individuals in the Netherlands, including youth, elderly, women, men, and families, face severe barriers to stable living and employment. Issues such as homelessness, addiction, mental health challenges, debts, and domestic violence create complex, intertwined problems that distance people from the labor market. Traditional support systems often fail to provide the integrated shelter, housing assistance, and ambulatory care needed to restore self-reliance, leaving vulnerable groups trapped in cycles of instability without pathways to sustainable jobs or training.​
innovations.desc:
Wender, as a unified organization, started operating under its current name in 2021. It emerged from the collaboration between Het Kopland and Zienn, with the name change announced in April 2021 and full legal merger completed by January 2023. The foundational work traces back further through its predecessor organizations.
Wender addresses these challenges through a client-centered approach that combines safe shelter, housing support, and personalized guidance to empower individuals toward autonomy. Operating in Friesland, Groningen, and Drenthe, the organization fosters resilience by helping clients regain control over their lives, tackling root causes like addiction and debt holistically. This method emphasizes collaboration with partners and networks, including Valente and regional chains for domestic violence and youth homelessness, to deliver tailored interventions beyond…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Wender's interventions enable clients to achieve a "positive turning point," securing safe, independent living and enhanced self-sufficiency. By strengthening personal agency, the approach supports long-term stability for those with multifaceted issues, reducing reliance on emergency services. Clients gain practical skills for daily life management, while partnerships amplify societal benefits, creating stronger community outcomes through bundled efforts with local organizations.​

innovations.name: Butterfly Effect
innovations.problem: Social isolation and fragmented community ties plague care locations in the Netherlands, where shortages of volunteers and housing exacerbate disconnection between residents with and without care needs. Traditional models struggle to integrate diverse talents, leaving gaps in mutual support and equal participation. This hinders well-being, safety, and natural human connections, particularly amid volunteer deficits and housing pressures, distancing vulnerable groups from active societal roles.
innovations.desc: Butterfly Effect deploys dedicated neighborhood connectors—local volunteers—who actively link residents, harnessing individual talents to build inclusive, buzzing communities. Collaborating with housing corporations and care organizations, it creates spaces where everyone contributes equally, blending care with everyday life. This social enterprise model promotes sustainable volunteer engagement, turning care sites into dynamic hubs of connection and shared responsibility.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Neighborhood connectors enhance resident well-being, safety, and belonging, as participants report stronger community bonds and genuine contributions to neighbors' lives. Testimonials highlight improved cohesion, with care woven into daily interactions, addressing volunteer shortages effectively. The approach yields societal gains through empowered locals driving vitality, proving scalable for broader social impact.

innovations.name: Broodje Aap & Linke Soep
innovations.problem: Newcomers and status holders in Tilburg face significant hurdles integrating into Dutch society, including language barriers, limited social networks, and distance from the labor market. Many struggle with practical participation, lacking opportunities to practice Dutch, gain work experience, or build connections essential for employment. Traditional integration paths often overlook hands-on, community-based approaches, leaving refugees and migrants with migration backgrounds isolated and without pathways to sustainable jobs or volunteering.
innovations.desc: Broodje Aap & Linke Soep creates an intercultural kitchen in Tilburg-West as a meeting place where newcomers cook lunches and catering alongside locals and volunteers. Programs like "Meedoen in de taalrijke keuken" and "Leren en werken in de horeca" offer language practice, horeca training, excursions, stages, and future planning, fostering societal participation. This social enterprise promotes cultural exchange and zero-waste principles through collaborative meal preparation and delivery.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence: Participants gain confidence, Dutch proficiency, horeca work experience, and new social networks, enabling steps toward paid work or volunteering. The initiative facilitates hundreds of global encounters via Tilburg4Global Goals, strengthens community ties in Tilburg-West with partners like De Reinevaer, and supports status holder inburgering as a Menss-partner. Intercultural meals enhance mutual understanding and practical societal inclusion.

innovations.name: Bovengrondse Vakschool
innovations.problem: In Heerlen-Noord, residents face significant barriers to employment, education, and well-being, with limited opportunities exacerbating social exclusion and economic stagnation. People distant from the labor market—such as long-term unemployed, single parents, and those needing skill development—struggle amid fragmented support systems that fail to connect training with real job needs. Traditional approaches often overlook personal growth, basic worker skills like punctuality and teamwork, and community integration, leaving individuals without sustainable pathways to work and trapping the region in cycles of low cohesion.
innovations.desc: The Bovengrondse Vakschool creates a collaborative platform uniting employers, education, government, and civil society to tailor training to candidates' strengths and employers' basic requirements. Offering practical programs in nine work spheres across vakwerk (green, technical, construction), dienstwerk (logistics, ICT, hospitality), and zorgwerk (horeca, cleaning, care), it emphasizes personal development alongside vocational skills. Community initiatives like bike repair donations via Stichting Leergeld and ANWB, plus intergenerational activities such as the naaiclub, build social bonds while aligning with circular reuse principles through repair and upcycling projects.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence: Participants gain employability, confidence, and social connections, as seen in stories like Dieudonnee Gans, who transitioned from isolation to bike repair work and aspirations in technical roles. The school boosts local cohesion via green maintenance, bike donations to underprivileged children, and community events reducing loneliness. Employers benefit from pre-vetted talent, while the region sees economic uplift through sustained job placements and strengthened networks, creating meaningful work that values personal growth over perfect vacancy matches.

innovations.name: Boefjes en Barista’s
innovations.problem:
Across Europe, both older adults and young parents often experience major life transitions that affect their social networks. Although their circumstances differ, both groups may find that the social connections that once supported them no longer fully match their needs.
At the same time, natural meeting places are disappearing from neighbourhoods and generations increasingly live separate lives. As a result, many people lack opportunities to build new relationships, experience belonging and find informal support within their community. In essence, many people no longer have the “village” they need. Rather than focusing solely on reducing loneliness, Boefjes en Barista’s creates the…
innovations.desc:
Boefjes en Barista’s is a community-based social intervention that transforms care homes into vibrant neighbourhood community spaces where older adults, parents and young children (0-4 years) meet, connect and become part of each other's lives.
“Boefjes” is a Dutch affectionate term for someone who is playful, curious and young at heart. In Boefjes en Barista’s, the “Boefjes” are not only the children. We believe that nobody is ever too old to play. Through play, laughter and shared experiences, older adults and young children bring out the playful side in one another and discover that the child within us never truly disappears. The “Barista’s” represent the welcoming coffee bar at the heart of the intervention. Together, playfulness and hospitality create a warm environment where meaningful relationships and a sense of belonging can grow across generations.
A “Bakkie” is a Dutch…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: Boefjes en Barista’s strengthens social connectedness by helping participants build new relationships, expand their social networks and experience a stronger sense of belonging. Participants get to know one another through repeated encounters, develop meaningful relationships and increasingly become part of a community in which they feel welcome, valued and recognised. The intervention also encourages reciprocity: participants both give and receive support, attention and friendship. Over time, informal support networks emerge naturally. Participants continue to meet outside the gatherings,…

innovations.name: Accessible Neighborhoods, Empowered Consumers
innovations.problem: Blind and visually impaired individuals faced significant barriers when accessing goods, services, and digital information. Businesses were often unprepared to interact effectively with blind customers, resulting in exclusion, reduced independence, and obstacles to community participation. Digital environments were frequently inaccessible, limiting access to essential information and online services.
innovations.desc: The project used role-reversal experiential learning, designed and facilitated by blind professionals. Participants engaged in hands-on activities that allowed them to understand the lived experience of blindness and challenge stereotypes.A blind developer led the digital accessibility component, offering practical tools for immediate improvement.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization
innovations.evidence: The completed project achieved: – Training of at least 100 people in physical shops – Training of over 150 participants through online webinars – Increased awareness and reduced stereotypes regarding blindness – Improved accessibility in neighbourhood shops – Enhanced digital accessibility for local small businesses – Stronger autonomy and independence for blind residents – Ripple effect: participants shared the experience with peers, families, and colleagues

innovations.name: Elliz in Company
innovations.problem: Elliz in Company aims to guide individuals to participation by creating a safe and welcoming environment first. We help people regain confidence, discover talents, and develop new skills at their own pace. Our ultimate goal is to empower them to become self-reliant and find meaningful work that suits their abilities and aspirations. It’s not just about making products—it’s about helping people grow and reclaim their place in society.
innovations.desc:
Elliz in Company is innovative because it transforms traditional reintegration into a human-centered, empowering experience.
Peer contact as a foundation : Elliz creates a warm, informal environment where participants connect at eye level. The “coffeetable” culture and collaborative workshops foster trust, mutual learning, and solidarity—people learn from and support each other instead of being treated as cases.
Freedom and autonomy : Participants set their own pace and choose activities that match their interests and talents, from textile crafts to technical work. This freedom builds confidence and ownership, making reintegration a personal journey rather than a rigid program.
Focus on well-being and meaningful work : Elliz prioritizes emotional safety and personal growth before productivity. Through the process of “ontdooien, ontplooien, zelf rooien,” individuals regain self-worth and…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Elliz in Company has supported hundreds of individuals in regaining confidence, discovering talents, and moving toward meaningful work. Participants report improved well-being, stronger social connections, and reduced isolation. Our approach leads to measurable outcomes: increased self-reliance and successful transitions to employment or education. Society benefits through reduced stigma and greater participation.

innovations.name: Binnenwerk
innovations.problem:
Standard jobs may not always fit these employees, for example because they are deemed to be too slow for the regular workpace or need extra instruction. Given the situation these employees are in, they also have specific needs from an employer.
Employers aren’t always equipped to provide this and may lack an incentive to put in the hard work, when there are other potential future employees available without such needs.
innovations.desc:
Binnenwerk collaborates with national and local governmental organisations to create sustainable, stable jobs for the target group. New jobs are created around work that needs to be done and the threshold to take up one of these jobs is lowered.
During their employment, Binnenwerk invests in the learning and long term development of their employees. They do so via trainings, coaching and support to get the appropriate licensings. And Binnenwerk offers clear answers to help the employees navigate in the complex situation they are (regarding regulations and labour laws). Thus helping them make choices and oversee consequences.
Employees can get a contract for indefinitely or could continue to another job if that is a better fit.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Sylvo Thijsen, director of Staatsbosbeheer (one of the main partners) "Research shows that Binnenwerkers are happy with their jobs; they do meaningful work, feel valued, and are simultaneously working on their own personal development." Over 1,000 jobs have now been created in archive work, property-related tasks, clearing personnel files, or forest and nature management.

innovations.name: The Day Centre for the Elderly in Novska
innovations.problem: The project addresses the growing challenges of population ageing, social isolation, and limited access to community-based care services for older people in the Novska region. Many elderly individuals face the risk of institutionalisation due to insufficient support in the community, lack of organised daily activities, and inadequate social and psychosocial assistance, which negatively affects their well-being and quality of life.
innovations.desc: The project introduces a community-based care model that allows older people to remain in their own homes while accessing comprehensive, organised support through a day centre. By combining personalised psychosocial assistance, structured activities, medical supervision, meals, and safe transport, the centre offers an integrated alternative to institutional care, reducing isolation and promoting active, dignified ageing within the local community.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.benef: Development Agency of the City of Novska – NORA
innovations.evidence: The project established a fully equipped Day Centre providing half-day and full-day services to 20 regular users and reaching more than 70 older persons through additional activities. It improved access to community-based care, reduced social isolation, and prevented unnecessary institutionalisation. Users benefit from personalised support, social and cultural activities, medical supervision, nutritious meals, and safe transportation. The centre also created new jobs, strengthened local cooperation among social services, and contributed to a more inclusive and resilient community. Overall,…
authors: Development Agency of the City of Novska – NORA

innovations.name: proBUDI VJEŠTinu
innovations.problem: Before the project “proBUDI VJEŠTinu”, the local community in Novska faced several interconnected challenges: a lack of social enterprises and limited opportunities for sustainable job creation, particularly for vulnerable groups; a high volume of bulky waste such as old furniture and textile products ending up in landfills; and very few services focused on repair, reuse, and upcycling of materials. This resulted in missed opportunities for circular economy development, environmental protection, and community-based skill-building. There was also no structured mechanism for reinvesting economic activity into the local community. The project addressed these issues by establishing the first…
innovations.desc: The project “proBUDI VJEŠTinu” introduced an innovative, community-based circular economy model by establishing the first social enterprise in Novska focused on the reuse, repair, and upcycling of wooden and textile products. The solution combines environmental impact with social entrepreneurship: discarded furniture and materials are transformed into functional, renewed products, reducing waste and promoting sustainable consumption. At the same time, the enterprise provides practical skill-building, new service opportunities (repairs, furniture assembly, custom wooden items), and reinvests generated profit into community development. This integrated model blending reuse practices, local craftsmanship, social enterprise governance, and reinvestment of profits for community benefit, represents a new approach within the local context and strengthens the foundations for long-term social…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: The project established the first social enterprise in Novska focused on reuse, repair, and upcycling of wooden and textile products, reducing bulky waste and extending product life. It created new local service opportunities and practical skill-building in carpentry and circular economy practices. The enterprise reinvests its profit into community development, strengthening local sustainability. Overall, the project delivered environmental benefits, promoted social entrepreneurship, and increased access to affordable repair and upcycling services for citizens.

innovations.name: Gardener's Stitch
innovations.problem: This project addresses several interrelated issues: excessive consumerism in the apparel sector, the lack of functionality in clothing designed for specific activities (gardening), and the lack of community empowerment in sustainable fashion. The project solves this by offering transformable and sustainable apparel that performs multiple functions at once (reducing the need to buy more), and through the educational program "Gardener's Stitch", which teaches community members to create the garments themselves from old fabrics, thus promoting the circular economy and reducing waste.
innovations.desc:
The innovation of this project lies in the combination of three elements: -Design Innovation: The creation of transformable gardener's apparel with adjustable and detachable details, which reduces the need for excessive consumption. -Educational Innovation: The "Gardener's Stitch" training teaches community members to create the functional garments themselves from old fabrics/scraps, directly fostering the circular economy. -Social Model: The successful integration of creativity, sustainability, and community empowerment through social entrepreneurship principles.
The project was inspired by the opportunity to participate in the "Dizaino sparnai" (Design Wings) project and to have the chance to collaborate with experienced mentors and young designers.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Key Results: -Transformable Collection: Creation of a functional, sustainable gardener's apparel design (with adjustable and detachable details) that allows the garments to be worn in multiple ways. -Educational Platform: Development of the "Gardener's Stitch" training and sewing instructions/video tutorials, focused on making clothes from old fabrics. Key Benefits: -Sustainability and Circular Economy: Significantly reduced excessive consumerism through versatile design and promotion of fabric reuse (zero waste principle). -Community Empowerment: Women acquire practical sewing skills and…

innovations.name: Platforma de mediu pentru București
innovations.problem: Bucharest faces increasingly severe environmental challenges that directly affect the quality of life of its residents. Air pollution, inadequate waste management, dirty streets, outdated public transport, heavy traffic, and sidewalks occupied by cars contribute to a deteriorating urban environment and recurring social tensions. The core issue is the absence of a long-term, structural, and collaborative approach capable of generating sustainable solutions. Fragmented efforts and limited coordination hinder progress toward cleaner air, better mobility, and improved urban infrastructure. A neutral space that enables cooperation among civil society, public institutions, companies, and citizens…
innovations.desc: Platforma de mediu pentru București is a neutral collaborative space where civil society, academia, public authorities, and companies work together to address the environmental issues of the capital city. Initiated by Fundația Comunitară București and ING Bank Romania, it supports the development of projects that identify and address environmental issues and opportunities within Bucharest’s communities. Fundația Comunitară București attracts private funding (from companies that pool their resources to increase community impact) and co-finances environmental initiatives in the form of grants awarded to NGOs and civic groups selected through periodic project calls (funding rounds). In each funding round, a number of projects are selected to receive support for a period of 3–4 years, depending on project results and on the platform’s ability to attract new sources of funding.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: By 2025, Fundația Comunitară București aims to build a community that can generate collective impact in addressing the complex environmental challenges of the capital, challenges that no single actor can resolve independently. As a facilitator, it provides a neutral collaborative space where community members can develop project ideas and advocacy initiatives. Through previous funding rounds, a total of 14,882,484 lei, including 2,521,250 lei supported through the În ZONA TA initiative, has been invested in the implementation of 58 environmental projects in Bucharest and Ilfov between 2021…

innovations.name: Vote Monitor
innovations.problem: Election observation has long relied on pen-and-paper reports, which are slow, hard to coordinate, and leave little chance for timely response. Observers might see violations on election day, but NGOs would only receive data hours or even days later (when using pen and paper)—too late to act. Even with tools like WhatsApp, information is fragmented, unstructured, and difficult to analyze. In Romania, election observation has long struggled with slow reporting methods. Observers relied on pen and paper, meaning watchdog NGOs could only issue first public statements or aggregated findings 5 to 24 hours after polling stations closed, based on mid-results we reviewed from the past decade. This…
innovations.desc: Vote Monitor replaces slow, paper-based election reporting with a fast, digital system. Observers use a simple mobile app to submit structured reports, attach photos or videos as evidence, and send updates instantly - even without internet, thanks to offline mode. NGOs receive this information in real time on a secure dashboard where all reports are automatically aggregated, visualized, and ready for analysis. This enables them to detect violations during election day, communicate directly with observers, and coordinate responses before polling stations close. By streamlining reporting, breaking language barriers with localization, and reducing delays from days to minutes, Vote Monitor turns election observation into a proactive tool that strengthens transparency and protects democratic standards. By tackling local barriers in Romania and Europe while scaling globally, the solution…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Vote Monitor, which just became WSA 2025 (World Summit Award) Winner and a Global Champion of Government and Citizenship Category, has significantly changed how election observation is carried out in practice, making it faster, more coordinated, and more actionable for NGOs and observers in the field. Instead of receiving fragmented or delayed information, NGOs now receive structured reports in real time as soon as polling stations open. This allows them to follow events as they unfold throughout election day, identify repeated issues early, and respond while voting is still ongoing.
One of…

innovations.name: consolid8 Festival
innovations.problem: The sustainability and social innovation ecosystem is highly fragmented, with key actors often working in isolation. Businesses, public institutions, academic experts, innovators and community groups often operate in separate spaces, with few opportunities to exchange ideas, align priorities or explore solutions together. The ecosystem lacks a shared space where the key actors needed to create impact can work together. The festival brings business leaders, public authorities, innovators, academia and the wider community into the same place to learn from experts, find inspiration through panels and keynotes, and collaborate toward a greener and more sustainable future powered by technology,…
innovations.desc: consolid8 Festival stands as a pioneering event in Eastern Europe, entirely dedicated to the realms of green technology and sustainability. It's the first event in Romania dedicated to green technologies and sustainable urban development, with a strong focus on sustainable solutions and social innovation. The festival brings together leaders from business, public administration, education, entrepreneurship and civil society who are interested in sustainability, innovation and social impact. consolid8 Festival is a unique event designed to bring together entrepreneurs, social enterprises, organisations, creators and communities interested in responsible solutions. It provides an accessible space where participants can explore approaches that address current challenges such as climate change, the transition to more sustainable business models, green cities, the digital transformation of…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: consolid8 Festival provides a comprehensive framework where participants gain access to numerous applied sessions such as keynotes, panels, masterclasses and workshops delivered by renowned international speakers. These sessions facilitate the transfer of knowledge across diverse fields to leaders from business, public administration, education, entrepreneurship and civil society, supporting the development of a more resilient, sustainable and inclusive future. The festival offers participants practical solutions and valuable perspectives drawn from the experience of professionals across…

innovations.name: Innovative approaches to engage Ukrainian youth and host communities through civic service and social innovation
innovations.problem: The war in Ukraine has led to the displacement of millions of people across Europe, with many young Ukrainians facing interrupted education, unemployment, social isolation and limited opportunities to participate in community life. While humanitarian assistance provides immediate support, there is a growing need for long-term solutions that promote social inclusion, personal development and active participation in host communities. Traditional volunteering programmes often struggle to engage young refugees due to administrative barriers, limited financial support and a lack of tailored pathways that recognise their specific circumstances. At the same time, local young people have limited…
innovations.desc: INNOVolunteering pilots a new model of youth volunteering inspired by Civic Service principles and adapted to the realities of displaced Ukrainian youth. The methodology combines several complementary elements: - mixed volunteer groups bringing together local young people and Ukrainian refugees in equal conditions; six-month volunteering pathways based on personalised learning objectives and mentoring; - financial support through monthly stipends and accommodation to remove participation barriers; host organisations selected jointly with municipalities to ensure that volunteering activities respond to real local community needs; - a structured training programme combining online learning modules and face-to-face workshops on civic engagement, inclusion, intercultural dialogue, humanitarian support, communication and employability; - continuous mentoring by youth workers and project…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Migrants and ethnic minorities, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.benef: Collectif pour un service civique europeen
innovations.evidence: xpected results include: 1. engagement of more than 100 young volunteers, including Ukrainian refugees and local participants; development of sustainable volunteering pathways lasting six months; 2. creation of mixed local and international volunteer teams supporting community initiatives; 3. strengthened social inclusion, language skills, confidence and employability of participating young people; 4. strengthened cooperation between municipalities, NGOs and youth organisations; development of reusable training modules, implementation guidelines and operational tools that can be transferred…
authors: Collectif pour un service civique europeen

innovations.name: IT.A.CÀ Festival del Turismo Responsabile
innovations.problem: Many destinations struggle with the negative effects of mass tourism: pressure on the environment, loss of local identity, exclusion of vulnerable groups and little involvement of communities in decision-making. Travel often becomes a product to consume quickly, rather than a meaningful encounter with a place and its people. IT.A.CÀ responds to this by promoting a slower, fairer and more respectful way of travelling that benefits both visitors and residents.
innovations.desc: The festival’s innovation lies in its bottom-up approach. IT.A.CÀ is not a fixed format: each territory shapes the programme according to its own story, resources and priorities. Everything, from the themes to the activities, is co-designed with local actors. The festival also encourages “slow mobility” (walking, cycling), accessible routes, community storytelling and events that highlight the social and cultural fabric of each area. It is an open, flexible model that communities can adopt and make their own.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: -Thousands of participants join every year across multiple Italian regions. - Hundreds of events help people rediscover local areas in sustainable and inclusive ways. - Over 700 organisations have been involved since 2009, strengthening collaboration between citizens, associations, institutions and tourism operators. -The festival raises awareness about responsible travel, supports local cultural initiatives and creates spaces for dialogue on sustainability, migration and global citizenship. -IT.A.CÀ has been recognised nationally and internationally for its innovative approach to tourism.

innovations.name: Housing Thessaloniki: From identifying vacant housing stock to creating a model of social housing for Greece
innovations.problem: Greece demonstrates one of the most acute housing crises exacerbated by the fact that it is also the sole EU member state with 0% social housing stock. Greece faces one of the most serious housing affordability crises in Europe. Stagnant incomes, rising ownership changes, and sharp increases in sale and rental prices (65% for rent from 2016–2023; 10% per year for sales over the past decade) have heightened housing insecurity for more people. The dominant housing interventions to date have been primarily based on market solutions with little investment in creating public social infrastructure to combat housing exclusion (subsidized loans, incentives for property owners without social…
innovations.desc:
The innovation of this project lies at many levels. Social Housing models have appeared in many cities throughout Europe. But few can compete with the labyrinthian trajectory that Housing Thessaloniki had to disentangle. The number of uncommon synergies achieved at multiple levels surpasses imagination.   Sharing data between Thessaloniki municipalities, connecting homeless challenges with environmental national obligations, shifting perceptions toward re-using vacant properties, having to pass new regulations to establish necessary legal management bodies and offering a portfolio approach to addressing homelessness, are only some of the tips of the icebergs below!
This project was inspired by the social rental agency models in Belgium, Poland and Hungary, as well as innovative housing modules implemented in Spain (La Borda) and Belgium (CALICO), along with the Housing First approaches…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.benef: Major Development Agency of Thessaloniki, Social Rental Agency (SRA)
innovations.evidence: - Renovation and energy upscaling of 40 housing units across the city through a single international tender (economies of scale) - Linked the housing units with national programmes combating housing exclusion whose major challenge was to find affordable housing units thus supporting optimizing results of other social programmes focusing on housing - Tested a local governance model for social housing generation and delivery - Methodology for the assessment and selection of properties - Matching system - SOPs for social monitoring and support - Standardised mechanisms for collab with…
authors: Major Development Agency of Thessaloniki, Social Rental Agency (SRA)

innovations.name: IKIGAI Social Hub
innovations.problem:
Within the Social Economy ecosystem, there is significant potential for innovation and territorial development, which risks remaining untapped due to a series of structural and cultural challenges that IKIGAI Social Hub aims to address through training and support. The main identified needs are:
Lack of specific entrepreneurial skills Many young people and social organizations have high-value social ideas but lack the skills necessary to transform them into economically sustainable projects.
Limited access to dedicated support programs Unlike traditional start-ups, social economy initiatives rarely find acceleration or incubation programs tailored to their hybrid characteristics.
Weak…
innovations.desc:
IKIGAI Social Hub adopts a distinctive approach to supporting start-ups and organizations in the social economy, adapting the tools and methodologies typical of the for-profit sector to the specific characteristics of the social economy. The project stands out for the following elements:
Integrated and modular pathway The program combines practical workshops, individual coaching sessions, and group activities, guiding participants from idea generation to business model validation.
Collaborative networks and co-creation The program fosters interaction between social start-ups, sector experts, investors, and local stakeholders, creating opportunities for partnerships and territorial synergies.
Personalized support and mentorship Each project receives tailored guidance from mentors with experience in the social economy and innovation, who support participants in strategic development and…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.benef: EURICSE – European Research Institute on Cooperative and Social Enterprises
authors: EURICSE – European Research Institute on Cooperative and Social Enterprises

innovations.name: Innovative Approaches to Refugee Integration: Bridging Employability and Social Inclusion through Mutual Exchange
innovations.problem:
The project responds to two intertwined needs: improving services that support the social and economic inclusion of migrants, and helping displaced people move from an initial phase of emergency towards a more stable and sustainable situation.
In both Italy and Poland, employment remains one of the central challenges. DPUs often face discrimination in the labour market, limited access to jobs due to language barriers, and difficulties securing positions that match their skills and qualifications. On top of that, the instability and temporary nature of the legal protection frameworks further undermine their prospects, creating uncertainty for DPUs and complicating the efforts of…
innovations.desc:
The project’s innovative solutions build on pre-planned actions by RED Nova in Italy and by PAH and the Emic Foundation in Poland. These actions are further strengthened through a needs assessment led by the OPORA Foundation and a structured mutual learning process within the consortium.
In Italy, RED Nova, which currently specialises in socio-legal assistance through its Helpline and casework on legal, mediation, and translation issues, will expand its support to include job counselling and job matching. In Poland, PAH will provide vocational training for DPUs in specific sectors such as technical professions and accountancy. With the support of Emic, participants will also access targeted job counselling and Polish language classes through a One Stop Shop (OSS), where DPUs can receive comprehensive assistance. Emic will additionally run an Entrepreneurship Academy that covers not only…
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities
innovations.evidence:
Needs-based, integrated support package in Poland
A comprehensive needs assessment confirms the importance of making the labour market more accessible for DPUs in Poland, with particular attention to language barriers. In response, PAH and the Emic Foundation will offer an integrated package combining vocational courses, targeted job counselling, and Polish language classes tailored to specific professional fields.
Adaptation of RED Nova’s Helpline into an OSS-like service in Italy
RED Nova will adapt its existing Helpline into a more holistic, OSS-like service delivered by phone. In addition…

innovations.name: Centrul Cultural Plai - AMBASADA
innovations.problem: Ambasada addresses the lack of accessible spaces and resources for collaboration within the creative and non-profit sectors. In Romania, independent artists, social entrepreneurs, and NGOs often struggle to find affordable venues, professional support, and cross-sector connections needed to develop impactful initiatives. At the same time, there is limited interaction between cultural actors, businesses, and local communities, which weakens social cohesion and innovation potential. Ambasada responds to these gaps by offering a shared, inclusive space that facilitates collaboration, education, and community engagement, turning cultural and social creativity into sustainable impact.
innovations.desc: Ambasada is a social enterprise in Romania developed with the aim of incubating and increasing the impact of the local, national and international doers. Since 2015, Ambasada has offered a meeting place for non-governmental organisations, freelancers, artists, musicians, social and creative entrepreneurs. It consists of a bistro, co-working space, meeting rooms, performance and rehearsal spaces, and an event hall accommodating between 100 and 300 people. It offers free facilities and services for the creative and non-profit sectors, supported by income from the bistro and related commercial activities. In 2020, as part of the Cultural and Creative Spaces and Cities project, AMBASADA launched a community garden in the Azur yard. Responding to feedback from its active community, it later transformed this space into a hybrid work and meeting area.
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence: At Ambasada, a free community space was established to bring together creative professionals and encourage dialogue between artists and cultural actors. Among its key results and benefits are the creation of a supportive environment for collaboration, the strengthening of local creative networks, and the promotion of cultural exchange. In addition, Ambasada carries out educational and inclusion activities for disadvantaged youth, providing opportunities for learning, creative expression, and social participation through culture. This holistic approach has positioned Ambasada as both a…

innovations.name: UrbanDig Adrianio
innovations.problem:
UrbanDig Adrianio addresses the invisibility and under-appreciation of the Hadrian’s Aqueduct as a cultural and environmental resource, the lack of citizen awareness and engagement with this shared heritage, and the resulting weak connections between the neighborhoods it links.
The project responds to limited community participation in shaping local urban development, the absence of creative and educational tools that connect people to water heritage, and the fragmentation between cultural, environmental, and planning sectors that prevents integrated and sustainable approaches to urban resilience.
innovations.desc:
UrbanDig Adrianio introduces an innovative, cross-disciplinary model that transforms an invisible piece of ancient infrastructure—the Hadrian’s Aqueduct—into a catalyst for cultural activation, environmental awareness, and community-led urban development.
By blending artistic research, participatory performance, place-based education, sensory mapping, and neighborhood co-design, the project creates new ways for citizens to engage with hidden heritage and to envision sustainable futures for their public spaces.
Its approach breaks down silos between culture, water management, education, and urban planning, offering a replicable methodology that uses storytelling, creativity, and collective action to strengthen social cohesion and support heritage-driven, climate-resilient urban regeneration.
Its main line of action has been participation in local, national, and European programmes that…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
UrbanDig Adrianio delivers a set of tangible cultural, social, and environmental results: it increases public awareness of the Hadrian’s Aqueduct as both heritage and living infrastructure, strengthens connections between neighborhoods along its route, and builds new channels for citizen participation in local decision making. It generates collaborative networks between cultural actors, schools, NGOs, and public authorities, leading to more integrated approaches to urban development.
Overall, the initiative enhances community identity, activates public spaces, and provides a replicable model…

innovations.name: PLANAVA – AI-Powered Event Planning & Accessibility Certification Platform
innovations.problem: Many cultural and educational organisations struggle to plan events efficiently and ensure full accessibility for people with disabilities, older adults, or socially excluded groups. There is no simple tool that helps organisers evaluate accessibility, meet EU guidelines, and improve inclusion. This results in uneven quality, inaccessible venues, and limited participation in cultural life.
innovations.desc: PLANAVA combines AI-driven event planning tools with an automated accessibility assessment engine. The platform helps organisations design events, check compliance with accessibility standards, identify barriers, and provide a certification label. It introduces a new, scalable model for inclusive event planning, integrating digital innovation, accessibility expertise, and user-friendly guidance.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: Improved accessibility and inclusion in cultural and educational events. Time savings for organisers through AI-powered planning automation. Increased participation of people with disabilities and marginalised groups. Clear, standardised accessibility certification for events and venues. Strengthened awareness of accessibility requirements in the cultural sector.

innovations.name: Buniz by OilRight – a scented candle making waste oil right
innovations.problem: Used cooking oil is a toxic waste for the environment. When it is not collected and recycled properly, it pollutes water and soil and clogs sewage systems, creating environmental damage and additional costs for public infrastructure. Despite being a common household waste, its improper disposal remains a widespread issue that requires sustainable and innovative solutions. At the same time, people with disabilities continue to face structural barriers to participating in the labour market. Many lack access to workplaces adapted to their needs, which results in limited economic opportunities and social exclusion. OilRight addresses these two problems simultaneously by transforming a harmful…
innovations.desc: The innovative core of OilRight is based on turning used cooking oil, a common but highly polluting waste, into a sustainable raw material for new products. Instead of relying on imported or resource-intensive materials, the organisation uses a locally available waste stream, which it collects from households, restaurants, and institutions. Through a careful filtration and processing system, the oil is transformed into a clean, stable base for eco-friendly candles, sold under the brand Buniz. What makes this solution stand out is the way it connects a clear environmental goal with social impact. The recycling process is not only an ecological intervention but also the foundation for an inclusive production model. The entire candle-making process takes place in a certified protected unit, where people with disabilities are directly involved in giving this waste a second life. By…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: The initiative has a strong impact on three main levels: environmental, social, and economic. From an environmental perspective, OilRight reduces pollution by collecting and recycling used cooking oil that would otherwise contaminate water, soil, and sewage systems. This process encourages more sustainable consumption habits among individuals, companies, and communities. On the social side, the initiative creates adapted jobs for people with disabilities, giving them real opportunities for stable employment, skill development, and active participation in society. At the same time, it raises…

innovations.name: Rock the Block
innovations.problem: Rock the Block redefines housing affordability at the local scale, by employing a series of technical-energy efficient, aesthetic, circular economy and participatory interventions and tools, in order to pilot policy solutions with local communities. It promotes community engagement, social cohesion, and local empowerment, transforming housing blocks into vibrant, inclusive spaces. The project aims to reduce urban decline, foster active citizenship, and improve residents’ quality of life through participatory affordable solutions on housing.
innovations.desc: Rock the Block employs multifamily housing blocks of flats (“polykatoikia”) as the housing intervention unit for creating affordable housing solutions. The overall aim is to offer multi-level innovation solutions and thus improve housing and living conditions, by enhancing communities of mutual support, solidarity and institutional coverage. The key innovation solutions lie on the re-conceptualisation of affordability through interventions that touch upon technical, aesthetic and energy efficient aspects, and circular economy and participatory tools to engage local communities and set them in collaboration.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: The establishment of the Housing Office and the Co-Living Hub, two municipal structures that are already established and will play a desicive role in the Municipality of Egaleo’s housing policy after the project ends. Both Municipal structures are expected to effect transferable impact to other European cities as well, especially the three transfer partners, i.e. the Municipalities of Paris, Napoli and Józsefváros (Budapest).

innovations.name: SEFIT | Social Ecosystems for Fair and Inclusive Transitions
innovations.problem:
The SEFIT project addresses a key systemic problem: local authorities, social innovation actors, and community stakeholders are not yet collaborating effectively enough to tackle the challenges of the green transition and the digital transition—especially for people in socio-economic disadvantage.
Imagine the problem of the green and digital transitions as a river to cross: the risk is that only a few have the boats (resources and skills) to reach the other shore. SEFIT does not just build a boat , but develops both the blueprint for building inclusive bridges (the Policy Paper and the Shared Support Guide, which teach how to create support structures and share best practices) and a…
innovations.desc: Fondazione Giacomo Brodolini
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
The Social Ecosystems for Fair and Inclusive Transitions (SEFIT) project has yielded several key results and benefits, primarily focused on creating knowledge, providing financial support for innovation, and establishing frameworks for fair and inclusive implementation of the twin (green and digital) transition.
The key results and benefits include:
The primary benefit of SEFIT is its focus on driving transformative change for marginalised communities in Cork, Ireland, and Turin, Italy. The project aims to eliminate barriers and achieve an equitable and inclusive future , ensuring that green…

innovations.name: EcoZani

Both mining and power generation has historically been a critical source of employment in WM: in 2018, it directly employed 3,899 individuals in full-time positions and additionally 750 on 8-month contracts. Employing the Kozani Carnival as a driver with strong bonds within generations and communities, Ecozani works towards an integrated legacy: the strategic goal is to unearth, harness and retain talent, while the tactics is to turn the event into the first Zero-waste/ Zero-emission/ Zero-exclusion (3Z) Carnival in Greece and Europe. - The Ecosystem of Talent develops a local ‘Talent Booster’ reinforcing local youth entrepreneurship by initiating a Business Youth Competition, to innovate round the 3Z transformation of Kozani’s Carnival.…

innovations.name: Impact Launchpad – Social Innovation & Impact Entrepreneurship Incubation Programme
innovations.problem: Many promising social innovation ideas fail to progress due to lack of structured support, limited entrepreneurial skills, insufficient access to mentors, and weak impact validation capacities. Early-stage innovators often lack networks, resources, and market-testing environments needed to turn ideas into viable, socially beneficial ventures.
innovations.desc:
The programme integrates business development with impact measurement, lean experimentation, and systems-thinking approaches. It uses a validated “Impact Pathway” methodology developed within Impact Hub Slovenia, combining mentoring, peer validation, expert clinics, and early traction testing. Participants receive tailored guidance, access to a multidisciplinary mentor pool, and connections to investors and partners.
Support is delivered through a structured incubation pathway, where each participant progresses through clearly defined stages:
Problem and solution validation (defining user needs and testing assumptions)
Prototype and MVP development (creating first functional solutions)
Market testing and early traction (engaging first users or beneficiaries)
Impact measurement and model validation (defining and testing social/environmental impact)
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Impact Launchpad is a targeted incubation programme, distinct from the broader activities of Impact Hub Slovenia, focusing specifically on early-stage social innovators progressing from idea to validated solution. Since its launch, the programme has supported 120+ innovators, primarily individuals and small teams aged 18-35, including students, early-stage entrepreneurs, and individuals from NEET or underemployed backgrounds.
Participants have worked on solutions across sectors such as:
youth employment and skills development
mental health and wellbeing
sustainable consumption and circular…

innovations.name: AER – a zero-waste store with natural products that bring you closer to nature
innovations.problem: Modern consumption habits often generate excess waste, especially through overpackaged goods, single-use plastics, and a lack of local, sustainable alternatives. Many consumers who want to reduce their ecological footprint struggle to find practical, everyday options that align with zero-waste and ethical values. On another front, local producers and artisans often lack platforms to reach customers who care about sustainability, and community engagement and environmental education are underdeveloped in many regions. AER seeks to address these gaps by creating a retail environment where sustainable consumption is accessible and by engaging the community through education and support for…
innovations.desc: AER’s innovation is based on combining multiple functions under one concept: a Zero Waste retail space, an artisan bakery, a café and relaxing green space, and a hub for community education projects. This hybrid model allows people to engage in sustainable consumption, experience ethically made food, and participate in ecological awareness programs. AER offers many products in bulk so customers can bring their own containers and reduce packaging waste. The store works with local, small-scale, and artisanal suppliers who share its sustainability principles. In the bakery, AER applies zero waste practices: it bakes in moderate quantities, transforms surplus into new products, and partners with anti-waste platforms to redistribute leftovers. Packaging is compostable or reusable, and ingredients are chosen for their quality and integrity. Through community projects such as ecological…

innovations.evidence: Environmental impact: • Reduction of packaging waste by offering bulk products and encouraging customers to bring their own containers. • Use of compostable or reusable packaging in the bakery and store. • Prevention of food waste through moderate production, product transformation, and partnerships with anti-waste platforms. • Promotion of sustainable consumption habits among customers. Social impact: • Creation of a community space that encourages sustainable living and environmental awareness. • Educational programs for children and adults, including ecological workshops such as “STOP…

innovations.name: Ophori – natural cosmetics and fresh skincare with a social mission
innovations.problem: The cosmetics industry often contributes to environmental degradation through the use of synthetic ingredients, excessive packaging, and a lack of transparency. These practices generate waste and pollution, putting additional pressure on natural resources and ecosystems. At the same time, people with disabilities face significant barriers to entering the labour market. Many lack access to adapted workplaces and opportunities for stable employment, which limits their economic independence and social participation. Ophori addresses both challenges through an integrated model that combines responsible cosmetic production with meaningful employment opportunities for people with disabilities.
innovations.desc: The innovative approach of Ophori is based on integrating sustainable cosmetic production with social inclusion and strong social values. All products are handcrafted using carefully selected ingredients, and the composition of each product is fully transparent and publicly available. The company uses recyclable and sustainable packaging to reduce environmental impact. Production takes place in a protected unit, where people with disabilities are directly involved in all stages of the process, from preparation to packaging. By operating as a legally recognised social insertion enterprise, Ophori combines environmental responsibility with a clear social mission, demonstrating that everyday consumer products can be produced in a way that respects both nature and people.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: Ophori demonstrates how a cosmetics brand can create both social and environmental value through a clear and transparent business model. As a protected unit and social insertion enterprise, the organisation employs mainly people with disabilities, offering adapted work conditions and stable jobs. This not only provides income but also supports professional development and inclusion in the labour market. All profits are reinvested in the social mission, ensuring that economic results directly strengthen community impact. From an environmental perspective, the company reduces waste by using…

innovations.name: Community Outreach for Inclusion of Ukrainian Refugees in Bulgaria and Romania - COEXIST
innovations.problem: The war in Ukraine has forced millions of people to seek refuge across Europe, including in Bulgaria and Romania. While emergency responses have provided short-term assistance, long-term social inclusion remains a major challenge. Refugees often face language barriers, cultural differences, limited access to education and employment, and social isolation. At the same time, local communities and institutions frequently lack the knowledge, tools, and structured frameworks needed to support meaningful integration. The project addresses the need to build local capacity, foster collaboration between refugees and host societies, and create innovative, sustainable pathways for inclusion and…
innovations.desc: COEXIST introduces a research-driven and community-based approach to refugee inclusion, combining academic expertise with grassroots action. The University of Wroclaw (Poland) plays a central role in designing and testing innovative methodologies for social inclusion, mentorship, and community engagement. These methods are grounded in evidence-based research and adapted to the specific social contexts of Bulgaria and Romania. By merging scientific analysis with local experience, the project generates practical tools and learning models that strengthen the capacity of local actors to support refugees effectively. This collaboration between academia and civil society creates a new framework for social innovation—scalable, inclusive, and transferable across Europe.
