innovations.name: Train the Trainers
innovations.problem: The current mental health paradigm recognizes the active role of individuals in their own recovery journey. The Recovery College serves as a model to support this approach. Well-established in the UK, the Recovery College is a learning space offering courses on mental health, enabling each person to become a "student of their own well-being." Within this framework, there is a growing need to train trainers capable of applying recovery principles across different contexts. The project aims to broaden the very concept of "trainer," by including so-called “experts by experience” — individuals who have personally faced mental health challenges — as key figures in the training process
innovations.desc:
The project’s innovation lies in developing an educational approach to mental health that empowers individuals to take responsibility and play an active role in their own recovery journey. The Recovery College model places strong emphasis on the role of *peer support*—individuals who draw on their own lived experience with mental health challenges to support others facing similar situations. This peer-to-peer dynamic fosters engagement, hope, and a renewed sense of possibility, which are essential elements in the healing process.
In 2022, the Bologna Local Health Authority (Azienda USL), in collaboration with the University of Bologna, the Municipality, and the Metropolitan City, launched the project *“Perché ci vuole una città”* ("Because It Takes a City"), which led to the creation of the Bologna Recovery College. This is an innovative learning space offering co-designed mental health…
innovations.target: Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.evidence: Expected benefits include: the creation of a professional network able to deliver Recovery College courses consistently and effectively; the promotion of a systemic approach to well-being; the transferability of the model at both local and broader levels; and the growth of an integrated ecosystem working to support mental health across communities.

innovations.name: MY OWN-concept
innovations.problem: People with intellectual disabilities or similar support needs often face barriers to exercising their rights, making independent choices, and being recognised as experts in their own lives. Traditional support systems may limit inclusion by focusing on care rather than person wants or needs or the full scope of a person’s life. When individuals lack accessible ways to express themselves or reflect on what matters to them, they risk becoming outsiders in their own lives. There is a need for inclusive, person-centred tools that support decision-making, identity, participation, and future thinking no matter how high person´s support needs are.
innovations.desc: My Own concept is an innovative and inclusive life-planning and decision-making model co-created with people who need support. It transforms the abstract idea of self-determination and inclusion into a tangible, everyday practice through structured tools, visual elements, and inspiring methods. It is a multidimensional approach including supported decision-making, future thinking, self-directed support, and gamified reflection tools, all designed to adapt to different communication styles, life situations and levels of support need. Unlike many traditional forms or service tools, My Own is not something fixed. It is a modular and flexible set of tools that helps each person think about their own life, choices, and experiences. The ten “keys” of the concept help people and their supporters talk about important topics like voice, will, rights, goals, and community. The concept is also new…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence:
The My Own concept leads to increased self-determination, participation, and inclusion for people with intellectual disabilities or similar support needs. It enables individuals to reflect on what matters to them, express their views, and make informed decisions. The concept improves the quality of support by providing professionals and family members with concrete tools for listening, discussing and co-planning. Key results include increased self-advocacy and inclusion and more person-centred planning of services.
My Own concept has resulted in tangible and meaningful changes on both the…

innovations.name: AlarmAlly
innovations.problem:
In many public institutions — such as universities, schools, and hospitals, as well as in hotels, shopping malls and similar places - emergency evacuation procedures, though formally established, often encounter significant challenges when put into practice. People who are excluded or need additional support are particularly vulnerable during such emergencies.
Despite the sincere efforts of public and private institutions to improve evacuation protocols and enhance safety, there is currently a lack of simple, reliable solutions available on the market. In dangerous situations Deaf individals must rely on ambient or visual signals, which are seldom paired with audible fire alarms. Some…
innovations.desc:
That’s where AllarmAlly steps in.
AlarmAlly is a free mobile app compatibile with both Android and IOS systems, as well as most wearable devices. Powered by artificial intelligence, the app detects the unique acoustic signature of fire alarms and immediately alerts the user through customisable vibrations and/or flashing lights. If no user response is registered, a pre-selected support person (such as a friend, parent, or safety officer) will be notified.
The app requires no additional devices - just your phone. Compared to similar features built into some phone models, AlarmAlly is more reliable - its operation has been tested under various conditions by Deaf, hard of hearing, and healthy people. The simple interface was designed in accordance with accessibility regulations, making it easy to use and intuitive.
AlarmAlly has its own landing page, where user manuals and installation…

innovations.name: EDKI
innovations.problem:
Children with graphomotor difficulties and spastic limbs are, in a way, excluded from artistic activities. Painting and drawing using regular crayons or writing tools is impossible for them. Observations have shown a strong need for these children to engage in painting, art, and creative activities. Artistic and manual play enriches a child's world, supporting the development of imagination, emotional expression, and fine motor skills. For children with spasticity, the main barriers are the lack of appropriate tools as well as templates—pre-prepared graphic materials that support artistic development and assist in hand therapy.
The identified problems affect not only the end users—children,…
innovations.desc:
The solution was developed as a micro-innovation by Aleksandra Satława, Polish innovator-designer with funding from the ESF. The project is currently supported by the ESF+ and is moving forward through the acceleration process.
The core of the innovation is therapeutic crayons for children with graphomotor difficulties. The innovation was originally designed for children with disabilities, primarily those with hand spasticity. However, it has now become a universal, innovative tool for working with children in general.
Thanks to their special shape, the crayons stimulate and activate the hand, fingers, wrist, and elbow to extend rather than close, supporting active therapy through play. The product enables young children with hand paresis to access creative artistic activities such as writing, drawing, and coloring – which are fundamental forms of activity in the harmonious development…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.benef: The Regional Centre for Social Policy in Cracow, Krakowskie Centrum Innowacyjnych Technologii INNOAGH sp. z o.o.
innovations.evidence:
The impressions of parents and children after the EDKI testing period were overwhelmingly positive. The crayons genuinely enabled children with spasticity to draw and proved to be significantly better than traditional crayons—primarily because they were easier to use and provided a greater sense of satisfaction from drawing. Importantly, the overall positive feedback came not only from younger testers (aged 2.5–4) but also from older children (aged 9–12).
An important finding from tests conducted in therapy centers was that EDKI proved highly effective when working with children with various…

innovations.problem: Addressing the need for support for Neurodivergent and Disabled People seeking to enter tech employment. Our programme also addresses the need to build the capacity of employers who want to create more inclusive workplaces.
innovations.desc: The Cuimsiú programme is not a 9-5 classroom-based programme. Our team holds online and in person events and training from March to November each year on a range of topics, while providing 1:1 support with our Employability Mentors. The programme is suitable for people who are unemployed, in employment or education. We have aimed to make the programme as flexible as possible for those who have multiple responsibilities. We offer personalised supports to help people reach their employment goals. What the programme covers: Access to tech training, platforms and workshops. 1:1 sessions with our Employability Mentors. Preparation for the workplace – interview preparation and CV workshops. Access to assistive technology. Opportunities to network with employers. Soft skills training – communication, leadership, team work, confidence and more! Mental health and wellbeing. Exploring career…

innovations.evidence: The Objectives of the Programme are: To improve the employment prospects of people with disabilities who are currently distant from the labour market. To build the capacity of employers to recruit, retain and progress people with disabilities within their workforce. To facilitate new partnerships amongst stakeholders (people with disabilities, disability services, employment services and employers) and new approaches to providing employment supports to people with disabilities.

innovations.name: ubbu
innovations.problem: There is a growing digital divide in education, particularly affecting children from under-resourced communities who lack access to structured, high-quality learning in computer science and digital literacy. Traditional education systems often do not include programming or computational thinking in their curricula, and when they do, schools frequently lack the resources, trained staff, or tools to implement these subjects effectively. This structural inequality puts millions of children at a disadvantage. According to the OECD, 65% of children entering primary school today will work in jobs that do not yet exist. Without foundational knowledge in areas such as computer science,…
innovations.desc: ubbu is an innovative, turnkey digital platform that enables any school, regardless of its resources or technical expertise, to teach coding, digital literacy, and STEAM subjects to children aged 6 to 12. What sets ubbu apart is its holistic and inclusive approach: it combines gamification, and interactive activities with a curriculum aligned to the SDGs, making learning both engaging and socially relevant. The platform was designed to be intuitive and accessible for both students and teachers. It does not require prior technical knowledge, offering structured lesson plans, training, progress monitoring, and pedagogical support. Teachers of any subject can integrate ubbu into their classes, allowing digital skills to be taught without the need for specialist staff. ubbu also distinguishes itself from how it leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) across multiple dimensions of the…

innovations.name: Automatic metaphor identification in online texts about suicidal ideation
innovations.problem: Suicidal ideation is one of the leading mental health issues among young people in Hungary and in the EU. The individuals suffering in presuicidal syndrome communicate about their mental problems manily in online texts (i.e., in forum posts, social media posts and email consueling). These texts constitute a vast amount of linguistic material for the research in discursive suicidology. However, we do not have either enough human resource or appropriate knowledge about what the typical patterns of metaphorical language use are in these discourses. As a result, the linguistic material on suicidal ideation, even if it is available for analysis, cannot be used in large-scale research and in the…
innovations.desc: To address this problem, our project aims at creating an online platform where any input texts can be analysed in terms of metaphorical language use. The project has two primary innovative aspect. First, it uses large language models (i.e., generative artificial intelligence) for automatic metaphor identification. Second, it develops a natural language processing pipeline that integrates a lexical database, automatic linguistic preprocessing and promtping techniques to provide a fast and effective solution for finding metaphors in online discourse. This methodological innovation targets the Hungarian language, but it can be implemented in other languages as well.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The most important result of the project is the online platform for metaphor identification. The key benefit of the project lies in the acceleration and support of creating a representative linguistic database. innovations.name: Machine-driven Identification of Talent
innovations.problem: Europe faces a critical digital skills gap, with forecasts indicating a shortage of up to 3.9 million ICT professionals by 2027 (McKinsey). Simultaneously, over 100 million workers across the continent will require reskilling to remain employable in a rapidly evolving labour market driven by automation and digitalisation (McKinsey). Traditional talent selection and training processes are slow, resource-intensive, and often biased, prioritising formal qualifications and past experience over actual potential. This excludes many individuals, particularly those from vulnerable or underrepresented backgrounds, who could thrive in ICT roles if given the opportunity. This mismatch has both social…
innovations.desc: MIT (Machine-driven Identification of Talent) is an innovative solution that transforms how talent is identified and reskilled for the ICT sector. Unlike traditional approaches, which rely on CVs, previous experience, or formal education, MIT leverages artificial intelligence, machine learning, and psychometric analysis to assess individuals’ potential for success in digital careers, before they acquire technical skills. The platform delivers a one-on-one introductory course in JavaScript and captures behavioural and cognitive data through user interactions. These include response times, error patterns, navigation behaviour, decision-making processes, and perseverance across tasks. A predictive model, developed in collaboration with a team of psychologists, was trained to identify the psychometric traits most strongly associated with successful rapid reskilling. This data-driven…
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion
innovations.evidence: MIT has already demonstrated significant results in pilots with major corporate partners. An illustrative example is a reskilling initiative where 700 candidates were evaluated using MIT’s predictive model. While traditional methods have an average success rate of 6%, Code for All, with the MIT platform achieves an 87.5% success rate in selecting candidates who completed training and were successfully integrated into ICT roles. innovations.name: Social Rental Agency in Dąbrowa Górnicza
innovations.problem: The project addresses the growing problem of the lack of affordable housing for people at risk of social and housing exclusion, such as those experiencing homelessness, leaving foster care, living with disabilities, or working in low-income jobs. Despite a sufficient number of housing units on the market, people with limited income have little realistic chance of securing a rental. The project offers an intermediary solution by renting apartments from private owners, providing rent subsidies and additional social and vocational support services, effectively removing the mentioned financial, social, and organizational barriers.
innovations.desc: The project introduces an innovative model of the Social Rental Agency (SRA), which integrates the private rental market with social and vocational services into a single coordinated system. A key innovation lies in the collaboration with private landlords while providing rent subsidies and integration support to tenants, enabling access to housing for people excluded from the traditional rental market. As a part of the project, private-market apartments are renovated and furnished, and made available to those in greatest need. In addition to housing, tenants receive support in areas such as job search, accessing benefits, and managing debt. Additionally, the target groups is also able to receive a rent subsidy for maximum one year.
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion

At least 100 people in difficult housing situation will gain access to safe rental housing along with comprehensive social and vocational support, including rent subsidies and integration services. As a result, the project not only offers a roof over their heads but also a real opportunity for independence and a dignified life.

According to official statistics and reports, often these difficulties derive from emotional and behavioural problems and other psychosocial circumstances. At this point, we have to take into account that young people with (even without) mental health diagnosis frequently do not know to manage their emotional ups and downs nor how to regulate their reactions in stressing situations. It is necessary to clarify that we have developed this methodology according to a participatory research. innovations.name: New Wave WorkAbility Garden Project
innovations.problem: The roots of the Garden Project lie in North Sligo, where it began with social farming visits to Tattie Hoaker’s organic vegetable farm. This was no ordinary training site. Tattie’s farm was a place where individuals—many of whom were distant from the workforce due to physical, intellectual, or emotional challenges—could reconnect with the land and with themselves. Participants were invited to try things they had never done before: digging soil, planting seeds, gathering herbs, or simply walking among the trees and breathing fresh air. Many found this simple, earthy work unexpectedly calming. The openness of the farm, combined with the non-pressured atmosphere, allowed people to build…
innovations.desc: Responding to demand and accessibility needs, the project expanded into a city-centre garden—an oasis of green tucked into the urban landscape. Here, participants cultivate organic vegetables, herbs, and flowers, transforming unused or neglected spaces into thriving, inclusive environments. This urban adaptation brings nature into reach for more people. Participants, regardless of background or ability, take part in a range of tasks such as planting, watering, composting, and harvesting. The garden becomes both a place of learning and healing—where growth is measured in confidence as much as in crops.

innovations.name: The Sky is the Limit
innovations.problem: Corpus Christi Primary School serves the community of Moyross in Limerick, an area that has faced social and economic challenges over time. Many of our pupils have been affected by Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), and families often require support with mental health, educational engagement, and access to employment. Accessing therapeutic or family support services can be difficult, with long waiting lists and limited availability locally. For many families, travelling to appointments across the city presents further challenges, particularly when transport or flexibility is limited. These circumstances highlighted the need for a coordinated, community-based support hub that can respond…
innovations.desc: The Sky is the Limit addresses these challenges by embedding therapeutic and family supports into the school setting. Through an on-site Family Centre, children and adults can access counselling, psychotherapy, play therapy, music therapy, and mindfulness programmes. A Family Support Worker and Employment Activation Officer ensure wraparound help for families most in need. Two Extended Learning Opportunities Coordinators create structured after-school opportunities for targeted children, reducing risk and increasing engagement. The model uses a shared staffing approach across schools to maximise reach and cost-efficiency, while placing children’s emotional safety and educational potential at the centre.

innovations.name: ICT-BASED DIAGNOSTIC TOOLS AND KNOWLEDGE DEVELOPMENT
innovations.problem: In recent years it has become evident from psychological research that underperforming in school is often caused by weak cognitive control functions which is not easily detected without expert assessment. Currently psychologists and special education professionals in Hungary do not have at their disposal a comprehensive sytem of assessment to this end. Thus our goal is to fill in this gap and develop an online test battery to measure these functions which is up to date, innovative, and in accordance with legislation concerning privacy and data handling. Our battery contains eight tests in total which measure different aspects of control fuctions including attention, memory, planning,…
innovations.desc: An important aspect of our innovation is adaptive testing. This makes it possible for the target group living with vulnerability to participate in enjoyable, motivating testing procedures that reveal their strengths and weaknesses. This expectation was confirmed by our external test-taking experts: our child participants worked in the online system with joy and perseverance, on the same tasks that they were reluctant to solve on a traditional paper-and-pencil basis. Given that only a digital device (e.g. smartphone) is required for the test, the examination and thus early screening can also be implemented in lagging micro-regions.
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: The goal of our project is to create an equitable educational environment, that is, e-inclusion, by which learning disadvantages can be minimized, and enable autonomous as well as cooperative learning for students. To acheve this, interactions in e-inclusion need to include not only the diagnosis of atypical development, but later also the application of online gamified intervention programs and subsequent efficiency measurement. In addition, the online platform makes possible the secure storage and handling of data, and minimizes data loss and damage.

innovations.name: ALMA (Aim-Learn-Master-Achieve) - Prácticas Transnacionales
innovations.problem: Young people from vulnerable backgrounds in Spain—particularly those with limited education, work experience, or social support—often face significant barriers to employment and social inclusion. These challenges are compounded by low self-confidence, limited mobility, and reduced access to international experiences that could expand their horizons and skills. Traditional training and job placement services are not always sufficient to engage and empower this target group in a sustainable way.
innovations.desc: The ALMA Programme introduces an innovative model that combines international mobility with structured, personalised professional internships in another EU country—in this case, Münster, Germany. What sets this initiative apart is its holistic approach: participants are supported before, during, and after their mobility experience through mentorship, intercultural preparation, and follow-up plans for their reintegration into education or employment back in Spain. This tailored, experiential learning framework helps participants develop not only technical skills but also key transversal competences such as resilience, adaptability, and intercultural communication.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion

Additionally, the programme fosters social inclusion and supports long-term labour market integration. innovations.name: Children Agora: Voices in Action
innovations.problem: In rural Lithuania, children from low-income families, single-parent households, Roma communities, and other socially excluded groups often lack real opportunities to influence decisions that affect their lives. While participation is a recognized right, in practice, it is rarely implemented meaningfully — especially outside formal education settings. Most community organizations do not have structures for children’s voices to shape services or programs, and children are often seen as passive recipients rather than active contributors. Debesų kiemas, a community-based organization rather than a school, works directly with vulnerable children in non-formal settings. This creates a unique…

While participation is often limited to older youth, this project intentionally includes younger children — starting from age 7 — based on the belief that democratic habits and civic confidence must be nurtured from an early age. Early involvement helps build a lasting sense of agency, responsibility, and belonging. The innovation lies in integrating real decision-making power into a non-formal, community-based setting rather than a school. innovations.name: Scientists Return to School
innovations.problem: The project aims to mitigate the low levels of scientific literacy in Portugal, as well as their consequences. Data from PISA 2022 shows a significant drop in science and math results compared to 2018, as well as an increase in “low performers” and a drop in 6th grade science literacy levels. Low scientific literacy is most evident in places that are under-served in terms of access to science and quality education, and in areas that are less privileged in socio-economic terms. The focus is on children creating relevant connections with science and being co-creators in the acquisition of knowledge through interaction with “real scientists”. The project is also based on the innovative concept of Circular Education, fostering the idea of giving back to our community. By implementing these concepts through an educational programme, it makes it possible to reach schools with less access to science/extracurricular activities, helping to transform vicious cycles into virtuous ones, through contact with scientists with whom the children can easily relate (from the same background). innovations.problem: In the 21st century new jobs have emerged, and also the way we do our jobs has also changed. Therefore, certain competencies have become more crucial, so the question emerges how higher education can prepare graduates for such changes.
innovations.desc: The project included an analysis of competency requirements in Hungarian business higher education, as well as the expectations of potential employers, based on job portal listings and focus group interviews with industry professionals. The identified competencies served as the basis for Q-methodology research aimed at exploring the importance and hierarchy of these competencies, as well as identifying distinct groups of employer representatives.

The research also explored the competence gap, identifying discrepancies in the areas of skills, abilities, and attitudes and values. innovations.name: The New Leaf Czechia
innovations.problem: In the Czech Republic, the number of people experiencing homelessness has been steadily increasing. According to national estimates, over 23,000 people are without stable housing, and more than 160,000 are at immediate risk of losing their home due to poverty, rising rents, and inadequate housing support. Existing systems are often conditional, fragmented, and overly bureaucratic. Many individuals remain trapped in a cycle of temporary shelter, administrative barriers, and limited opportunities for real change. Social workers are overstretched, and people in need are often treated with suspicion rather than trust. New Leaf Czechia addresses this by testing whether unconditional financial…
innovations.desc:
New Leaf Czechia was inspired by the New Leaf Project in Canada, implemented by the non-profit organisation Foundations for Social Change in partnership with the University of British Columbia. The Canadian pilot provided unconditional cash transfers to people experiencing homelessness and showed promising outcomes in housing stability, food security, and well-being. This evidence-based approach, combined with growing interest in trust-based interventions, served as the foundation for adapting the model to the Czech context, while adding a strong component of exclusive social work as a key innovation.
New Leaf Czechia introduces a bold combination of two underused approaches in Central Europe: unconditional cash transfers and exclusive, relationship-based social work. Instead of controlling behaviour through conditional aid, the project invests trust in people by giving them a one-time…

innovations.name: Secret Sound
innovations.problem:
Despite advances in technology and inclusion, millions of people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or deafblind still face major barriers to fully accessing audiovisual content, cultural events, and public communication. Current solutions are often:

Inaccessible: Services like sign language interpretation are limited, expensive, and not scalable.

Sport is often seen solely as physical activity, but it has untapped potential to drive broader social change. It can be a powerful catalyst—not just for improving health, but for building confidence, fostering relationships, strengthening communities, and opening new life pathways.

Rather than prescribing fixed interventions, the programme empowers Local Sports Partnerships and dedicated ESF+ Social Innovation in Sport Officers to collaborate directly with individuals and communities to co-design initiatives that respond to their real, lived needs.
Each local initiative is unique — shaped through engagement with target groups and tailored to the specific social, cultural, and economic contexts of the area. This decentralised, human-centred design model ensures that sport is not only inclusive, but also relevant and impactful in addressing broader challenges such as social isolation, unemployment, and lack of educational pathways.
A national support structure underpins this local innovation, including ongoing training in social…

innovations.problem: The programme aims to ensure that people with disabilities are fully supported to find and maintain employment and organisations which employ programme participants are supported to ensure that their employment is successful.
innovations.desc:
WorkAbility works with pupils with a disability throughout their final two years of secondary education, and for a further 12 months after they leave school, to support their own personal development and assist their move into education/training or work roles that match their potential.
The progression pathway for participants is based on a strong working relationship with a Job Coach and includes regular individualised job coaching, work experience and networking opportunities.
The programme focuses on supporting employers to increase their capacity to recruit, retain and progress people with disabilities. Through engagement with businesses, jobseekers will be matched to job opportunities and both the employee and employer will be supported through the initial period of employment.

The tools that were already available before the start of our project were not suitable for use in the…

The materials and tools available to youth NGOs, young people, youth leaders and youth workers were not comprehensive and often only partially useful for them - the tools focusing on organisations tended to have a strong entrepreneurial orientation or focused on only part of the organisation's activities (e.g. events). We designed the project based on a needs analysis of the end-users - youth workers and leaders - and during the pilot testing phase of our project's results, we gathered feedback and upgraded the tools to better address the needs of the users. The aim of the online training for developing green competences was to bring about a change in the…

Online training to develop or upgrade green competences, focusing on individuals' needs for knowledge about the environment, ecological footprint and climate change, ways to adapt to it, and greener lifestyles,

innovations.name: Living Labs for digital and innovative solutions for elderly and disabled citizens
innovations.problem:
In Croatia more than 22% of the population is 65 and older (in 2024). Forecasts for 2050 predict more than 30%. 17% of population are persons with disabilities (2024).
There is a growing need for technological and social innovations to support the inclusion and care of this population. Social service providers face challenges in serving an increasing number of people, while tech startups and innovators working in the social services sector struggle to find sustainable business models.
innovations.desc: New technologies are developed all over and it’s time to apply them to tackle our societal challenges in the sphere of social services. To foster this transformation, we establish our labs integrated into care facilities. They are the place to be for ambitious teams to present their innovative solutions to users and buyers for in-depth evaluation and co-development.

The living labs will expand their role to include social innovations as well, connecting stakeholders from different sectors who can propose and develop innovative solutions.

innovations.problem:
The problem addressed by VOICE is the limited access to targeted, inclusive, and scalable upskilling and reskilling opportunities for Ukrainian refugees across Europe, particularly in the wake of Russia’s war of aggression and the resulting displacement crisis.
More specifically, VOICE responds to several interlinked challenges:
Employment Barriers Many Ukrainian refugees face difficulty entering the labor market in host countries due to mismatched qualifications, lack of recognition of prior learning, or limited access to vocational training aligned with local demands.
Digital and Skills Gap Refugees often lack digital literacy, entrepreneurial competencies, and soft skills that are…

At the heart of social innovation lies the power of education—not as a static system, but as a transformative force that enables individuals to acquire the capabilities they need to participate fully in society.
This vision, echoed in the European Commission’s Prospective Report on the Future of Social Innovation in Education, inspired the design of the VOICE project.
By empowering displaced Ukrainians through accessible, skills-based, and inclusive learning, VOICE turns education into a pathway for social integration, employability, and long-term resilience across Europe while fostering diversity and promoting the acquisition of social skills, empathy, and tolerance in the long term (Prospective report on the future of social innovation in education, p. 45).

Mixed-group piloting of refugees and local citizens promoting integration and social cohesion.
Open Educational Resources (OER) platform hosting training, tests, certificates, glossary, gamification tools, and success stories.

innovations.name: Vitamines12
innovations.problem: Transportation in rural areas is neither inclusive nor low-carbon compatible. In areas where public transportation is non existent, achieving carbon neutrality goals for mobility is a major challenge. These rural areas often face systemic barriers such as long daily commutes, social isolation, and lower-than-average incomes, which prevents investments in zero-emission conventional vehicles. These combinations of factors lead to total car dependency. There is a growing need to decarbonize transports and promote social inclusion through new and efficient means of transportation adapted to rural areas.
innovations.desc: In’VD develops and supports a project called Vitamines12 that addresses these challenges through practical, real-life experiences with prototype vehicles that meet the real needs of the rural population. In’VD aims to promote a new category of vehicles called Vélis, Véhicules Légers Intermédiaires (UltraLight intermediate vehicles, L category) that bridges the gap between bicycles and cars. These vehicles are designed to be sober, recyclable, and efficient, all under a total weight of 600 kg. These specifications help to achieve low cost mileage, such as 0.75€ per 100km (QBX Sorean) compared to 2.7€ per 100km for a regular electric car (Renault Zoé) with a fith of the purchase cost and low maintenance, while maintening almost a similar travel duration. The initiative also targets all population categories : active, inactive, retired, young and older citizens, with and without children.…
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Other target groups
innovations.evidence: In'VD has developed low-carbon transportation solutions for the local population that meet professional and specific needs. The promotion of transportation through active vehicles, where one can pedal, also helps in fighting health issues, especially obesity, that has risen from 8.5% (1997) to 17% (2020) (INSERM and CHU Montpellier). The program has accumulated in 2025 a hundred months of experimentation ( >100,000km), 48% women, 52% men, with an effective satisfaction around 80% where individuals have successfully replaced their need of a conventional car without compromising their daily…

innovations.name: Bureaux du Coeur
innovations.problem:
In France alone, at least 330,000 people are homeless, sleeping on the streets, in cars, squats or emergency accommodation. With the housing market so tight, even working people can find themselves in precarious housing situations. Whatever the age or situation, the experience of the street is extremely violent and destructive and accelerates desocialization.
At the same time, every night and weekend, thousands of offices are heated, lit... and empty.
This was the observation behind Bureaux du Coeur.
innovations.desc:
We develop the use of professional premises as individual temporary accommodation at night and over the
weekend for people following an integration project. We rely on a tripartite relationship between:
- The host organizations, mainly businesses, public actors and associations, who make available for 3 to 6
months a sleeping area set up in an office or meeting room.
- Our partners, social integration structures or associations, who are responsible for identifying a guest
among their beneficiaries and supporting him/her in his/her daytime integration project (employment, access
to rights, healthcare, training).
- The guest, who uses the space free of charge at night and over the weekend.
By bringing these players together and actively accompanying them through the hosting process, Bureaux
du Coeur, allows each guest to bounce back.
To do this, Bureaux du Coeur relies on a large number…
innovations.target: Homeless persons, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion

720 guests have been hosted since the program was created, representing 98,000 overnight stays
80% of guests have had a “positive exit” from the program, into permanent housing
300 host organizations welcome their guests every evening
290 partner organizations (solidarity associations, public bodies, etc.) assist the guests with their
reintegration projects
250 volunteers are mobilized to find solutions in 38 delegations, in France and elsewhere in Europe

innovations.problem: It remains a challenge for marginalized children and young people to break free from negative social heritage. This is especially linked to a lack of deep relationships and healthy ties to family and friends, making it difficult for children and youth in vulnerable life situations to build long-lasting networks to draw upon as they enter adolescence and adult life. Mentorkid addresses this by matching children and youth with a FriendshipFamily, who voluntarily invites the child into their family and everyday life.
innovations.desc: Mentorkid offers a unique solution to a complex societal challenge. Mobilizing voluntary families with the main focus on building lasting relationships was — and still is — a socially innovative initiative navigating on the margins of the public sector and civil society. Hence Mentorkid plays a key role in the development of social competencies and networks for children and youth, supporting their path into the educational system and, subsequently, the labour market.

This leads to improved quality of life and increased self-esteem. It also enhances their educational opportunities and supports their ability to participate in society. The Friendship Families also benefit greatly from their voluntary work with Mentorkid. In addition to forming deep bonds with a child or young person, they gain knowledge and experience by learning about different life circumstances and find great…

innovations.name: The shared house of Artolie
innovations.problem: In rural areas, many retirees face isolation, unsuitable housing for aging. Vacant buildings and declining village centers further weaken social ties. Without alternatives, seniors are often forced to leave their communities or live in inadequate conditions, leading to a loss of autonomy, security, and social engagement.
innovations.desc: Habitats des possibles addresses the lack of suitable housing options for retirees in rural areas by offering shared, inclusive homes designed with and for local communities. Our homes allow seniors to maintain their independence with private spaces, foster daily mutual support through shared areas, and stay connected to village life. We aim to support meaningful aging by promoting freedom of choice, social ties, and well-being, while revitalizing rural centers and encouraging a more collaborative, affordable model of living.

The house includes 8 private apartments and 231 m² of shared spaces like a lounge, kitchen, dining room, and garden. Through 13 participatory workshops, future residents actively shaped the design and project vision, fostering a strong sense of ownership. Located in central Lestiac-sur-Garonne, the house promotes social connections with easy access to local services and…

innovations.name: Un abri qui sauve des vies (A shelter that saves lives)
innovations.problem:
Every year in France, over 200,000 women report being victims of domestic violence. Many wish to flee urgently, but cannot find a safe place to go. Emergency shelters are saturated or hard to access, especially for women with children, undocumented persons, or those outside major cities. This lack of immediate, adapted shelter options forces many to remain in dangerous environments or accept inadequate solutions.
Public systems alone cannot meet the need. There is an urgent demand for alternative, community-rooted responses that are safe, fast to deploy, and supportive of victims’ agency and dignity.
innovations.desc:
Un abri qui sauve des vies offers an innovative model of citizen-led emergency shelter. We mobilise local volunteers who can host a person or a family for a few nights or a few weeks, depending on the situation.
We ensure a rigorous process of host recruitment, training, and support, including background checks, home visits, and ongoing contact. We also work hand in hand with professionals who refer victims to us and continue their follow-up.
During the stay, we act as a bridge between the host, the guest, and the professionals: we coordinate logistics, provide a listening ear, assist with transport, access to food, and appointments, and make sure safety protocols are respected.
This model enables rapid, flexible and deeply humane shelter options for people who are often invisible in traditional systems.
innovations.target: Individuals experiencing gender marginalization, Individuals experiencing poverty or social exclusion, Individuals whose mental health or wellbeing is compromised
innovations.benef: Un abri qui sauve des vies
innovations.evidence:
Since 2020, Un abri qui sauve des vies has facilitated more than 8,500 nights of shelter for victims of domestic and family violence. Over 550 women and children have been hosted in safe, caring environments, thanks to a growing network of 1 000 volunteer hosts (abritant·e·s) across France
The organisation is active nationally and operates through local branches (antennes) in Île-de-France, Hautsde-France, Normandie, and Pays de la Loire, with a team of 400 volunteers, and a small operational team of 5 salaried staff and 3 freelancers .
The model has demonstrated high efficiency and strong…

innovations.name: Housing First Pula: Social Innovation for Homelessness Prevention
innovations.problem: Traditional approaches to homelessness in Croatia emphasize transitional housing and shelters, often failing to provide long-term stability. Homeless individuals face multiple social barriers, including unemployment, mental health issues, and lack of institutional support.
innovations.desc: The "Housing First" model reverses conventional approaches by ensuring immediate, permanent housing, accompanied by individualized support services. These services include employment assistance, psychological counseling, healthcare access, and community reintegration programs. Unlike traditional models, Housing First does not require sobriety, employment, or participation in rehabilitation programs as a precondition for housing.

innovations.name: DUO for a JOB
innovations.problem: Many young people, especially those with a migrant background, face significant barriers to entering the workforce. These challenges include systemic discrimination, limited access to professional networks, and a lack of support to navigate job markets, leaving their potential untapped. At the same time, older professionals, despite possessing valuable experience and expertise, often grapple with social and professional disengagement after retirement or career shifts, leading to underutilized skills and a sense of isolation. This dual challenge not only hinders individual progress but also limits societal growth by failing to leverage the talents of both groups effectively.
innovations.desc: DUO for a JOB offers a unique mentoring program that connects young job seekers with a migrant background with experienced professionals aged 50+. Through one-on-one mentoring, the program fosters knowledge transfer, providing practical guidance, career advice, and skill development tailored to the mentee's needs. It also builds confidence by empowering young people to overcome challenges and realise their potential. By opening access to mentors' networks, it helps mentees navigate the hidden job market and create new opportunities. At the same time, mentors remain socially and professionally engaged, contributing their expertise to society. This approach not only enhances job seekers' employment prospects but also promotes intergenerational solidarity and social cohesion, creating a positive impact for individuals and communities alike.
innovations.target: Migrants and ethnic minorities, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.evidence: DUO for a JOB significantly improves employment prospects for young job seekers: 50% secure employment. In total, 70% find a positive outcome (job or training). Beyond job placement, mentees gain confidence, soft skills, and access to professional networks, breaking barriers to inclusion. Mentors stay engaged, sharing expertise and fostering intergenerational solidarity. The program strengthens social cohesion, fights discrimination, and maximises the potential of both youth and experienced professionals, creating a win-win dynamic for individuals and society.

innovations.problem: Social inclusion has been on the EU’s policy agenda since the 1970s and has become a central political goal in Finland during the last decades. A large number of projects and interventions have been initiated to promote social inclusion among people in disadvantaged positions. However, there is neither a common definition for the concept of social inclusion on the individual level nor a commonly agreed measurement for it. innovations.desc: The Experience of social inclusion scale (ESIS) is a brief closed survey instrument to assess particularly subjective experiences of social inclusion. Hence, the ESIS reaches beyond traditional statistical parameters used for social inclusion and fills an important gap in the field. It measures the experience of inclusion with ten statements. The statements assess the respondent's experiences of belonging, meaningfulness, capabilities for action, and manageability in everyday life. The statements are based on a comprehensive framework on social inclusion emphasising quality of social interaction, belonging and getting heard, agency and opportunities to influence the course of life and the living environment. innovations.name: Solidary Basic Income
innovations.problem: To address long-term unemployment, the State of Berlin has initiated a pilot project called “Solidary Basic Income” ( Solidarisches Grundeinkommen (SGE) ), running from July 2019 to December 2025. This pilot offers long-term unemployed individuals a permanent job in socially relevant activities as an alternative to receiving unemployment benefits. The goal is for participants to transition into unsubsidized permanent employment, enhancing their reintegration and advancement in the labor market and social participation, while also promoting work that benefits the community at large.
innovations.desc: Around 1,000 permanent jobs were created in local public administrations, public companies, and social service providers for individuals unemployed for one to three years. These jobs offer fair wages and additional coaching and training to support participants' transition into unsubsidized employment. If participants do not transition, the jobs must benefit the community without replacing regular employment, such as by enhancing public transport or day care centre accessibility. Employers receive financial incentives and support, including coaching for HR staff and a EUR 2,500 bonus for each SGE employee who secures a job in the unsubsidized labour market.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.benef: Senate Department for Integration, Labour and Social Services
innovations.evidence:
By November 2020, all 1,000 slots in the Solidary Basic Income (SGE) program were filled. The initiative is being evaluated to guide future labor market policies in Berlin using various methods, including surveys.
Key lessons learned from the SBI program include the option to temporarily suspend contracts to allow for trial periods outside the program, easing concerns among employees about job security. There's also consideration of facilitating employer changes within the SBI to enhance participants' prospects for sustainable employment. The coaching service provider plans additional…

innovations.name: MAGMA (ended)
innovations.problem: In the early 20th century, Marienthal was a thriving industrial town, with a large textile factory employing a significant portion of the local population. However, the factory closed down in the early 1930s, leading to a devastating economic crisis in the area. This crisis was famously studied by a team of sociologists, who published their findings in the influential book “The Unemployed of Marienthal” in 1933 (Jahoda, Lazarsfeld and Zeisel, 2017).
innovations.desc: Starting in October 2020, the three-year pilot project Modellprojekt Arbeitsplatzgarantie Marienthal (MAGMA; “job guarantee pilot project”) started to offer a job guarantee for the long-term unemployed in that location. Initiated by the regional office of the Austrian Public Employment Service in Lower Austria, the programme aims to abolish long-term unemployment, counter its social and individual effects, and provide counselling to help participants secure employment in the regular labour market. However, unlike traditional active labour market policies, which prioritise reintegration into the regular labour market, MAGMA differs significantly and is more similar to income support or welfare initiatives. As part of the innovative concept, MAGMA was designed as a field experiment to evaluate the causal effects of guaranteed employment on individuals and the local labour market.
innovations.target: Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons
innovations.evidence:
The MAGMA project illustrates the viability of a job guarantee program and underscores the necessity for alternative programmes for long-term unemployed individuals. Key to its success is partnering with capable entities that provide meaningful tasks relevant to the primary labour market. Equally crucial is robust counselling by public employment services or similar institutions before participants enter the program. Collaboration among all relevant institutions is essential to integrate social security networks and secure collective funding for such initiatives.

innovations.name: UP! Tutoring support
innovations.problem: The primary issue addressed in the research is the significant educational inequality in Austria, where children from low socio-economic backgrounds have substantially lower chances of achieving educational standards compared to their peers from higher socio-economic backgrounds. This disparity in educational outcomes is rooted in various socio-economic factors that limit access to academic support and resources, thus perpetuating a cycle of disadvantage for children from poorer families.
innovations.desc:
The innovative solution proposed involves a structured tutoring program where secondary school students and adult volunteers provide free tutoring to primary school children. innovations.name: Minduu
innovations.problem:
Patient Problem
Finding information about mental health professionals is hard, and it is even harder to find one that has available appointments and suits your specific needs and personality. What makes matters worse, is that most professionals work as independent practitioners causing the market to be extremely scattered.
Therapist Problem
As therapists work mostly as private practitioners, they have to handle everything themselves from customer acquisition to invoicing and making patient notes. This can be very time consuming, costly and burdensome. Until now there has not been online solutions at the market designed especially for psychotherapists.
innovations.desc:
Solution for Patients
With Minduu the process of finding a mental health professional that matches your needs is made easy and simple. Minduu offers relevant information about the professionals displayed in a way that is useful for the customer and makes it effortless to book a time online.
Solution for Therapists
For professionals Minduu is a new sales and marketing channel, but also provides CRM, patient notes, invoicing, messaging and video meetings. It’s a one-stop shop for mental health professionals. Minduu takes care of the business and let’s professionals concentrate on their clients.

We've created a network of around 1500 therapists and are the most popular portal in Finland to find a psychotherapist. Every year we help tens of thousands of people in finding the right therapist for them and make it quicker and easier to start psychotherapy.
In addition we enable private practitioners to continue working independently by providing them with the right tools and support.

innovations.name: Gathering Forces for Increased Youth Employment
innovations.problem: Securing a job is not a given for many young people. A lack of understanding, a lack of role models, inefficient processes, prejudice and segregation are just some of the many challenges that a young person can face in trying to find a job. These trends are reflected in the increasing youth unemployment rates in Sweden, with young people from socio-economically disadvantaged areas notably being the worst affected. At the same time, social entrepreneurs are sitting on innovative solutions to address these issues, but are struggling to find sustainable long-term models to support their successful scaling.
innovations.desc: This project sees effective cross-sectoral collaboration as the solution to the above challenges- collaboration which promotes a more equal and non-discriminatory labour market for young people. Social entrepreneurs and municipalities have potential to jointly address social challenges in an effective way, but find difficulties to understand and exploit each others’ strengths and weaknesses. This project builds upon a previous initiative, implemented by Reach for Change and Right by Me and financed by Delegation against segregation, which aimed to gain insights into existing barriers and brainstorm new potential models of collaboration between the two different types of stakeholders. Together with Eskilstuna municipality, we now test and refine a model of collaboration for implementation and dissemination among other municipalities in Sweden.

innovations.evidence: Workshops and capacity development activities will bring together youth leaders and youth participants to foster stronger attitudes and self-confidence related to taking on working life. innovations.problem: In 2018, Acción Contra el Hambre and the EPINUT research group of the Universidad Complutense de Madrid observed that unemployed people had worse health conditions, compared to the employed population, and that, at the same time, this fact could influence their employability. In other words, unemployment and job insecurity do not only affect the economic well-being of people in a situation of social vulnerability, but also lead to a worsening of their physical, emotional, and social health. Against this background, socio-occupational insertion programmes were identified as a suitable resource for the incorporation of other activities that could have an impact on the health of the most…
innovations.desc:

innovations.name: Chat net („Plaudernetz“)
innovations.problem:
Chat net was launched to combat loneliness and promote social cohesion, in response to the following challenges:
1.5 million people in Austria live alone, and 600,000 people in Austria feel lonely on a regular basis.
Even before Covid-19, loneliness has been classified as a disease of civilization, with 12% of Europeans having felt lonely more than half of the time. This number has doubled to over 25% during the Corona pandemic, with harmful repercussions on people's mental and physical health.
Current multiple crises further exacerbate the situation for those affected. Many people have an increased need for exchange and long for human interactions.
innovations.desc:
Chat net offers an easily accessible way to anonymously connect with others with the aim to combat loneliness . Thereby, it closes a gap in social care and unburdens existing structures.
Rather than a crisis hotline, Chat net aims at increasing social well-being by connecting people in need with chat net partners.  The beauty of the solution lies in its simplicity – whenever a person feels lonely, they call chat net. Registration is not required, making the service easily accessible for all target groups. This “chat service” is unique in Austria and an example how digital innovation can alleviate social problems.
Chat net enables also a new way of volunteering for people with limited mobility or time. Thus, a new form of location-independent engagement is made possible, so that older people can volunteer from home. It also enables people with limited time, to volunteer based on their…
innovations.target: Other target groups
innovations.evidence:
Since April 2020, Chat net has been used by ~8,000 volunteers and callers across Austria. So far, the project has achieved the following results:
32,700 conversations were enabled since April 2020, with more than 11,000 conversations in 2022.
On average, calls last 25 minutes. This sums up to 790,000 minutes of chatting.
4,100 voluntary chat partners have registered for Chat net.
More than 4,900 callers have called the Chat net number. New callers join daily - 3 per day on average in 2022.

innovations.name: House of Skills
innovations.problem: Technological and social evolution mean that the content and skills requirements of almost every job evolve frequently. This represents a challenge in Belgium, where opportunities for workers to develop new skills are rather limited. In Ghent, many workers are active in industries connected with the port of Ghent, where important changes will see significant numbers of low-skilled administrative jobs disappear in a short period. Lifelong learning, upskilling and reskilling are thus extremely relevant and should be a priority for every working person.
innovations.desc:
House of Skills is a pilot service that encourages employees to proactively acquire the new skills that will equip them for transitions in the labour market (e.g. introduction of new technologies, digitalisation, green transition). House of Skills is innovative in that it combines existing stand-alone services and offers them as part of an integrated process.
House of Skills combines career guidance linked to the evolution of the labour market with modular training, which offers a high degree of flexibility for workers. Workers engage in tailored training, starting at their own level and learning at their own pace, through a blended learning approach.
The first step of the service is to establish a contact with the company, in order to get an overview of  the current state, its ambitions and plans for the future in order to identify its skills needs. Organisational and personal goals…

innovations.evidence:
House of Skills is currently piloted with two companies in Ghent: Europabank and Volvo Car. Each year, 15 individuals per company are involved, on average. The impact on employers and employees will be measured by Artevelde University following a process-tracing for impact evaluation, a qualitative analysis methodology focusing on the various links in the process and establishing the causality between them, in order to obtain a full picture of the impact of the project.
The evaluation is ongoing and will be completed by August 2022.

innovations.name: Obce blíže lidem
innovations.problem: Some categories of individuals living in rural areas, such as older people with no pensions, people experiencing homelessness, refugees, ex-prisoners and addicts are particularly at risk of social exclusion. Crucial services, such as psychiatric care and help to address addictions, are often limited or unavailable in rural areas, with waiting times of three to four months to secure an appointment in the city.
innovations.desc:
This EU-funded project addresses the risk of social exclusion in rural regions among vulnerable groups, such as older people, homeless people, refugees, etc.
‘Bring villages closer to people’ ( Obce blíže lidem ) works closely with key stakeholders in rural communities, such as mayors, schools, food banks, and other leaders and service providers, to reach vulnerable people and provide both short-term and long-term assistance. It seeks to eliminate access barriers through the assistance of social workers. These workers liaise closely with stakeholders in rural areas to unify people within communities, destigmatise vulnerable groups, and raise awareness of both local needs and support available. Activating communities thus leads to a sustainable source of assistance.

Gradually, local mindsets have begun to change, with more people realising the risk of vulnerability and coming forward to offer their support.

innovations.name: En Ergo
innovations.problem: For many years, in Cyprus, there has been a shortage of qualified care workers to work with persons with disabilities in their homes. As a result, persons with severe mobility issues caused by spinal injuries, including paraplegia and tetraplegia, mainly had to rely on family for help or to employ unskilled domestic workers.
innovations.desc:
The En Ergo: Independent Living project is implemented by the Cyprus Paraplegic Organisation (CPO) to train unemployed people to become home-care service professionals for persons with disabilities. The project seeks to facilitate independent living and social inclusion for all people with similar disabilities.
The project began in 2018 and will run until 2023. It is fully funded by the ESF through schemes serving two purposes:
1. Creating skilled professionals to provide home-care services for persons with disabilities.
2. Decreasing unemployment by hiring unemployed persons;
The innovative approach targets both unemployment and the development of quality care services, thereby encouraging social inclusion.
The project offers unemployed people the opportunity to obtain the European Care Certificate [1] , a Europe-wide qualification which fully qualifies them for a carer role. The…

Annual member and employee satisfaction surveys collect feedback on the service. Based on the feedback received, the CPO has managed to further adapt the services to the end clients’ needs. For example, the feedback highlighted that it would be beneficial to broaden the aim and services of the programme to other categories of people with severe mobility issues. As a result, the CPO has broadened the scope of the programme and…

innovations.name: Fit4Coding
innovations.problem: Luxembourg has been experiencing in the last 10 years a gap between its strong economic growth and its talent base, particularly in information technology (IT) jobs for coders and developers. Organisations aiming to adapt to digital transformation were hindered by the shortage of digital competencies. At the same time, many young adults were observed to be outside the paths of conventional education. This created an opportunity to align their upskilling training with the needs of the digital job market. The first phase of the ‘Fit4Coding’ project ran from 2016 until 2017, while the second phase ran from 2018 to 2019. The European Social Fund (ESF) funded 50% of each phase, complemented by a…
innovations.desc: Fit4Coding Jobs offered the first coding bootcamp training in Luxembourg. Its innovation was the combination of technical and employability skills in a setting that allowed for individual support. Trainees received 490 hours of training in an intensive ‘bootcamp format’ from experts on the most popular coding technologies (HTML, CSS, JS, Angular, Laravel, PHP, Bootstrap, JQuery). Classes were in-person, in small groups (max. 20), which was well-suited to those without previous academic training. Participants also took an employability module, ensuring they were prepared to meet potential employers. Another innovation was running the project in English rather than French, reflecting the fact that some 70% of Luxembourg’s workforce is composed of immigrants and cross-border workers. Finally, the selection process for project participants was itself innovative, focusing on applicants’…

However, the ESF (national level) audited the project every six months, and the Ministry of Labour, Employment and the Social and Solidarity Economy carried out an internal evaluation at the end of the first phase, concluding that the intervention was effective and suitable for further funding. Numeric4All continuously measures participants’ progress, providing regular feedback to trainees and reporting results, first to the ESF and now to the Ministry of Labour, Employment and the Social and Solidarity Economy. innovations.name: Personal assistant: to be or not to be
innovations.problem: Article 19 of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities stresses the equal right of all people with disabilities to live in the community, with choices equal to others. It stipulates that State parties shall take effective and appropriate measures to facilitate full enjoyment by persons with disabilities of this right, and their full inclusion and participation in the community. Until 2017, the Flemish Government provided a budget for the specialised support and care of persons with disabilities directly to institutions and service providers, limiting self-determination and freedom of choice for persons with disabilities and their family members to choose the set-up of their…
innovations.desc: In 2017, the Flemish Government adopted significant policy changes on the provision of financial support to persons with disabilities. The budget is no longer transferred to institutions and service providers, but, rather, is given directly to people with disabilities themselves. This optimises their control over how their support is arranged and tailored to their needs. ‘Personal assistant: to be or not to be’ was designed to help families in making decisions, specifically to assess whether or not direct relatives such as parents, siblings or partners will themselves engage in the care of the person. It does so on the basis of a toolbox that helps family members to reflect critically on what it means to become and/or remain the personal assistant of a person with disabilities, including information and reflection prompts around the areas of ‘formal, financial and practical aspects’,…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities
innovations.evidence: ‘Personal assistant: to be or not to be’ was evaluated by the Flemish Managing Authority of ESF through an expert panel composed of policy-makers, practitioners and other stakeholders familiar with the needs of the family members of people with disabilities. The role of the panel was to share general advices on how to further improve the project design and its implementation, as well as dissemination of the toolbox to a wide audience. Following their recommendations, KU Leuven collaborated with international partners such as Euro Carers, the European Association Working for Carers, and COFACE…

innovations.problem:
A specific personal situation, such as a disability or an incapacity, might limit the right of every citizen to independent living [1] , as they might not be able to perform some types of activities themselves. This can lead to dependence on family member(s) and have a negative impact of quality of life.

innovations.desc:
In 2017, the Portuguese Government launched the Independent Life Support Model (MAVI). The project started in December 2018 and is expected to end in June 2023. It aims to fund pilot projects to support people with severe physical or mental disabilities to live their lives independently and to ensure the conditions in which they can exercise their right to make decisions about their lives.
MAVI creates the conditions for people with disabilities and incapacities to have an independent, self-determined life and provides personal assistants to people with disabilities to help them perform activities they cannot perform by themselves. People aged 16 or over, with a certified degree of disability of at least 60% (certified by a Multipurpose Disability Certificate or a Military Forces Disability Card [1] ) are eligible for this personal assistance programme. innovations.name: Skills Centre for Foreigners
innovations.problem:
The region of South Moravia in Czechia receives significant flows of migrants from a wide range of countries and with diverse backgrounds. It is difficult for migrants to obtain formal recognition of their knowledge, skills and qualifications. In addition, they face barriers to integration, including language difficulties and complex daily administrative procedures. These barriers often lead migrants to take jobs that do not match their skills.
At the same time, in South Moravia, employers are struggling to meet their labour force needs, particularly in the information technology (IT) sector. Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have limited staff and lack the necessary resources to…
innovations.desc:
The ‘Skills Centre for Foreigners’ organises free-of-charge Czech and English language courses, legal and social counselling, cultural activities and adaptation-integration courses for migrants in order to facilitate their integration into the Czech society. The Centre focuses on new education pathways for foreigners, as Czech curricula remain solely available in Czech.
The Skill Centre also helps employers to identify a workforce that can meet their needs and supports them with the administrative processes required to hire migrants.
The Skill Centre is developing digital tools to support migrants to address their challenges. In the framework of the Ukrainian crisis, the Skill centre developed a platform allowing Ukrainian migrants to create a CV in Ukrainian, provide their qualifications, and select the sectors in which they are interested in working. These CVs are then translated into…

innovations.name: Support services for ex-convicts
innovations.problem: Once prisoners are released, they face a variety of risks, including income and housing uncertainty, broken relationships, debt and stigmatisation. They often look for cash-in-hand jobs and do not register as unemployed, hindering their access to medical care and other services. The main goal of the project is to facilitate ex-prisoners to access the labour market and prevent re-offending.
innovations.desc:
The innovative aspect of the project is that for six months before leaving prison and for up to 12 months afterwards, ex-prisoners receive mentoring and housing services free of charge. The mentoring continues when they enter the labour market, supporting them in their decision-making.
The mentor and mentee agree on a ‘working alliance’, in order to reinforce trust and cooperation. They meet, on average, once per month during the six months in prison. Mentees are advised how to approach life outside prison, given links to other service providers and specialists based on their needs, and generally helped them to integrate into working life. Once they leave prison, their mentor will meet them, reinforcing their trust in the alliance and directing them towards the available support.
If ex-prisoners have nowhere to stay upon their release from prison, they can live in a housing community…

The project aims to have 75% of ex-prisoners supported to enter the labour market (i.e. registered as jobseekers with the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund) and 30% on the workers register (i.e. currently working) within one month of leaving the service.

innovations.name: Máš na to podnikat a pracovat! - You can make business and work!
innovations.problem: In Czechia, disadvantaged people who are willing to start their own businesses but who live in rural areas face substantial barriers. Groups include long-term unemployed jobseekers, economically inactive people, persons with disabilities, low-skilled people and employees who have been dismissed. Barriers include isolation in rural communities, a lack of business/entrepreneurial knowledge, and very low confidence and ambition as a result of the lack of role models. This ESF project aims to develop entrepreneurial capacity among these groups in order to reduce the amount of undeclared work, help people to become less dependent on social benefits, and support micro-businesses in rural areas of…
innovations.desc:
Máš na to podnikat a pracovat! (You can make business and work!) supports people to find a suitable job or to start their own business. Its main innovation is its ability to provide a guaranteed income to participants while they develop and test their business ideas, thus eliminating the pressure of having to self-finance the process. This is done through the Business and Employment Cooperative (BEC), which follows a three-step process: business incubation, testing and self-employment.
The business incubation phase typically lasts between two and three months. During that time, participants are eligible to receive unemployment benefits from the labour office (the exact amount depends on their previous working situation) as they are participating in special business training session. The project finances counselling, tuition and mentoring on creating a solid business plan. The project…
innovations.target: Individuals with disabilities, Long-term or repeatedly unemployed persons, NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training)
innovations.evidence:
BEC is responsible for evaluating project progress. The main goals are for 40% of phase 1 participants follow the programme through to phase 3, and for no more than 10-20% of participants to return to unemployment.
During the project, BEC uses a simple diagnostic tool for participants to evaluate the riskiness of starting their business. That tool also evaluates their attainment of entrepreneurial knowledge and flags when additional extra support is needed to mitigate such risks. This tool can be used at the beginning and end of the process.

innovations.problem:

At the same time, there is a lack of inter-generational solidarity, with young people seeming quite disconnected from their communities.

‘Social entrepreneurship connects us’ aims to help people in social and economic need using social entrepreneurship. The project organiser, Auxilium, works to promote and develop social entrepreneurship in Osijek and beyond. It seeks to encourage local young people to get involved in their community and develop socially-responsible behaviour, while supporting their acquisition of skills in demand in the labour market.
Auxilium piloted the project in the city of Osijek, among young students from the vocational Geodetic and Civil Engineering School. As part of their curriculum, students partner with Auxilium to undertake practical courses to help people in need with various tasks, such as household repairs or cleaning. The pilot provides an opportunity for students to gain experience in the labour market, to explore, learn, discover and test social entrepreneurship.

There is a lack of community-based outreach and family support services to help vulnerable families and an absence of social housing. Children are often placed in care because their families face extreme poverty and are unable to cope.
Young people who grew up in institutional settings might experience difficulties in transitioning to independent living.
